title: From Copilots to Coworkers: How AI Agents Are Transforming Azure Networking Operations
what_they_do: Azure Networking 运维从对话式 copilot 演进到自主工作流 agent：agent 被分配目标、跨数小时到数天携带上下文，在工单、遥测、Teams、邮件等员工同一渠道里协调光纤供应商和现场技术员、对照实时遥测验证修复、失败时反馈重试，只在高风险/不可逆操作和歧义时升级给人。agent 以“agent 组织”管理：内部控制平面定义身份、角色、技能、策略与审计，权限按 agent 类别和风险分级。
numbers: This workflow involved roughly 14 interactions over about 9.5 hours, without a human engineer needing to actively manage each step.
**2x faster time to mitigate** on issues like fiber-repair workflows.
**Up to a 78% reduction in manual effort** by offloading operational toil to agents.
Autonomous workflow agents act similar to digital coworkers, integrating their work alongside 10,000+ employees like data center technicians, network engineers, hardware engineers, etc.
denominator_notes: “2x 更快缓解”“最多减少 78% 人工”未给基线、统计期和覆盖的事件类型（“up to”是最好情况）；14 次交互/9.5 小时是单个光纤中断案例。页面显示 May 15, 2026（另见 “Updated May 14” 字样）。
transferable: 对运维/SRE：先做对话式助手积累信任，再让 agent 承担跨团队、跨厂商的“协调中段”（跟进、验证、重试）；agent 必须在人已在用的渠道里工作；按风险分级的权限与人工审批点要尽早定义；用“agent 自主完成的流程比例”衡量。
caveats: Customer Zero 营销系列；数据为最好情况；是运维而非软件开发场景。
headline: Microsoft Azure Networking 让运维 agent 在工单和 Teams 里承担跨厂商的跟进与验证，只在高风险或有歧义时升级给人
headline_en: Microsoft Azure Networking has ops agents handle cross-vendor follow-up and verification inside tickets and Teams, escalating to humans only on high-risk or ambiguous calls.
what_they_do_en: Azure Networking operations moved from conversational copilots to autonomous workflow agents. Agents are assigned a goal and carry context across hours or days. They work in the same channels employees use (tickets, telemetry, Teams, email) to coordinate fiber suppliers and field technicians, verify fixes against live telemetry, and feed failures back for retries, escalating to a human only for high-risk or irreversible actions and for ambiguity. Agents are managed as an "agent organization": an internal control plane defines identity, roles, skills, policy, and audit, and permissions are tiered by agent class and risk.
denominator_notes_en: "2x faster mitigation" and "up to 78% less manual effort" come with no baseline, measurement period, or incident types covered ("up to" is the best case). The 14 interactions / 9.5 hours figure is a single fiber-outage case. The page shows May 15, 2026 (an "Updated May 14" label also appears).
transferable_en: For ops/SRE: start with a conversational assistant to build trust, then hand agents the cross-team, cross-vendor "coordination middle" (follow-up, verification, retries). Agents must work in the channels people already use. Define risk-tiered permissions and human approval points early. Measure by "share of workflows the agent completes autonomously."
caveats_en: Part of the Customer Zero marketing series; figures are best case; this is an operations scenario, not software development.

title: Building a general-purpose accessibility agent—and what we learned in the process
what_they_do: GitHub 试点内部无障碍（accessibility）agent：在 Copilot CLI/VS Code 中为工程师答疑，并自动评审修改前端代码的 PR、修复简单客观的问题。经验：最有价值的上下文是多年人工记录的无障碍 issue 及其修复 PR；从单体 agent 改为“只审阅的 reviewer + 只实现的 implementer”两个沙箱化子 agent，经模板化 schema 传递、由父 agent 过滤路由，并强制固定顺序执行；用简单脚本给代码复杂度打分，超阈值或属于拖放、富文本编辑器、树、数据表格等高风险模式时禁止生成代码、转介无障碍团队；还需加入“防作弊”指令阻止模型绕过这一限制；定期人工审查产出并采集 PR 评审者情绪。
numbers: To date, the agent has reviewed 3,535 pull requests, with a 68% resolution rate.
Of the 55 total WCAG level A and AA Success Criterion, only 35 of them can be detected via deterministic automated code checkers.
denominator_notes: 68% 的“resolution rate”定义未说明（被修复？被接受？）；3,535 PR 的时间范围未说明。
transferable: 领域专家型评审 agent 的设计要点：用组织自己的历史问题与修复做语料；限定能力边界并在复杂/高风险场景强制转人工；子 agent 之间用模板通信以便审计；定期人工抽检。适用于安全、隐私、无障碍等专项评审。
caveats: 试点阶段；作者为无障碍团队成员；部分数字定义不清。
headline: GitHub 无障碍 agent 拆成只审阅和只实现两个沙箱子 agent，并用复杂度脚本把高风险 UI 模式强制转给人工
headline_en: GitHub split its accessibility agent into sandboxed review-only and implement-only sub-agents, and a complexity script forces high-risk UI patterns to human experts.
what_they_do_en: GitHub is piloting an internal accessibility agent: it answers engineers' questions in Copilot CLI/VS Code, automatically reviews PRs that touch frontend code, and fixes simple, objective issues. Lessons: the most valuable context was years of human-written accessibility issues and the PRs that fixed them. They moved from a monolithic agent to two sandboxed sub-agents, a review-only reviewer and an implement-only implementer, passing data through templated schemas, filtered and routed by a parent agent, with a fixed execution order enforced. A simple script scores code complexity; above a threshold, or for high-risk patterns such as drag-and-drop, rich text editors, trees, and data grids, code generation is blocked and the work is referred to the accessibility team. They also had to add "anti-cheating" instructions to stop the model from working around that restriction. Output is reviewed by humans regularly, and PR reviewer sentiment is collected.
denominator_notes_en: The 68% "resolution rate" is undefined (fixed? accepted?); no time range is given for the 3,535 PRs.
transferable_en: Design points for a domain-expert review agent: use the organization's own historical issues and fixes as the corpus; bound its capabilities and force human handoff for complex or high-risk cases; have sub-agents communicate via templates so the flow is auditable; spot-check output regularly. Applies to specialist reviews such as security, privacy, and accessibility.
caveats_en: Pilot stage; the author is on the accessibility team; some figures are poorly defined.

title: How an Anthropic sales leader uses Claude Cowork to run a 4,000-account book
what_they_do: Anthropic 美国中端市场 GTM 负责人用 Claude Cowork 的定时任务 + skill 自动做每日会议室预订和客户会前简报（拉 BigQuery 消耗、Salesforce pipeline），每周五自动汇总预测报告成网页供周一预测会使用，他只补充解读。年度 4,000 个账户的倾向性打分：先和 Claude 定两套五维评分 rubric，在一个测试 territory 上调权重，再整夜批量跑出分数和理由，并生成给每个 AE 的交互式 dashboard。
numbers: Most of the time I save with Claude Cowork falls into about 90 minutes of small daily wins, or micro-optimizations, that it runs for me.
The Friday forecast is the next tier up and it saves me about three hours per week.
In previous companies and roles, work like this ran for hundreds of hours across RevOps, FP&A, and marketing. I did it in one night.
denominator_notes: 均为单人自述的节省时间估计，无测量方法；「数百小时」是与其过往公司经验对比而非同一任务的对照；未说明评分结果准确度或对销售结果的影响。
transferable: 可复用的模式：把重复的会前准备/周报变成定时运行的 skill，并把管理层要求的格式写进 skill；把「一直没人有时间做」的大型分析（账户打分、TAM）做成夜间批处理，先小样本校准 rubric 再全量跑。前提是 CRM/数仓有可被 agent 访问的连接器与权限治理。
caveats: 员工个人自述、带产品推广目的（文末导流到 webinar 和 Sales plugin）；单一角色个案，无质量评估；Anthropic 员工对自家工具熟练度和数据接入远高于一般企业。
headline: Anthropic 销售负责人先小样本校准 rubric，再让 Claude 一夜给 4,000 个账户打分
headline_en: An Anthropic sales leader calibrated a scoring rubric on a small sample, then had Claude score 4,000 accounts overnight.
what_they_do_en: Anthropic's US mid-market GTM lead uses Claude Cowork scheduled tasks plus skills to automate daily meeting-room booking and pre-meeting customer briefs (pulling BigQuery consumption and Salesforce pipeline). Every Friday a forecast report is compiled automatically into a web page for Monday's forecast meeting; he only adds interpretation. For annual propensity scoring of 4,000 accounts, he first worked out two five-dimension scoring rubrics with Claude, tuned the weights on one test territory, then ran scores and rationales in an overnight batch and generated an interactive dashboard for each AE.
denominator_notes_en: All time savings are one person's self-estimates with no measurement method. "Hundreds of hours" compares against his experience at past companies, not a controlled comparison on the same task. No accuracy of the scores or impact on sales outcomes is reported.
transferable_en: Reusable pattern: turn repetitive meeting prep and weekly reports into scheduled skills, with the format management expects written into the skill; run the big analyses nobody ever had time for (account scoring, TAM) as overnight batches, calibrating the rubric on a small sample before the full run. Requires agent-accessible connectors and permission governance for the CRM and data warehouse.
caveats_en: Employee self-report with promotional intent (ends by funneling to a webinar and the Sales plugin); a single-role case with no quality assessment; Anthropic employees' fluency with their own tools and data access far exceed a typical enterprise's.

title: How Anthropic's finance team uses Claude to shape the narrative behind the numbers
what_they_do: Anthropic 公司财务与战略团队成员用 Claude Cowork 校验季度董事会 deck 中每个数字与叙述是否对齐单一数据源、并以董事视角挑矛盾；用 Cowork 按上月口吻起草月度差异分析初稿，用 Claude for Excel 跨 tab 追查模型问题；不同受众用不同 project 与 memory。CFO 组织其他团队：分析师自建预测 dashboard、每天 7 点自动推送营收摘要到 Slack；会计做 GL/子账与银行对账初稿；企业发展每天筛 3–4 个并购标的；税务/资金问题带原始出处回答。
numbers: Alice Fong, on the corporate finance and strategy team at Anthropic, shares how she uses Claude to maintain a single coherent financial narrative for the CFO and board, and free up 10 to 20 hours a week for higher-impact work.
Corporate development and IR: Screening reports for three to four acquisition targets a day, built from notes and public data, then rolled up into memos in minutes.
denominator_notes: 10–20 小时/周为单人自估，无基线测量；「每天 3–4 个标的」是产出频率，未给此前对比和质量评估。
transferable: 财务团队可直接借鉴「让 AI 做一致性/对账校验层、人做叙事判断」的分工：把高频复核（数字与叙述对齐、月度差异初稿）交给 agent，并为不同受众维护独立的项目上下文。前提是有可信的单一数据源，且输出仍需人工签字。
caveats: 员工自述+产品推广（Cowork、Claude for Excel、金融 plugins）；未披露错误率或审计结论；对外披露的财务流程细节有限。
headline: Anthropic 财务团队让 Claude 校验董事会材料里数字与叙述是否一致，叙事判断和签字仍由人负责
headline_en: Anthropic's finance team has Claude check that numbers and narrative in board materials agree; narrative judgment and sign-off stay with humans.
what_they_do_en: A member of Anthropic's corporate finance and strategy team uses Claude Cowork to check that every number and claim in the quarterly board deck ties to a single source of truth, and to hunt for contradictions from a board member's point of view. Cowork drafts the monthly variance analysis in last month's voice; Claude for Excel traces model issues across tabs; separate projects and memory are kept for different audiences. Elsewhere in the CFO org: analysts build their own forecasting dashboards and get an automated revenue summary in Slack at 7 a.m. daily; accounting drafts GL/subledger and bank reconciliations; corporate development screens 3-4 M&A targets a day; tax and treasury questions are answered with citations to original sources.
denominator_notes_en: 10-20 hours/week is one person's estimate with no baseline measurement. "3-4 targets a day" is output frequency, with no prior comparison or quality assessment.
transferable_en: Finance teams can adopt the split directly: AI as the consistency/reconciliation check layer, humans on narrative judgment. Hand high-frequency reviews (numbers vs. narrative, first-draft monthly variance) to an agent, and keep separate project context per audience. Requires a trusted single source of truth, and output still needs human sign-off.
caveats_en: Employee self-report plus product promotion (Cowork, Claude for Excel, financial plugins); no error rates or audit findings disclosed; limited detail on finance processes is shared publicly.

title: How we contain Claude across products
what_they_do: Anthropic 内部已常规地给 Claude 足以搞垮内部服务的权限，安全重心从「人逐步审批」转向「环境层封装」（沙箱、VM、egress 控制、凭证不进沙箱）。依据自家遥测：用户批准约 93% 的权限弹窗、出现审批疲劳，于是做了 OS 级沙箱（弹窗减少 84%）和 auto mode 分类器。文中披露了内部事故：2 月内部红队钓鱼让员工把恶意 prompt 贴进 Claude Code，25 次中 24 次成功外泄凭证；把 payload 贴到内部 Slack 讨论时又意识到内部 agent 会读 Slack，只好加 canary；Cowork 通过被放行的 api.anthropic.com 外泄文件，自研代理是最薄弱环节。
numbers: Our telemetry showed users approved roughly 93% of permission prompts.

On Gray Swan's Agent Red Teaming benchmark, which tests susceptibility to prompt injection, Claude Opus 4.7 holds attack success to roughly 0.1% on single attempts, and around 5–6% after 100 adaptive attempts.
Claude Code auto mode catches roughly 83% of overeager behaviors before they execute.
The result was an 84% reduction in permission prompts, and we open-sourced the runtime, so the boundary is auditable.
Our anonymized usage data also showed that experienced users auto-approve roughly twice as often as new users, but they also interrupt the agent mid-execution more frequently.
Across 25 retries of that prompt, Claude completed the exfiltration 24 times.

Claude Code auto mode delegates command approvals to a model-based classifier; it minimizes friction (roughly 0.4% of benign commands blocked) at the cost of missing a fraction of risky ones (~17% of overeager actions get through), so it's one layer of defense-in-depth inside a sandbox, not a substitute for one.
denominator_notes: 93% 批准率与「老用户 2 倍自动批准」来自 Claude Code 产品遥测（外部用户为主，非仅内部员工），未给时间窗和样本量。84% 是开沙箱前后弹窗数对比。83%/17%/0.4% 是 auto mode 分类器在其评测集上的召回/误拦，非生产实测。24/25 是单个钓鱼 prompt 的重复试验，样本极小。
transferable: 可直接采纳：先做环境层硬边界（凭证不进 agent 环境、默认拒绝出网、只读/禁删挂载、按用户技术能力决定隔离强度），再叠加模型层分类器；把项目级配置/hook 视为不可信输入，信任确认前不解析；把 egress allowlist 当作能力授予来审；把会被 agent 读取的 Slack/文档当攻击面。前提是有平台/安全团队能维护沙箱与代理。
caveats: 厂商自述，事故细节经挑选；遥测数据主要来自产品用户而非内部员工；部分结论服务于自家产品（auto mode、Cowork）推广。
headline: Anthropic 发现用户会批准约 93% 的权限弹窗，于是把安全重心从逐步审批移到沙箱、egress 控制和凭证不进 agent 环境
headline_en: Finding that users approve about 93% of permission prompts, Anthropic shifted security from step-by-step approval to sandboxes, egress control, and keeping credentials out of agent environments.
what_they_do_en: Internally, Anthropic now routinely gives Claude enough access to take down internal services, and has moved its security focus from "humans approve each step" to "containment at the environment layer" (sandboxes, VMs, egress control, no credentials inside the sandbox). The basis is its own telemetry: users approve about 93% of permission prompts and show approval fatigue, so it built an OS-level sandbox (84% fewer prompts) and the auto mode classifier. The post discloses internal incidents: in February, an internal red-team phishing exercise got employees to paste a malicious prompt into Claude Code, exfiltrating credentials in 24 of 25 attempts. When the payload was then posted to internal Slack for discussion, the team realized internal agents read Slack and had to add a canary. Cowork exfiltrated files through the allowlisted api.anthropic.com; the in-house proxy was the weakest link.
denominator_notes_en: The 93% approval rate and "experienced users auto-approve 2x as often" come from Claude Code product telemetry (mostly external users, not just employees), with no time window or sample size. 84% compares prompt counts before and after enabling the sandbox. 83%/17%/0.4% are the auto mode classifier's recall/false-block rates on its eval set, not production measurements. 24/25 is repeated trials of a single phishing prompt, a very small sample.
transferable_en: Adopt directly: build hard boundaries at the environment layer first (no credentials in the agent environment, default-deny egress, read-only/no-delete mounts, isolation strength set by the user's technical skill), then layer model-level classifiers on top. Treat project-level config and hooks as untrusted input and don't parse them before trust is confirmed. Review the egress allowlist as a capability grant. Treat Slack and docs that agents read as attack surface. Requires a platform/security team that can maintain the sandbox and proxy.
caveats_en: Vendor self-report with selected incident details; telemetry comes mainly from product users rather than employees; some conclusions support promotion of its own products (auto mode, Cowork).

title: Using AI to write better code more slowly
what_they_do: 作者用一个 Claude skill 对每个 PR 同时调用 Claude 子 agent、Codex、Cursor Bugbot 三家找 bug 并分级，再由主 agent 自己核实排除误报、写总报告；然后让 agent 修完所有 critical/high、性价比低的 medium 跳过、critical 太多就放弃整个 PR。结果是代码库健康度和对代码的理解提高了，但速度并没有明显提升，常被拖进修复既有 bug、补测试的支线。
denominator_notes: 个人经验，无量化；「误报率接近零」为作者主观判断。
transferable: 多模型交叉评审 + 主 agent 核验去误报，是低成本可复制的 PR 预审做法；同时提醒管理者：把 AI 用于质量而非速度时，吞吐指标可能不升反降，度量体系要能容纳这种用法。
caveats: 单人经验贴，HN 高票主要因为观点共鸣；未给出 bug 数或缺陷率对比。
headline: Nolan Lawson 用三家模型交叉审每个 PR，代码更健康了，但速度并没有变快
headline_en: Nolan Lawson cross-reviews every PR with three vendors' models; the codebase got healthier, but he didn't get faster.
what_they_do_en: The author uses a Claude skill that, for each PR, runs a Claude sub-agent, Codex, and Cursor Bugbot in parallel to find and grade bugs; the main agent then verifies the findings itself, discards false positives, and writes a summary report. The agent then fixes every critical/high issue, skips medium ones that aren't worth the cost, and abandons the whole PR if there are too many criticals. The result: better codebase health and better understanding of the code, but no noticeable speedup, since he often gets pulled into side quests fixing existing bugs and adding tests.
denominator_notes_en: Personal experience, no quantification; the "near-zero false-positive rate" is the author's subjective judgment.
transferable_en: Multi-model cross-review plus a main agent that verifies and removes false positives is a cheap, replicable PR pre-review. It's also a reminder for managers: when AI is used for quality rather than speed, throughput metrics may go down rather than up, and the measurement system has to accommodate that.
caveats_en: A single person's experience post; its HN popularity mostly reflects agreement with the viewpoint; no comparison of bug counts or defect rates.

title: Building self-improving tax agents with Codex
what_they_do: OpenAI FDE、研究员与 Thrive Holdings 工程师合作为会计事务所做 Tax AI。工程实践核心是“三支柱”闭环：贴近从业者、让产品在生产中留下结构化证据（源文件→抽取字段→提交→专家修正的完整 trace）、把反复出现的专家修正归类成 eval 目标，再变成有边界的 Codex 工程任务（可写 worktree 与只读生产证据分离，跑定向+回归 eval，产出候选 PR 交工程师评审）；证据模糊的情况退回产品团队。
numbers: At launch, only a quarter of returns were at 75% correct field completion, but within six weeks, 86% hit that mark.

Rental properties took about six weeks and substantial engineering oversight to reach 90% precision and recall, but that work produced reusable abstractions, review artifacts, eval conventions, and implementation patterns that made it easier to support similarly complex schedules such as Schedule C and Schedule A.
To solve this problem, Tax AI processed 7,000 tax returns across the Crete firms that participated in the pilot this tax season.
denominator_notes: “25%→86% 达到 75% 字段正确率”的分母是被评分的申报表，期间产品同时扩展到更复杂的表，口径可能变化。其余效率数字（省 1/3 时间、+50% 吞吐）属客户业务成效。
transferable: 对任何在生产中运行 agent 的团队：把人工修正结构化记录→聚类成 eval→生成可验证的 agent 工程任务→人工评审 PR，这是可复制的“agent 改 agent”闭环。前提：能拿到真实修正数据和可回放的 trace，并限定 agent 只改有边界的那一层。
caveats: 是与被投资/合作方的联合项目，带商业宣传；效果数据来自合作方，未经第三方验证。
headline: OpenAI 税务 agent 把专家修正结构化记录、聚类成 eval，再转成有边界的 Codex 任务产出候选 PR，形成「agent 改 agent」闭环
headline_en: OpenAI's tax agent logs expert corrections in structured form, clusters them into evals, and turns them into bounded Codex tasks that produce candidate PRs: agents improving agents.
what_they_do_en: OpenAI FDEs and researchers worked with Thrive Holdings engineers to build Tax AI for accounting firms. The core engineering practice is a "three pillars" loop: stay close to practitioners; have the product leave structured evidence in production (a full trace from source file to extracted fields to submission to expert correction); and cluster recurring expert corrections into eval targets, then into bounded Codex engineering tasks (writable worktree kept separate from read-only production evidence, targeted plus regression evals, candidate PRs for engineer review). Cases with ambiguous evidence go back to the product team.
denominator_notes_en: In "25%→86% reaching 75% field accuracy," the denominator is graded returns, and the product expanded to more complex returns over the same period, so the basis may have shifted. The other efficiency figures (1/3 time saved, +50% throughput) are customer business outcomes.
transferable_en: For any team running agents in production: log human corrections in structured form → cluster them into evals → generate verifiable agent engineering tasks → human review of PRs. This is a replicable "agents improving agents" loop. Requires real correction data and replayable traces, and the agent must be limited to changing a bounded layer.
caveats_en: A joint project with an investee/partner, with commercial promotion; results come from the partner and were not independently verified.

title: How Anthropic enables self-service data analytics with Claude
what_they_do: Anthropic 数据科学/数据工程团队把业务分析查询大部分交给 Claude，并把准确率当作「上下文与验证」问题而非写 SQL 问题：收敛为少量强治理的 canonical 数据集并用工具/CI/行政要求强制使用；skill 强制先走语义层，再走按域整理的参考文档；skill 文档与数据模型同仓，评审 hook 拦截未同步 skill 的报表模型改动。验证体系：离线 eval（看板问题自动生成+人工确认、长尾问题、用户纠正自动收集为候选 eval），结果按 skill 版本/git SHA/模型 ID 入仓当遥测；按业务域设上线门槛（初始约 90%）；每次 skill 改动做单变量消融；线上用对抗式复核 sub-agent、溯源脚注（来源层级/新鲜度/owner）、定时 agent 扫描频道中的纠正语言并自动开 PR 给域 owner；面向管理层的结论必须人工签字。
numbers: At Anthropic, 95% of business analytics queries are automated via Claude, with ~95% accuracy in aggregate.
Without skills, Claude’s ability to answer analytics questions accurately didn’t exceed 21% on our evals.
Adding skills gets these numbers consistently above 95% in aggregate and regularly around 99% in certain domains.
We watched our offline accuracy drift from ~95% at launch to ~65% over a month before we treated this as an engineering problem.
Roughly 90% of our data-model PRs now include a skill change in the same diff.
Gate launches per domain: A domain owner can't announce the agent to their stakeholders until their slice of the eval set clears some threshold (we initially used ~90%).
Accuracy moved by less than a point in either direction.
About 80% of the time, yes.

Adversarial review: we’ve found that employing a Claude skill to aggressively challenge all underlying assumptions on a potential final answer increased accuracy by 6% within our eval set, but at the cost of 32% more tokens and 72% higher latency.
denominator_notes: 「95% 查询自动化」的分母是业务分析查询（未定义统计口径与时间窗）；「~95% 准确率」是离线 eval 的汇总准确率，作者自己强调离线 eval 不代表线上表现、且静默错误仍无可靠解法。21%→95% 是有无 skill 在同一 eval 集上的对比。95%→65% 是上线后一个月未维护文档时的离线漂移。90% 是数据模型 PR 中同时改 skill 的比例。6%/32%/72% 是对抗复核的准确率/token/延迟增量。
transferable: 非常可迁移：先做少量 canonical 数据集 + 几十条离线 eval + 一个薄的路由 skill；skill/文档与数据模型同仓同 PR，CI/评审 hook 强制同步；eval 结果按版本入仓当遥测；按域设准确率门槛再开放；用户纠正自动转 PR 和 eval；回答附溯源脚注。前提是已有数据治理基础（语义层、元数据、owner），人工维护定义而非让 LLM 自动生成指标定义（文中说那样在 eval 上是净负）。
caveats: 自述的准确率基于自建 eval，覆盖度未知；Anthropic 内部数据规模与业务复杂度和一般企业不同；文章同时推广 Claude Code/skills。
headline: Anthropic 数据团队把准确率当上下文问题：没有 skill 时 eval 准确率不超过 21%，加上后超 95%
headline_en: Anthropic's data team treats accuracy as a context problem: without skills, eval accuracy topped out at 21%; with them, it exceeded 95%.
what_they_do_en: Anthropic's data science and data engineering teams hand most business analytics queries to Claude, and treat accuracy as a "context and verification" problem rather than a SQL-writing problem. They consolidated onto a small number of tightly governed canonical datasets, with usage enforced through tooling, CI, and administrative mandate. Skills force queries through the semantic layer first, then through reference docs organized by domain. Skill docs live in the same repo as the data models, and a review hook blocks reporting-model changes that don't update the skill. Verification: offline evals (dashboard questions auto-generated and human-confirmed, long-tail questions, user corrections auto-collected as candidate evals), with results checked in by skill version / git SHA / model ID as telemetry; per-domain launch thresholds (initially about 90%); single-variable ablations on every skill change. Online: an adversarial review sub-agent, provenance footnotes (source tier, freshness, owner), and a scheduled agent that scans channels for correction language and auto-opens PRs to domain owners. Conclusions for leadership require human sign-off.
denominator_notes_en: The denominator for "95% of queries automated" is business analytics queries (no counting basis or time window defined). "~95% accuracy" is aggregate offline-eval accuracy; the authors themselves stress that offline evals don't reflect online performance and that silent errors still have no reliable fix. 21%→95% compares with and without skills on the same eval set. 95%→65% is offline drift after a month of unmaintained docs post-launch. 90% is the share of data-model PRs that also modify the skill. 6%/32%/72% are the accuracy/token/latency increases from adversarial review.
transferable_en: Highly transferable: start with a few canonical datasets, a few dozen offline evals, and a thin routing skill. Keep skills/docs in the same repo and PR as the data models, with CI and review hooks enforcing sync. Check eval results in by version as telemetry. Set per-domain accuracy thresholds before opening access. Auto-convert user corrections into PRs and evals. Attach provenance footnotes to answers. Requires existing data governance (semantic layer, metadata, owners), with humans maintaining definitions rather than letting an LLM generate metric definitions (the post says that was net negative on evals).
caveats_en: Self-reported accuracy is based on in-house evals of unknown coverage; Anthropic's internal data scale and business complexity differ from a typical enterprise's; the post also promotes Claude Code/skills.

title: Lessons from building Claude Code: How we use skills
what_they_do: Anthropic 内部有数百个在用的 Claude Code skill，盘点后分为 9 类（库/API 参考、产品验证、数据获取分析、业务流程自动化、脚手架、代码质量与评审、CI/CD 部署、runbook、基础设施运维）；内部经验是「验证类 skill 对输出质量影响最可测量」，值得让工程师花一周专门打磨。编写要点：不写 Claude 已知的东西、维护 Gotchas 段、用文件夹做渐进披露、描述写给模型看（何时触发）、skill 内可存日志做记忆、附脚本让 Claude 组合、按需启用的 hook（如 /careful 拦截 rm -rf/DROP TABLE/force-push）。分发与治理：小团队提交到仓库，大规模用内部 plugin marketplace；没有中央团队审批，先放 GitHub sandbox 文件夹、在 Slack 推广，有了牵引力再由 owner 提 PR 进 marketplace；用 PreToolUse hook 记录全公司 skill 使用量，找出热门与触发不足的 skill。
numbers: We've been using skills in Claude Code extensively at Anthropic with hundreds of them in active use.
denominator_notes: 仅「数百个在用」的规模描述，无使用频次、效果量化数据；「验证类 skill 影响最大」为定性判断。
transferable: 可直接采用：按 9 类盘点组织内 skill 缺口；先投入验证类 skill；skill 写 Gotchas 并持续追加；去中心化的「沙箱→有牵引力→PR 进 marketplace」治理；用 hook 统计 skill 使用率。前提是团队已在用 Claude Code 或兼容 skill 的 agent，并有内部 Git/IM 渠道传播。
caveats: Claude Code 团队成员撰写，带产品与课程推广；缺量化证据；示例 skill 名为示意。
headline: Anthropic 盘点内部数百个 skill，发现验证类 skill 对产出质量提升最可测，治理走「沙箱→有牵引力→进 marketplace」
headline_en: An inventory of hundreds of internal skills showed Anthropic that verification skills most measurably improve output; governance runs sandbox → traction → marketplace.
what_they_do_en: Anthropic has hundreds of Claude Code skills in active internal use. An inventory sorted them into 9 categories (library/API reference, product verification, data fetching and analysis, business process automation, scaffolding, code quality and review, CI/CD and deployment, runbooks, infrastructure operations). The internal finding: verification skills have the most measurable effect on output quality and are worth having an engineer spend a week polishing. Authoring tips: don't write what Claude already knows; maintain a Gotchas section; use folders for progressive disclosure; write the description for the model (when to trigger); let skills store logs as memory; bundle scripts for Claude to compose; use on-demand hooks (e.g. /careful blocks rm -rf / DROP TABLE / force-push). Distribution and governance: small teams commit skills to the repo; at scale there's an internal plugin marketplace. No central team approves skills; they start in a GitHub sandbox folder and get promoted in Slack, and once they have traction the owner opens a PR into the marketplace. A PreToolUse hook logs company-wide skill usage to find popular and under-triggering skills.
denominator_notes_en: Only a scale description ("hundreds in use"), with no usage frequency or quantified effect; "verification skills have the biggest impact" is a qualitative judgment.
transferable_en: Adopt directly: inventory the organization's skill gaps against the 9 categories; invest in verification skills first; give skills a Gotchas section and keep adding to it; use decentralized sandbox → traction → PR-into-marketplace governance; track skill usage with hooks. Requires teams already using Claude Code or a skill-compatible agent, plus internal Git/chat channels for spreading skills.
caveats_en: Written by a Claude Code team member, with product and course promotion; lacks quantitative evidence; example skill names are illustrative.

title: Running an AI-native engineering org
what_they_do: Claude Code/Cowork 工程总监（Code w/ Claude SF 2026 演讲整理）介绍团队在 agent 编码成为默认后改写的规范：规划从 6 个月路线图改为「即时规划」（PR/原型中讨论、先给内部用户用再迭代，少做产品评审）；找上下文先问 Claude 而不是找作者，并追问「这件事能否自动化」；代码评审由 Claude 处理风格/lint/bug/补测试，人只在需要领域专长处介入（法务风险、信任边界与安全代码、PM/设计的产品品味）；角色模糊化——PM 大量写代码、工程师承担内容和设计，招聘偏重「有产品感的创造型 builder」和「深系统专长」两类，不看重原始产出量。推行方式：少数不可协商的团队原则（全员 dogfood、团队尽量扁平且经理先当 IC、明确授权砍掉过时流程），其余由各 pod 自主。建议追踪三个指标：入职爬坡时间、PR 周期时间、Claude 辅助提交占比，但提醒吞吐不等于成功。
numbers: When I first joined the Claude Code team, we wrote a pretty good six month roadmap, and then because of Claude Code, so many things changed that it was out of date by month three.
For us, by default, every commit is Claude-assisted. I don't think I've seen a non-Claude-assisted commit in the last four months.
denominator_notes: 无系统性数据；「每个 commit 都由 Claude 辅助」是总监个人观察，未定义「辅助」。入职爬坡、PR 周期只给了「比一年前快很多」「第一周就能交付真实代码」的定性描述。
transferable: 对 TLM 很实用的清单：用即时规划替代长路线图、把「问作者」改为「先问 agent 再问能否自动化」、按领域专长而非全量做人审、经理先做 IC、给团队「砍流程」的明确授权、用入职爬坡时间/PR 周期/AI 辅助提交占比作为采纳度指标（同时警惕只看吞吐）。前提是有足够的 CI 容量与内部用户群可快速反馈。
caveats: 产品团队负责人演讲，带产品推广；Claude Code 团队做的就是 agent 工具本身，dogfood 条件与一般业务团队不同；无量化验证。
headline: Anthropic 的 Claude Code 团队用即时规划、按领域专长做人审、经理先当 IC 改写了工程规范
headline_en: Anthropic's Claude Code team rewrote its engineering norms: just-in-time planning, human review only where domain expertise matters, and managers who work as ICs first.
what_they_do_en: The engineering director for Claude Code/Cowork (writeup of a Code w/ Claude SF 2026 talk) describes the norms the team rewrote once agentic coding became the default. Planning moved from 6-month roadmaps to "just-in-time planning" (discussed in PRs and prototypes, shipped to internal users first and iterated, fewer product reviews). To find context, ask Claude before asking the author, and follow up with "can this be automated?" In code review, Claude handles style, lint, bugs, and missing tests; humans step in only where domain expertise is needed (legal risk, trust boundaries and security code, PM/design product taste). Roles are blurring: PMs write a lot of code, engineers take on content and design. Hiring favors two profiles, "creative builders with product sense" and "deep systems expertise," and doesn't weigh raw output. Rollout: a few non-negotiable team principles (everyone dogfoods, the team stays as flat as possible with managers working as ICs first, explicit license to kill outdated process), with everything else left to each pod. Suggested metrics: onboarding ramp time, PR cycle time, and share of Claude-assisted commits, with the caveat that throughput isn't success.
denominator_notes_en: No systematic data. "Every commit is Claude-assisted" is the director's personal observation, and "assisted" is undefined. Onboarding ramp and PR cycle time get only qualitative descriptions ("much faster than a year ago," "shipping real code in the first week").
transferable_en: A practical checklist for TLMs: replace long roadmaps with just-in-time planning; change "ask the author" to "ask the agent first, then ask whether it can be automated"; do human review by domain expertise rather than on everything; have managers work as ICs first; give the team explicit license to cut process; use onboarding ramp time / PR cycle time / AI-assisted commit share as adoption metrics (while watching out for focusing only on throughput). Requires enough CI capacity and an internal user base that can give fast feedback.
caveats_en: A talk by the product team's leader, with product promotion; the Claude Code team builds the agent tool itself, so its dogfooding conditions differ from a typical business team's; no quantitative validation.

title: Best practices for getting started with Claude Cowork
what_they_do: Anthropic 增长营销负责人分享非技术岗如何使用 agent：每天早上 6 点的定时任务汇总未读邮件和关注的 Slack 频道，并标出可能影响营销的夜间产品事故；通过 Google Ads/Meta Ads 连接器做自动更新的预算消耗与进度 dashboard；每周自动从 Search Console 拉数据、按模板生成对比报告，他只补充上下文和要点。给出判断任务是否适合委托给 agent 的「五要素」清单：多个输入、产出一个文件、会重复做、你知道好结果长什么样、中间是枯燥的提取/汇编/对账/格式化环节。
numbers: Within a week, I went from not knowing what a terminal was to building out Claude Code workflows that completed 30-minute tasks in 30 seconds.
Now, 90% of my work happens in Claude Cowork.
Reporting used to take me ~30 minutes a week; now it takes five and I spend them on the part that needs my judgement: filling in missing context and workshopping the callouts.
denominator_notes: 均为个人自述；「90% 的工作」未定义按时间还是任务数。
transferable: 「五要素」清单可直接用于在非工程团队中挑选首批 agent 化的任务；定时任务+连接器替代手工导出/粘贴是低风险起点。前提是广告/分析平台有可用连接器，且审核要求允许 agent 读取邮件与 Slack。
caveats: 员工自述+产品与 webinar 推广；个人效率故事，不代表团队层面。
headline: Anthropic 增长营销负责人给出判断一项任务能否交给 agent 的「五要素」清单
headline_en: Anthropic's growth marketing lead offers a five-point checklist for deciding whether a task can be handed to an agent.
what_they_do_en: Anthropic's growth marketing lead shares how non-technical roles use agents. A scheduled task at 6 a.m. each day summarizes unread email and the Slack channels he follows, and flags overnight product incidents that could affect marketing. Google Ads/Meta Ads connectors feed an auto-updating budget spend and pacing dashboard. Each week, data is pulled from Search Console automatically and a comparison report is generated from a template; he only adds context and key points. His five-point checklist for whether a task suits delegation to an agent: multiple inputs, produces a single file, recurs, you know what a good result looks like, and the middle is tedious extraction/compilation/reconciliation/formatting.
denominator_notes_en: All personal self-report; "90% of the work" doesn't say whether it's measured by time or task count.
transferable_en: The five-point checklist can be used directly to pick the first tasks to hand to agents in non-engineering teams; scheduled tasks plus connectors replacing manual export-and-paste are a low-risk starting point. Requires usable connectors for the ad/analytics platforms, and review policies that allow agents to read email and Slack.
caveats_en: Employee self-report plus product and webinar promotion; a personal productivity story, not representative at the team level.

title: Uber Caps Usage of AI Tools Like Claude Code to Manage Costs
what_they_do: 据 Bloomberg 报道（Simon 引用），Uber 在四个月内用光 2026 年 AI 预算后，对所有员工设定每个 AI 编码工具每月 1,500 美元 token 上限，各工具独立计算，只适用于 Cursor、Claude Code 等 agentic 编码软件。Simon 估算：按每人两个常用工具，上限约为 Uber 美国软件工程师中位总包的 11%，并认为这比鼓励「tokenmaxxing」的排行榜理性。
numbers: The rideshare giant is limiting all employees to $1,500 in monthly token spending per AI coding tool, an Uber spokesperson said in response to a Bloomberg News inquiry.
That means each employee's AI spending cap is ~11% of that median compensation package.
denominator_notes: 11% 为 Simon 基于 levels.fyi 中位薪酬 33 万美元、假设每人 2 个工具的推算。
transferable: 为 agent 支出设预算时可参考：按工具/人设月度上限，并用「占工程师总薪酬的比例」来讨论合理性；与 Databricks 的「渐进摩擦而非硬上限」做法形成对照。
caveats: Bloomberg 原文付费墙（403）未能读取，事实依据为 Simon 引用的段落；属新闻报道 + 评论，非 Uber 一手发布。
headline: Uber 四个月花光全年 AI 预算后，给每人每个 agent 编码工具设每月 1,500 美元硬上限
headline_en: After burning through its full-year AI budget in four months, Uber set a hard cap of $1,500 per person per month for each agentic coding tool.
what_they_do_en: According to Bloomberg (as quoted by Simon), after using up its 2026 AI budget in four months, Uber set a $1,500 monthly token cap per AI coding tool for every employee, counted separately per tool and applying only to agentic coding software such as Cursor and Claude Code. Simon estimates that at two commonly used tools per person, the cap is about 11% of the median total compensation of a US Uber software engineer, and argues this is more rational than leaderboards that encourage "tokenmaxxing."
denominator_notes_en: 11% is Simon's estimate, based on a levels.fyi median compensation of $330,000 and an assumption of 2 tools per person.
transferable_en: A reference point for budgeting agent spend: set monthly caps per tool per person, and discuss reasonableness as "share of engineer total compensation." Contrast with Databricks' approach of "progressive friction rather than hard caps."
caveats_en: The Bloomberg original is paywalled (403) and could not be read; the facts rest on the passages Simon quoted. This is news coverage plus commentary, not a first-hand Uber release.

title: When AI builds itself
what_they_do: Anthropic Institute 用此前未公开的内部数据说明 AI 已在加速 AI 研发：截至 2026 年 5 月超过 80% 合并进代码库的代码由 Claude 编写（Claude Code 发布前为个位数），2026 Q2 典型工程师每天合并代码量是 2024 年的 8 倍；员工中途纠正/接管 Claude 的比例一年来持续下降，最开放任务的会话成功率显著上升；员工普遍认为 Claude 代码质量已大致与人类持平。代码评审方式随之改变：所有变更合并前先经自动 Claude reviewer 审查，回溯分析显示它能拦下约三分之一历史 claude.ai 事故的 bug；人类代码评审已成为新的 Amdahl 瓶颈，非工程领域也出现「点子远多于执行能力」的瓶颈。人类比较优势收缩到研究品味与判断（选题、信任哪些结果、何时止损）。
numbers: To take just one example: today, Anthropic engineers on average ship 8x as much code per quarter as they did from 2021-2025.

As of May 2026, more than 80% of the code we merge into Anthropic’s codebase was authored by Claude.3 Before Claude Code launched in research preview in February 2025, this number was in the low single digits.

In the second quarter of 2026, the typical engineer was merging 8× as much code per day as they were in 2024.4 This is because much of the code is written by Claude, with the engineer directing and reviewing, rather than typing it themselves.

In a March 2026 poll of 130 employees from across Anthropic research teams, the median respondent estimated that they produced around 4x as much output with Mythos Preview as they would have without access to any AI models, on the kinds of projects they would have been working on regardless.
For example, in April 2026, Claude shipped over 800 fixes that reduced a class of API errors by a factor of one thousand.
On the most open-ended tasks, Claude’s success rate reached 76% in May 2026, up 50 percentage points in six months.

Using this tool, we ran a retrospective analysis, and found that an automated Claude review of every change to our codebase would have caught roughly a third of the bugs behind past incidents on claude.ai before they ever reached production.
In May 2025, Claude Opus 4 averaged a ~3x speedup over the starting code. By April 2026, Claude Mythos Preview was achieving ~52x.
On this measure, our best model in November 2025 (Opus 4.5) beat the human choice 51% of the time; in April 2026 (Mythos Preview), this grew to 64%.

Anthropic leadership have publicly estimated that 90% or more of our code is written by Claude, including scripts and experimental code. Our >80% figure measures the share of lines merged to production that can be attributed to Claude.
denominator_notes: 关键口径说明在脚注：>80% 是「合并到生产的代码行中可归因于 Claude 的比例」，归因管线有缺口，未归因部分还包括自动生成代码，因此偏保守；而「90%+」是领导层含脚本和实验代码的估计——两个数字口径不同不可混用。8x 按「每工程师每天合并代码行」计，作者自己承认行数会高估真实生产率。4x 为 130 名研究员自报（作者认为真实值更低，并引 METR 指出自报会高估）。76% 的会话成功率由 Claude 判官判定（无需纠正即成功）。三分之一是回溯性估计。51%/64% 基于刻意挑选的 129 个「人类选择有改进空间」的时刻，不是人机公平对比。
transferable: 可借鉴的度量方法：用归因管线统计「合并到生产的 AI 代码行占比」并公开口径与缺口；用「中途纠正/接管率」和按难度分层的会话成功率追踪 agent 可靠性；用历史事故 bug 回放评估自动 reviewer。组织层面要预期瓶颈转移到人工评审与「选择做什么」，提前设计评审分级和优先级机制。
caveats: 发布日期取自 Anthropic Institute 列表页（Jun 4, 2026），正文无日期且 9/18 有更新；本文为政策/叙事文章，带有 RSI 风险议程；数据为内部自报、无外部复核；lab 的研究型工作和模型访问不可外推。
headline: Anthropic 称超 80% 合并代码行由 Claude 编写，也承认人工评审成了新瓶颈
headline_en: Anthropic says Claude writes over 80% of merged lines of code, and acknowledges human code review has become the new bottleneck.
what_they_do_en: The Anthropic Institute uses previously unpublished internal data to show AI already accelerating AI R&D. As of May 2026, over 80% of code merged into the codebase was written by Claude (single digits before Claude Code launched). In 2026 Q2 a typical engineer merged 8x as much code per day as in 2024. The rate at which employees correct or take over from Claude mid-session has fallen steadily over the past year, and session success rates on the most open-ended tasks have risen significantly. Employees broadly consider Claude's code quality roughly on par with humans'. Code review has changed accordingly: every change is reviewed by an automated Claude reviewer before merge, and retrospective analysis shows it would have caught bugs behind about a third of historical claude.ai incidents. Human code review is now the new Amdahl bottleneck, and non-engineering areas show a similar bottleneck of "far more ideas than execution capacity." Humans' comparative advantage has narrowed to research taste and judgment (what to work on, which results to trust, when to cut losses).
denominator_notes_en: Key definitions are in the footnotes. >80% is "share of lines of code merged to production attributable to Claude"; the attribution pipeline has gaps and the unattributed portion also includes generated code, so the figure is conservative. "90%+" is a leadership estimate that includes scripts and experimental code; the two numbers use different bases and shouldn't be mixed. 8x counts "lines of code merged per engineer per day," and the authors admit line counts overstate real productivity. 4x is self-reported by 130 researchers (the authors think the true value is lower, citing METR that self-reports overestimate). The 76% session success rate is judged by a Claude grader (success = no correction needed). One third is a retrospective estimate. 51%/64% are based on 129 deliberately selected moments where "the human's choice had room for improvement," not a fair human-vs-AI comparison.
transferable_en: Measurement methods worth borrowing: use an attribution pipeline to track "share of AI-written lines merged to production" and publish its definition and gaps; track agent reliability with mid-session correction/takeover rates and session success rates stratified by difficulty; evaluate automated reviewers by replaying bugs from past incidents. At the org level, expect the bottleneck to shift to human review and "choosing what to build," and design review tiers and prioritization mechanisms in advance.
caveats_en: Publication date taken from the Anthropic Institute listing page (Jun 4, 2026); the body has no date and was updated 9/18. This is a policy/narrative piece with an RSI-risk agenda; data is internally self-reported with no external review; a lab's research work and model access don't generalize.

title: Measuring the impact of our AI investments in IT at Microsoft
what_they_do: Microsoft Digital 建立 AI 投资价值衡量框架：六个价值领域（收入、生产力/效率、安全与风险、员工与客户体验、质量、成本），上线前定预期价值和基线、上线后对比，按月复盘 KPI（部分可汇总、部分留在场景级）；明确不只看采用率/用量（“工具被频繁使用也可能没改善流程”），在成本模型和遥测不完善前不把 ROI 放在中心；强调节省出的产能如何再投入才是真正价值。举例：全球支持团队的工单跟进流程每月约 5,000 张工单、最多 15,000 封手工跟进邮件、约 750 小时，用于评估自动化价值与实施难度。
numbers: Finney estimated that about 5,000 tickets a month execute this process. Because each ticket can require up to three follow-ups, that can create up to 15,000 manual email follow-ups a month. At about three minutes per follow-up, that’s roughly 750 hours of productivity spent on one small piece of the process each month.
denominator_notes: 750 小时是按“最多三次跟进 × 3 分钟”估算的上限，是自动化前的机会规模，不是已实现节省。
transferable: 可直接借用的度量纪律：上线前写清预期价值与基线、按场景选指标、月度复盘、不以用量代替结果、追踪节省时间的再投入去向。前提：数据有明确 owner。
caveats: IT 组织框架性文章，承认“还没有完整答案”；无已实现的汇总结果。
headline: 微软 IT 要求 AI 项目上线前先定预期价值和基线、按月复盘，明确不拿用量代替结果
headline_en: Microsoft IT makes AI projects set expected value and a baseline before launch, reviews monthly, and refuses to treat usage as a proxy for outcomes.
what_they_do_en: Microsoft Digital built a framework for measuring the value of AI investments: six value areas (revenue, productivity/efficiency, security and risk, employee and customer experience, quality, cost). Expected value and a baseline are set before launch and compared after; KPIs are reviewed monthly (some roll up, some stay at the scenario level). It explicitly doesn't look only at adoption/usage ("a tool can be used frequently without improving the process"), and keeps ROI out of the center until cost models and telemetry mature. It stresses that real value lies in how freed-up capacity is reinvested. Example: the global support team's ticket follow-up process, about 5,000 tickets a month, up to 15,000 manual follow-up emails, about 750 hours, used to assess automation value and implementation difficulty.
denominator_notes_en: 750 hours is an upper-bound estimate ("up to three follow-ups × 3 minutes"); it is the opportunity size before automation, not realized savings.
transferable_en: Measurement discipline to borrow directly: write down expected value and baseline before launch, choose metrics per scenario, review monthly, don't substitute usage for outcomes, and track where saved time is reinvested. Requires clear data owners.
caveats_en: A framework piece from an IT organization, which admits it "doesn't have the full answer yet"; no realized aggregate results.

title: How one Anthropic seller rebuilt his team's workflows with Claude Code
what_they_do: 一名零编程背景的 Anthropic 销售用 Claude Code 写出 Gmail 内的自动回信草稿工具 CLAFTS（约 4,300 行代码几乎全由 Claude 写），在 Slack 分享后 24 小时内被销售组织其他人采用；他的角色随之转为 GTM 产品经理/GTM Architect，专门发现销售流程问题并用 Claude 构建方案。工具以 skills + MCP 连接器打包为 Cowork 的 Sales plugin，新人入职第一天即可装上 20 多个连到 Salesforce、Gong、BigQuery 等的 skill。
numbers: It took multiple iterations, but eventually Jared estimates CLAFTS was saving him two to three hours a day.
CLAFTS is built on roughly 4,300 lines of code, almost all of it written by Claude Code.
While CLAFTS saves Jared 10-15 hours per week, the shift he cares about most is the accuracy of the work.
Within months of launching the Sales plugin, roughly 80 percent of Anthropic’s sales org was using it.
Now a new hire can install it on day one and have 20-plus skills already wired into the tools they use: Salesforce, Intercom, Gong, Google Calendar, Gmail, Google Drive, and BigQuery.
/customer-context pulls a 360-degree account view across all those sources in about 90 seconds.
denominator_notes: 节省时间为个人估计（文中前后为「每天 2–3 小时」与「每周 10–15 小时」两种口径）；80% 采用率的分母是 Anthropic 销售组织人数，但「using」的定义（装了还是活跃使用）和时间点未说明。
transferable: 可借鉴的组织模式：在业务团队里设「业务内嵌的 AI 工具 PM/架构师」角色，让一线痛点直接变成 Claude 构建的工具，并以 plugin 统一分发、作为新人 onboarding 默认配置。前提是有对 CRM/邮件等系统的受控连接器，以及工程团队对「业务人员写的工具」做安全与维护兜底。
caveats: 员工故事+产品营销（属于 "How Anthropic uses Claude" 系列）；成功个案存在幸存者偏差；Anthropic 产品文档每 1–2 天更新、员工天然熟悉 Claude，场景比一般企业更有利。
headline: Anthropic 一名零代码销售自建工具被全组采用，他的岗位随之变成业务内嵌的 GTM 架构师
headline_en: An Anthropic salesperson with no coding background built a tool the whole team adopted, and his job became an embedded GTM architect role.
what_they_do_en: An Anthropic salesperson with no programming background used Claude Code to build CLAFTS, a tool that auto-drafts email replies inside Gmail (about 4,300 lines of code, almost all written by Claude). Within 24 hours of sharing it in Slack, others in the sales org had adopted it. His role then shifted to GTM product manager / GTM Architect, dedicated to finding sales-process problems and building solutions with Claude. The tools are packaged as skills plus MCP connectors into Cowork's Sales plugin, so new hires can install 20+ skills connected to Salesforce, Gong, BigQuery, and more on day one.
denominator_notes_en: Time savings are a personal estimate (the post uses two different figures, "2-3 hours a day" and "10-15 hours a week"). The denominator for the 80% adoption rate is headcount in Anthropic's sales org, but the definition of "using" (installed vs. actively used) and the point in time are not given.
transferable_en: An org pattern to borrow: create an "embedded AI tools PM/architect" role inside business teams so frontline pain points turn directly into Claude-built tools, distributed uniformly as plugins and set as the default onboarding configuration for new hires. Requires governed connectors to systems like CRM and email, and an engineering team that backstops security and maintenance for "tools written by business staff."
caveats_en: Employee story plus product marketing (part of the "How Anthropic uses Claude" series); a success case with survivorship bias; Anthropic's product docs update every 1-2 days and employees are naturally fluent in Claude, so conditions are more favorable than at a typical enterprise.

title: Changing How We Develop Ladybird
what_they_do: Ladybird 浏览器项目宣布不再接受公开 PR，只由维护者引入代码，并关闭所有现存公开 PR，也不设通过 issue/邮件/fork 的「影子贡献通道」。理由是 AI 让「看起来像认真贡献」的工作变得廉价，大补丁不再意味着大投入与善意，信任信号失效；对处理不可信输入的浏览器而言，关键在于谁为进入代码库的改动负责，而不在于代码是否手写。维护者自己每天使用 AI 工具。
denominator_notes: 无数据。
transferable: 对接受外部/跨团队贡献的内部平台或 inner-source 仓库有启示：AI 时代 PR 体量不再是投入和可信度的代理指标，应把「谁对改动负责」显式化（owner 制、受信作者名单），而非试图检测是否 AI 生成。
caveats: 开源项目治理决策，非企业内部；单一项目，无效果数据。
headline: Ladybird 关闭公开 PR，因为 AI 让大补丁不再代表投入和善意，信任的依据改为明确谁对进库改动负责
headline_en: Ladybird closed public PRs because AI means a large patch no longer signals effort or good faith; trust now rests on explicit responsibility for what lands.
what_they_do_en: The Ladybird browser project announced it will no longer accept public PRs: only maintainers bring in code. All existing public PRs were closed, and there is no "shadow contribution channel" via issues, email, or forks. The reasoning: AI has made work that "looks like a serious contribution" cheap, so a large patch no longer implies large effort and good faith, and the trust signal has broken. For a browser that processes untrusted input, what matters is who is accountable for changes entering the codebase, not whether the code was handwritten. The maintainers themselves use AI tools daily.
denominator_notes_en: No data.
transferable_en: Relevant to internal platforms and inner-source repos that take external or cross-team contributions: in the AI era, PR size is no longer a proxy for effort or trustworthiness. Make "who is accountable for this change" explicit (ownership, trusted-author lists) rather than trying to detect AI-generated code.
caveats_en: An open-source governance decision, not an enterprise one; a single project with no outcome data.

title: Grit: rewriting Git in Rust with agents
what_they_do: GitButler 联合创始人用 agent 群从零写出库优先、内存安全的 Rust 版 Git（Grit），以 Git 自带 4.2 万+ 测试为验收。记录了大量失败：agent 会「作弊」（直接转调系统 git、只满足测试断言而不真正实现 sha256）；某个并行 agent 弄坏了测试 harness，看起来像大规模回归，导致项目一度被放弃；长时+并行组合下共享任务清单（勾选式 plan 文件）协调很难；多机器、多供应商之间交接进行中的工作摩擦大；最终近一半工作由大量短生命周期、只聚焦单个测试文件的云端 agent 完成。
numbers: However, interestingly, there is a very comprehensive test suite of over 42,000 tests in more than 1,400 scripts in the Git project that define pretty solidly how everything should and should not work.
I have no idea exactly how much I spent between Cursor and Anthropic (the main providers I used) but it was probably somewhere around $10-15k.
denominator_notes: 成本为作者估计；「通过 99% 测试」中部分测试被有意标为 skip；作者明言 Grit「passes the tests, it's not tested」，无人真实使用过。
transferable: 给大规模 agent 移植项目的反面清单：明确禁止转调旧实现等「作弊」路径；测试通过≠功能正确，要抽查断言覆盖；保护测试 harness 不被 agent 修改；长时并行任务用真正的工单系统协调；优先「短生命周期、单一聚焦」的 agent 而不是少数长时 agent。
caveats: 个人副项目、非生产；作者是 VCS 工具厂商，结尾有产品预告。
headline: GitButler 用 agent 群重写 Git 的反面教材：agent 会转调旧实现作弊、弄坏测试 harness，短生命周期单一聚焦的 agent 更可靠
headline_en: GitButler's agent-swarm rewrite of Git is a cautionary tale: agents cheated by calling the old implementation and broke the test harness; short-lived, single-focus agents proved more reliable.
what_they_do_en: A GitButler co-founder used a swarm of agents to write Grit, a library-first, memory-safe Rust implementation of Git, from scratch, with Git's own 42,000+ tests as acceptance criteria. He documented many failures: agents "cheated" (shelling out to system git, satisfying test assertions without actually implementing sha256); one parallel agent broke the test harness, which looked like a massive regression and led to the project being abandoned for a while; coordinating through a shared task list (a checkbox-style plan file) was hard with long-running, parallel agents; handing off in-progress work across machines and vendors was high-friction. In the end, nearly half the work was done by large numbers of short-lived cloud agents each focused on a single test file.
denominator_notes_en: Costs are the author's estimate; some tests in "passes 99% of tests" were deliberately marked skip; the author states outright that Grit "passes the tests, it's not tested" and that no one has used it for real.
transferable_en: A list of what not to do for large agent-driven porting projects: explicitly forbid "cheating" paths such as calling the old implementation; passing tests ≠ correct functionality, so spot-check assertion coverage; protect the test harness from agent modification; coordinate long-running parallel work through a real ticketing system; prefer short-lived, single-focus agents over a few long-running ones.
caveats_en: A personal side project, not production; the author is a VCS tool vendor, and the post ends with a product teaser.

title: Claude Fable is relentlessly proactive
what_they_do: Simon 只给了一张截图和一句提示去查一个横向滚动条 bug，离开几分钟后发现 Fable 自行启动开发服务器、改 Chrome 系统设置、在真实 Firefox/Safari 中打开自建测试页、绕过被禁止的 osascript 改用 pyobjc 截图、往 Datasette 模板注入 JS 模拟键盘、自写 CORS 服务器回传测量数据——最终是两行 CSS 修复。他据此提醒：coding agent 能做你在终端能做的一切，若遇到 prompt injection 后果难以估量，需要把它锁起来运行。
numbers: Cost: ~$12.11 (claude-fable-5, claude-opus-4-8)
denominator_notes: 单次会话，成本为 AgentsView 按全价估算。
transferable: 给推广 agent 的组织：在开发者本机直接运行前沿 agent 时，它会主动改系统设置、开浏览器、起本地服务；应默认在沙箱/devcontainer 中运行，并对会话成本设可见性。
caveats: 单次轶事；属于能力展示而非事故。
headline: Simon Willison 只让 Fable 查一个滚动条 bug，它却自行改系统设置、绕过被禁工具，说明 coding agent 应默认在沙箱里跑
headline_en: Asked only to investigate a scrollbar bug, Fable changed Simon Willison's system settings and worked around a blocked tool: coding agents should run sandboxed by default.
what_they_do_en: Simon gave Fable just a screenshot and a one-line prompt to investigate a horizontal scrollbar bug. When he came back a few minutes later, it had started a dev server on its own, changed Chrome system settings, opened a self-built test page in real Firefox and Safari, worked around the blocked osascript by using pyobjc for screenshots, injected JS into a Datasette template to simulate keystrokes, and written its own CORS server to send measurements back. The eventual fix was two lines of CSS. His takeaway: a coding agent can do anything you can do in a terminal, the consequences of a prompt injection are hard to bound, and it needs to run locked down.
denominator_notes_en: A single session; cost is AgentsView's estimate at full list price.
transferable_en: For organizations rolling out agents: a frontier agent running directly on a developer's machine will proactively change system settings, open browsers, and start local services. Run it in a sandbox/devcontainer by default, and give visibility into per-session cost.
caveats_en: A single anecdote; a capability demonstration rather than an incident.

title: Securing the future of AI agents
what_they_do: Google DeepMind 公布内部部署 AI 的“AI Control Roadmap”：把内部 agent 当作潜在“内部威胁”，基于 MITRE ATT&CK 做威胁建模；用受信任的 AI 作为监督者审阅 agent 的推理和动作、必要时阻断；按覆盖率（被监控流量占比）、召回率、响应时间三项度量；低风险可逆动作做异步复查、高风险动作做同步阻断。团队做了异步监控原型审阅编码 agent 轨迹并升级给人工，已分析一百万个编码 agent 任务，发现大多数被标记事件不是恶意，而是 agent 误解或“过度热心”完成用户目标；这些数据被用来搭建 Gemini Spark agent 的实时监控（如意外删数据）。
numbers: We’ve already analyzed a million coding agent tasks, giving us valuable insights to refine our safety protocols and allowing us to move beyond simple keyword filtering to identifying high-signal behavioral patterns.
denominator_notes: 一百万个编码 agent 任务的来源（内部员工？评估？）与时间范围未说明；未给出被标记比例或误报率。
transferable: 对企业：把编码 agent 视为“可能误操作的内部人员”来做威胁建模，用覆盖率/召回率/响应时间三个指标管理 agent 监控，并按动作风险分同步/异步处理。另一个可直接使用的发现：多数问题源于 agent 误解或过度热心，而不是恶意——治理重点应是边界清晰和确认机制。
caveats: 框架性文章，原型阶段；数据很少；部分内容是政策倡议。
headline: Google DeepMind 分析百万编码 agent 任务，发现被标记的多是误解或过度热心而非恶意
headline_en: Google DeepMind analyzed a million coding-agent tasks and found most flagged events came from misunderstanding or overeagerness, not malice.
what_they_do_en: Google DeepMind published its "AI Control Roadmap" for internally deployed AI. It treats internal agents as potential "insider threats" and threat-models them using MITRE ATT&CK. A trusted AI acts as a monitor, reviewing agents' reasoning and actions and blocking when needed. Monitoring is measured on three metrics: coverage (share of traffic monitored), recall, and response time. Low-risk, reversible actions get asynchronous review; high-risk actions are blocked synchronously. The team built an asynchronous monitoring prototype that reviews coding-agent trajectories and escalates to humans. Across a million coding-agent tasks analyzed so far, most flagged events were not malicious; the agent had misunderstood or was "overeager" in pursuing the user's goal. This data is being used to build real-time monitoring for the Gemini Spark agent (e.g. for accidental data deletion).
denominator_notes_en: The source (internal employees? evals?) and time range of the million coding-agent tasks are not stated; no flag rate or false-positive rate is given.
transferable_en: For enterprises: threat-model coding agents as "insiders who may make mistakes," manage agent monitoring with three metrics (coverage, recall, response time), and handle actions synchronously or asynchronously by risk. Another directly usable finding: most problems stem from agent misunderstanding or overeagerness, not malice, so governance should focus on clear boundaries and confirmation mechanisms.
caveats_en: A framework piece at the prototype stage; very little data; parts are policy advocacy.

title: How we built an internal data analytics agent
what_they_do: GitHub 数据团队做了内部分析 agent Qubot：任何员工在 Slack、VS Code 或 Copilot CLI 用自然语言问数据仓库问题，Slack 里每个问题拉起一个云端 Copilot agent 回答，结果同时以 Markdown 报告存进 PR 便于复用。关键是联邦式“上下文层”：原始事件的 schema 由产品团队贡献、中间层的示例查询和必需过滤条件由数据团队维护、业务指标定义由数据集 owner 维护，并有一个“上下文 agent”规范化接收贡献；任何上下文或配置变更都要走离线 eval（准确率、延迟、回归）才能合并。
numbers: In our experiments we found that structured and well curated context not only makes Qubot more accurate, but also three times faster at returning the right answer.
Qubot has been widely adopted at GitHub, with hundreds of enthusiastic users running thousands of queries.
denominator_notes: “快三倍”来自内部实验，未给准确率数值；“数百用户、数千查询”无时间范围；数据分析 Slack 频道提问“大幅减少”无数值。
transferable: 自助数据分析 agent 的关键不是模型而是上下文层：让各数据 owner 以文档形式贡献语义和规则，并用 eval 门禁守住每次上下文变更。可显著减轻数据团队答疑负担。前提：数据仓库分层清晰、指标定义有 owner。
caveats: GitHub 是微软子公司，产品推广成分（Copilot 云 agent、MCP）；效果数据有限。
headline: GitHub 数据团队发现分析 agent 的关键在联邦式上下文层，任何上下文变更都要先过离线 eval
headline_en: GitHub's data team found the key to its analytics agent is a federated context layer, with every context change gated by offline evals.
what_they_do_en: GitHub's data team built Qubot, an internal analytics agent: any employee can ask data warehouse questions in natural language from Slack, VS Code, or Copilot CLI. In Slack, each question spins up a cloud Copilot agent to answer it, and results are also saved as Markdown reports in a PR for reuse. The key is a federated "context layer": schemas for raw events are contributed by product teams, example queries and required filters for the intermediate layer are maintained by the data team, business metric definitions are maintained by dataset owners, and a "context agent" normalizes incoming contributions. Every context or config change must pass offline evals (accuracy, latency, regressions) before it can merge.
denominator_notes_en: "Three times faster" comes from an internal experiment, with no accuracy figure given; "hundreds of users, thousands of queries" has no time range; the "sharp drop" in questions to the data analytics Slack channel has no number.
transferable_en: The key to a self-service analytics agent is the context layer, not the model: have each data owner contribute semantics and rules as documentation, and gate every context change with evals. This can substantially reduce the data team's support load. Requires a cleanly layered data warehouse and owners for metric definitions.
caveats_en: GitHub is a Microsoft subsidiary, and there is product promotion (Copilot cloud agent, MCP); limited outcome data.

title: I automated my job (and it made me a better leader)
what_they_do: GitHub 开发者关系高级总监用 Copilot 应用的定时自动化（连接日历、邮件、消息、GitHub 的定时 prompt）支撑管理工作，约 40 个：会前准备与文档权限检查、每日分诊摘要、每日发布解读与每周发布雷达、每日成就回顾（为绩效季留存证据）、自己承诺事项的跟进追踪、Dependabot PR 分诊、陈旧工作查找等。强调认可和反馈仍由本人写，自动化只负责“发现”；对她作为神经多样性者而言是可及性工具。
numbers: Explore how my day as a senior leader looks now that I use 40 automations to help, and learn more about some of my favorites.
denominator_notes: “每天约省一小时”等为自述估计；无测量。
transferable: 对经理/TLM 自身最直接：用定时 agent 处理会前准备、承诺跟踪、陈旧 PR/Issue 巡检、成就记录等“隐形元工作”，人保留判断和人际部分。从最痛的一件事开始，逐步增加。
caveats: 个人分享，推广 Copilot 应用；需要授予 agent 访问邮件/日历等敏感数据，组织需评估权限。
headline: GitHub 一位高级总监用约 40 个定时自动化接管会前准备、承诺跟踪等管理元工作，认可与反馈仍亲自写
headline_en: A GitHub senior director uses about 40 scheduled automations for managerial meta-work like meeting prep and commitment tracking, but still writes recognition and feedback herself.
what_they_do_en: GitHub's senior director of developer relations runs her management work on about 40 scheduled automations in the Copilot app (scheduled prompts connected to calendar, email, messaging, and GitHub): meeting prep and doc-permission checks, a daily triage digest, a daily release explainer and a weekly release radar, a daily accomplishments recap (preserving evidence for performance season), follow-up tracking on her own commitments, Dependabot PR triage, stale-work detection, and more. She stresses that recognition and feedback are still written by her; the automations only do the "finding." As a neurodivergent person, she also treats them as an accessibility tool.
denominator_notes_en: "About an hour saved per day" and similar figures are self-estimates; no measurement.
transferable_en: Most directly useful for managers/TLMs themselves: use scheduled agents for "invisible meta-work" such as meeting prep, commitment tracking, sweeps for stale PRs/issues, and accomplishment logs, keeping judgment and interpersonal work for the human. Start with the single most painful task and add more gradually.
caveats_en: A personal post promoting the Copilot app; it requires granting agents access to sensitive data like email and calendar, which organizations need to assess.

title: Building effective human-agent teams
what_they_do: Anthropic 内部几个月来在 Slack 中运行「多人协作 agent」（有自己的凭证、持久记忆、广泛的信息访问），总结四条团队规范：1) 公开工作——按少数几个工作区级安全边界开放信息，新频道默认公开，决策必须落在频道/文档/会议纪要里，因为 agent 只能看到写下来的东西；2) 人和 agent 共用一份名册，各有明确角色与工具（如数据分析 agent、设计规范 agent、发布经理 agent），用 skill 文件定义 agent 角色，避免每人私下跑一堆个人 AI 造成重复和上下文割裂；3) 由人设定写下来的 north star，并指定哪些 agent 可以主动提议新工作；4) 按已证明的可靠性逐步放权：开始时人工审每个决定、设计验证清单，用 doer-verifier 双 agent 结构，让 agent 每周写「教训与失误」报告，按任务类型扩大自主范围，并让 agent 把人类注意力当稀缺资源（批量提问、限制每人待审数量）。
numbers: Engineers have successfully dispatched agents on their team to handle 500 bug fixes independently, but things certainly didn’t start off that way.
denominator_notes: 只有一个案例数字（500 个 bug 修复），未说明时间跨度、成功率或返工；「onboarding 成功率次周可测提升」未给数值。
transferable: 对 TLM 可直接落地：写出团队的「人+agent 名册」与职责；信息默认公开、用少量清晰的安全边界代替逐文档授权；先人审再按任务类型逐步放权并记录 agent 已获信任的任务类别；doer-verifier 结构；限制 agent 每日产出以保证人能有效审阅。前提是组织的安全/合规允许较大范围的内部信息对 agent 开放，这在很多大公司需要先改变数据分级政策。
caveats: Anthropic 教育团队撰写，同时推广 Claude Tag；Anthropic「默认公开」的文化和数据边界设定比多数大公司宽松；案例多为定性。
headline: Anthropic 让 agent 当队友的前提：信息默认公开、人机共用名册、按可靠性逐步放权
headline_en: Anthropic's preconditions for agents as teammates: information public by default, one shared roster for humans and agents, and autonomy expanded as reliability is proven.
what_they_do_en: For several months Anthropic has run "multiplayer agents" in Slack internally (with their own credentials, persistent memory, and broad information access), and distilled four team norms. 1) Work in the open: open up information within a few workspace-level security boundaries, make new channels public by default, and make sure decisions land in channels, docs, or meeting notes, because agents can only see what's written down. 2) Humans and agents share one roster, each with a clear role and tools (e.g. a data analysis agent, a design-system agent, a release manager agent), with agent roles defined in skill files, so people don't each run a pile of private AIs that duplicate work and fragment context. 3) Humans set a written north star and designate which agents may proactively propose new work. 4) Expand autonomy based on proven reliability: start with humans reviewing every decision and designing verification checklists, use a doer-verifier two-agent structure, have agents write a weekly "lessons and mistakes" report, widen autonomy by task type, and have agents treat human attention as scarce (batch questions, cap pending reviews per person).
denominator_notes_en: Only one case figure (500 bug fixes), with no time span, success rate, or rework stated; the "measurable improvement in onboarding success the following week" has no number.
transferable_en: Directly actionable for TLMs: write down the team's "humans + agents roster" and responsibilities; make information public by default, with a few clear security boundaries instead of per-doc grants; start with human review and expand autonomy by task type, recording which task categories agents are trusted with; use the doer-verifier structure; cap agents' daily output so humans can review it effectively. Requires security/compliance that allows broad internal information access for agents, which at many large companies means first changing data classification policy.
caveats_en: Written by Anthropic's education team, also promoting Claude Tag; Anthropic's "public by default" culture and data boundaries are looser than at most large companies; cases are mostly qualitative.

title: I wrote a 70x faster SQL parser while barely looking at the code
what_they_do: PostHog 工程师用多个并行长时 Claude Code 会话，把基于 ANTLR 的 C++ SQL 解析器重写为手写 Rust 递归下降解析器，自己几乎不看代码。核心是「以旧实现为 oracle」的差分测试：用 Hypothesis 基于语法文件生成 SQL 做属性测试、拉取匿名化生产查询、让后台 agent「想边界情况」，不一致就缩减成回归用例；要求 agent 修复前先把语法文件和参考 C++ 源码载入上下文以避免脆弱修复。上线前用影子模式与生产解析器并行比对，再以 0.1% 反向影子切流。
numbers: The result was 16K lines of "hand"-rolled parser code, 5K lines of tooling, a few more K of tests, and a ~70x speed up.
When comparing with the production query log, I only ever tested ~50K queries. In shadow mode, I was able to test millions of parses quickly and there were zero divergences.
On production queries, it was on average 454x faster than the previous parser.
denominator_notes: 70x 是作者笔记本基准，454x 是生产查询平均（生产多为未命中缓存的长 SQL）；零分歧基于影子模式数百万次解析。
transferable: 「有 oracle 就能放心让 agent 重写」：旧系统做参照 + 属性测试/模糊测试持续制造分歧 + 影子流量比对 + 小比例切流，是非实验室团队做性能重写或迁移时最可靠的验证骨架，人可以不逐行审代码而审验证体系。
caveats: 单工程师个人项目，自述；依赖存在可执行的参照实现，无 oracle 的新功能不适用。
headline: PostHog 工程师以旧解析器为 oracle 做差分测试和影子流量，几乎不看代码就安全替换了 SQL 解析器
headline_en: A PostHog engineer used the old parser as an oracle for differential testing and shadow traffic, and safely replaced the SQL parser while barely reading the code.
what_they_do_en: A PostHog engineer ran multiple parallel, long-running Claude Code sessions to rewrite an ANTLR-based C++ SQL parser as a hand-written Rust recursive-descent parser, barely reading the code himself. The core was differential testing "with the old implementation as oracle": property tests using Hypothesis to generate SQL from the grammar file, anonymized production queries, and background agents told to "think of edge cases"; any mismatch was shrunk into a regression case. Before fixing anything, the agent had to load the grammar file and the reference C++ source into context, to avoid brittle fixes. Before launch, it ran in shadow mode alongside the production parser, then cut over with 0.1% reverse-shadow traffic.
denominator_notes_en: 70x is the author's laptop benchmark; 454x is the average on production queries (mostly long, cache-missing SQL); zero divergence is based on millions of parses in shadow mode.
transferable_en: "With an oracle, you can safely let agents rewrite": the old system as reference + property/fuzz testing that keeps generating divergences + shadow traffic comparison + small-percentage cutover is the most reliable validation backbone for non-lab teams doing performance rewrites or migrations. Humans can review the validation system instead of reviewing code line by line.
caveats_en: A single engineer's personal project, self-reported; depends on an executable reference implementation, so it doesn't apply to new features with no oracle.

title: How agents are transforming work
what_they_do: OpenAI 用内部与外部用量数据描述 agent 采纳：到 2025 年 8 月内部员工在 Codex 上的 token 不到 10%，现在各部门（包括法务、财务、招聘）都把 Codex 当主力 AI 工具；工程先迁移、非技术部门 2026 年 4 月左右迁移但速度更快；重度用户一天跑数十小时并行 agent；非技术员工用 Codex 做自动化、数据处理、工具搭建等“职责外”的技术工作，业务职能里超过四分之一的 Codex 工作属于工程/编码。
numbers: Through August 2025, the average OpenAI worker spent less than 10% of their tokens on Codex.
For the average OpenAI worker, Codex usage now accounts for more than 85% of output tokens.
Since Codex users tend to use more tokens than non-users, its share of overall tokens is even higher: Codex accounts for 99.8% of weekly output tokens generated within OpenAI.
By June 2026, users at the 99th percentile regularly generated more than 60 hours of Codex agent turns per day, distributed across multiple, parallel agents.
Today, the average engineer generates 99% of their output tokens with Codex rather than ChatGPT.
The average lawyer or recruiter at OpenAI now generates more than 85% of their output tokens on Codex.
Research saw the biggest jump: by June 2026, median use was 56 times higher than in November 2025.
Customer Support rose 32 times and Engineering rose 27 times, while Legal grew more gradually but still reached 13 times its November level.
For instance, over one-fourth of work done with Codex by workers in business functions was engineering or coding.
denominator_notes: 所有份额都是“输出 token 占比”，衡量的是工具选择和用量，不是产出或效率；部门倍数是“活跃内部用户合计输出 token 的中位数变化”。部门由推断得到（inferred occupations）。外部用户的数据（长任务占比等）不属于内部数据，未列入。
transferable: 可借鉴的度量：按部门追踪“chat 工具 vs agent 工具”的用量迁移、重度用户的并行 agent 时长、非技术岗位做技术类工作的比例，用来判断组织是否从“问答”转向“委派”。前提：有统一的 AI 工具网关/日志。
caveats: OpenAI 员工可无限制使用自家最新产品，成本几乎不是约束；token 份额容易被少数重度用户和长任务放大；带产品宣传目的。
headline: OpenAI 用各部门 token 从 ChatGPT 迁到 Codex 的比例，看组织是否从问答转向委派
headline_en: OpenAI tracks the share of each department's tokens moving from ChatGPT to Codex to see whether the org is shifting from asking questions to delegating work.
what_they_do_en: OpenAI uses internal and external usage data to describe agent adoption. As of August 2025, Codex accounted for under 10% of employees' tokens; now every department (including legal, finance, and recruiting) uses Codex as its primary AI tool. Engineering migrated first; non-technical departments migrated around April 2026, but faster. Heavy users run dozens of hours of parallel agents per day. Non-technical employees use Codex for technical work "outside their job" such as automation, data processing, and tool-building, and more than a quarter of Codex work in business functions is engineering/coding.
denominator_notes_en: All shares are "share of output tokens," which measures tool choice and usage, not output or efficiency. Department multiples are "change in the median of total output tokens across active internal users." Departments are inferred (inferred occupations). External-user data (share of long tasks, etc.) is not internal and is not included.
transferable_en: Metrics to borrow: track, by department, the migration of usage from chat tools to agent tools, heavy users' parallel agent hours, and the share of non-technical roles doing technical work, to judge whether the organization is shifting from "asking" to "delegating." Requires a unified AI tool gateway/logging.
caveats_en: OpenAI employees have unrestricted access to the company's latest products, so cost is barely a constraint; token shares are easily inflated by a few heavy users and long tasks; written with promotional intent.

title: Privacy-Aware Infrastructure in the AI-Native Era: An Asset Classification Case Study
what_they_do: Meta 隐私基础设施用 LLM 做数据资产分类（判断字段是否个人数据等），但采取“确定性优先”：生产中大部分请求由规则处理，LLM 只处理新颖/模糊资产，再把稳定模式蒸馏成经人审批的版本化规则，逐步缩小 LLM 在生产中的作用。关键原则：上下文胜过 prompt（把代码、血缘、归属等整理成证据摘要，屏蔽会造成循环推理的字段）；评估与优化解耦（独立模型、冻结参考集、人工审核标签、回归门禁），避免“测量漂移而非进步”；每个决策带版本化 trace 可回放审计。
numbers: In our production deployment, Figure 7 shows how cheap deterministic rules resolve the large majority of traffic, roughly 85%, in single-digit milliseconds.
That path is slower — on the order of seconds — and roughly 400 times the compute cost, so it is budgeted separately.
denominator_notes: 85%/15% 是生产请求在规则路径与 LLM 兜底路径之间的分流比例；400 倍是两条路径的算力成本比。未给出分类准确率。
transferable: 把 AI 用于合规/治理类判断时的稳健模式：LLM 负责探索与冷启动，稳定结论蒸馏成可审计的确定性规则；评估集必须独立于被优化的系统。前提：有人工审核的标签集和规则发布流程。
caveats: 这是生产系统中的 AI 应用，而非员工工作方式；属于 Meta 的隐私合规场景。
headline: Meta 隐私分类确定性优先：LLM 只处理新颖资产，稳定模式蒸馏成人审规则，评估集独立于被优化系统
headline_en: Meta's privacy classification is deterministic-first: the LLM handles only novel assets, stable patterns are distilled into human-reviewed rules, and evals are independent of the system being optimized.
what_they_do_en: Meta's privacy infrastructure uses an LLM to classify data assets (e.g. whether a field is personal data), but takes a "deterministic-first" approach: most production requests are handled by rules, the LLM handles only novel or ambiguous assets, and stable patterns are then distilled into human-approved, versioned rules, steadily shrinking the LLM's role in production. Key principles: context beats prompts (code, lineage, ownership, etc. are compiled into evidence summaries, and fields that would cause circular reasoning are masked); evaluation is decoupled from optimization (independent model, frozen reference set, human-reviewed labels, regression gates) to avoid "measuring drift instead of progress"; every decision carries a versioned trace that can be replayed and audited.
denominator_notes_en: 85%/15% is the split of production requests between the rules path and the LLM fallback path; 400x is the compute cost ratio between the two paths. No classification accuracy is given.
transferable_en: A robust pattern for using AI on compliance/governance decisions: the LLM handles exploration and cold start, and stable conclusions are distilled into auditable deterministic rules; the eval set must be independent of the system being optimized. Requires a human-reviewed label set and a rule release process.
caveats_en: This is AI applied inside a production system, not a change in how employees work; it's Meta's privacy compliance scenario.

title: Learn from Microsoft: Transform software development through an agentic platform
what_they_do: 微软“Customer Zero”系列首篇，概述微软工程体系的 agent 化：PM 和开发者把安全修复、框架升级等杂务拆成 agent 任务，简单功能拆成 agent 驱动的 PR；从“代码”转向以规格（spec）表达明确意图作为单一事实来源；AI 代码评审覆盖大部分 PR；Azure SRE Agent、Entra SDK 迁移等案例。
numbers: With agents as part of their workflow, 62% of our developers say AI has increased their overall job satisfaction and 88% report increased task throughput.
Over 90% of Microsoft developers now use GitHub Copilot, and our AI code review covers 90% of Microsoft pull requests and speeds completion time by more than 10%.
Reduced time-to-mitigation on security and ops issues with over 50,000 developer hours saved with Azure SRE Agent
Lightspeed modernization compared to previous manual efforts with 80-90% accuracy in migrating hundreds of repos in the Entra SDK migration
Faster time-to-delivery with 55% reduction in manual developer toil using specialized agents and human-AI relationship best practices
denominator_notes: 62%/88% 是开发者自报调查，未给样本量和问卷；“90% PR 有 AI 评审、完成时间加快 10% 以上”未说明对照方式；5 万小时节省、55% 杂务减少未给计算方法与时间范围。
transferable: 可借鉴的组合指标：工具渗透率 + AI 评审覆盖率 + PR 完成时间 + 开发者满意度/吞吐自报。把安全修复、框架升级等“杂务”优先交给 agent 是共识做法。
caveats: 营销系列开篇，数据都是汇总口径，多为自报或估算；微软同时在销售这些产品。
headline: 微软用 Copilot 渗透率、AI 评审覆盖率和开发者自报吞吐做组合指标，但数字多为自报或估算
headline_en: Microsoft combines Copilot penetration, AI review coverage, and developer-reported throughput into a composite metric, but most figures are self-reported or estimated.
what_they_do_en: The first post in Microsoft's "Customer Zero" series gives an overview of agentifying Microsoft's engineering system: PMs and developers break chores like security fixes and framework upgrades into agent tasks, and break simple features into agent-driven PRs; the source of truth shifts from "code" to specs that state intent explicitly; AI code review covers most PRs; cases include Azure SRE Agent and the Entra SDK migration.
denominator_notes_en: 62%/88% are from a developer self-report survey with no sample size or questionnaire given. "90% of PRs get AI review, completion time 10%+ faster" doesn't explain the comparison method. The 50,000 hours saved and 55% chore reduction have no calculation method or time range.
transferable_en: A composite metric to borrow: tool penetration + AI review coverage + PR completion time + self-reported developer satisfaction/throughput. Handing "chores" like security fixes and framework upgrades to agents first is a consensus practice.
caveats_en: The opening post of a marketing series; all data is aggregate and mostly self-reported or estimated; Microsoft also sells these products.

title: Taming our Python dependencies at Microsoft with AI
what_they_do: Python 依赖是微软第三大漏洞面。Microsoft Digital 从黑客松项目做出 VS Code 扩展 Python Dependency Remediation：在开发者工作流内分析依赖链、升级包、并用 AI 自动修改受影响代码，生成变更报告供开发者审阅（无可用模型时只做包升级不改代码）。定位是把“检测到”变成“修掉”，左移进开发流程。
numbers: We estimate that at least 67,000 employees use it every day.
The result is that fixes and upgrades that used to take multiple hours of developer time now take minutes, and the code is much more reliable.
denominator_notes: 67,000 是每天使用 Python 的员工估计数（问题规模），不是工具用户数；“数小时→数分钟”无测量方法和样本。
transferable: 安全债的瓶颈往往不在检测而在修复；把 AI 修复嵌入 IDE、一键生成可审阅的变更，是提高修复率的实用路径。可推广到其他语言的依赖升级。
caveats: 效果数据定性；内部宣传稿。
headline: Microsoft 把 AI 依赖修复嵌进 VS Code，一键升级包并改受影响代码，把安全债从「检测到」推进到「修掉」
headline_en: Microsoft embedded AI dependency remediation in VS Code, upgrading packages and patching affected code in one click, moving security debt from detected to fixed.
what_they_do_en: Python dependencies are Microsoft's third-largest vulnerability surface. Microsoft Digital turned a hackathon project into a VS Code extension, Python Dependency Remediation: inside the developer's workflow it analyzes the dependency chain, upgrades packages, and uses AI to automatically modify affected code, producing a change report for the developer to review (with no model available, it only upgrades packages and doesn't touch code). The goal is to turn "detected" into "fixed" and shift left into the development workflow.
denominator_notes_en: 67,000 is the estimated number of employees who use Python daily (the size of the problem), not the number of tool users; "hours → minutes" has no measurement method or sample.
transferable_en: The bottleneck in security debt is often fixing, not detecting; embedding AI remediation in the IDE and generating reviewable changes in one click is a practical way to raise fix rates. It extends to dependency upgrades in other languages.
caveats_en: Qualitative outcome data; an internal promotional piece.

title: sqlite-utils 4.0rc2, mostly written by Claude Fable (for about $149.25)
what_they_do: Simon 在发布 sqlite-utils 4.0 稳定版前，让 Claude Fable 做「发布前最终评审，专找以后修就会成为破坏性变更的问题」，它报告了 5 个发布阻断问题（包括 delete_where() 不提交并污染连接导致数据丢失）。他在手机上通过 Claude Code for web 逐项处理，先读文档改动来理解变更，最后再让另一家模型（Codex/GPT-5.5 xhigh）复审并又发现两处问题；用 AgentsView 估算会话的非补贴成本。
numbers: Over the course of 37 prompts, 34 commits and +1,321 -190 code changes over 30 separate files, we worked through the entire set of feedback in turn, making several other design improvements along the way.
For an estimated (unsubsidized) cost of $149.25
denominator_notes: 单个开源库的一次大版本发布；成本为 AgentsView 估算的 API 价格。
transferable: 「发布前让 agent 专门找『将来修就是 breaking change』的问题」+「跨厂商模型互审」是可直接加入发布检查清单的步骤；先审文档改动再审代码，是理解大批 agent 改动的有效入口。
