We perform on the order of 25 million code checkouts per day for CI, before counting developer environments, agent sandboxes, and research jobs.
Fetched naively, that would be over 600 PB of git traffic per day.
Each tier of this system maintains a cache hit rate of over 99% and does not require long-lived state, so it’s easy to scale up if needed.
Our Scion infrastructure footprint is now 200x smaller than our previous git mirroring infrastructure in terms of CPU and memory requirements.

CI and research jobs check out code two orders of magnitude faster (in seconds rather than minutes), which frees up a sizable amount of capacity across the fleet; CI alone realized a 25% CPU capacity win.

We asked it to rewrite the whole thing, and with no further instructions, it produced a version that consumed 20x less memory and was 4x faster, while preserving all of the implicit invariants around ingestion ordering and data structures.

A team of seven people built both Scion and Antique (our code review tool, which we could easily write a whole other blog post about), not to mention half a dozen related systems, and fully migrated to them in five months.
We did all this while the volume of code merged per day increased by 10x.
denominator_notes: 合并量为 monorepo 每日合并的 code changes 数（5 月日均 vs 9 月），未区分人写/Claude 写、未给变更平均大小，变更粒度可能随 agent 化变小，所以 12 倍增长不等于 12 倍产出。25M checkouts/天仅指 CI。200x、25% CPU 是相对旧 git 镜像设施的基础设施成本，不是研发效率指标。20x/4x 是单个原型 ingestion pipeline 的个案。「工程师都认为 Claude 写代码比自己强」是团队内自评，无样本数（团队 7 人）。
transferable: 非 lab 组织可提前普查「为人类规模设计」的基础设施（merge queue、CI、checkout、代码评审）在 agent 化后的瓶颈；可直接借鉴的是：按语义分级的评审审批规则（让人只盯高风险改动）、评审重心从逐行读改为审意图、post-merge/pre-deploy 测试替代全局锁、给关键组件配持续盯指标的 agent。前提是已有足够高的 agent 合并量与可靠的自动化测试/回滚能力。
caveats: 厂商自述、无外部审计；文中自己承认 Anthropic 内部 token 预算远超一般企业、只有超大 monorepo 才需要自研 VCS，Scion 本身不建议他人照搬。合并数增长部分来自内部推广新模型，存在为展示能力而写作的动机。
headline: Anthropic 日合并量涨到 3 万后自研源码管理，评审从逐行读代码改为审变更意图
headline_en: After daily merges hit 30,000, Anthropic built its own source control, and review shifted from reading code line by line to checking change intent.
what_they_do_en: Claude-written code drove merge volume up sharply (about 2,500/day in May to 30,000+/day in September), making source control, builds, and CI the biggest bottleneck. A 7-person team spent 5 months building Scion, a version control system designed for "always-on agent clients," and Antique, a code review tool, and moved the monorepo entirely off git. Review changed: humans still review every change request, but they look at the intent of the change rather than reading code line by line, and the review tool can classify changes by semantic sensitivity (e.g., comment-only vs. sensitive logic) so people focus on the critical ones. They dropped the globally locked merge queue in favor of post-merge / pre-deploy automated testing, with Claude fixing concurrent conflicts. For operations, they use Claude Tag in Slack to give each component a "superfan" Claude that watches its telemetry and logs.
denominator_notes_en: Merge volume is the number of code changes merged into the monorepo per day (May daily average vs. September). It does not separate human-written from Claude-written changes or give average change size, and change granularity may have shrunk as work became agent-driven, so 12x growth is not 12x output. 25M checkouts/day refers to CI only. 200x and 25% CPU are infrastructure costs relative to the old git mirror setup, not engineering productivity metrics. 20x/4x is a single prototype ingestion pipeline. "Engineers all think Claude writes better code than they do" is the team's self-assessment with no sample size (the team is 7 people).
transferable_en: Non-lab organizations can audit ahead of time where infrastructure "designed for human scale" (merge queue, CI, checkout, code review) will bottleneck once agents arrive. Directly borrowable: review approval rules tiered by semantic risk (so humans watch only high-risk changes), shifting review from line-by-line reading to checking intent, post-merge/pre-deploy testing instead of a global lock, and agents that continuously watch metrics for critical components. Prerequisites: agent merge volume high enough to matter, and reliable automated testing and rollback.
caveats_en: Vendor self-report with no external audit. The post itself acknowledges that Anthropic's internal token budget far exceeds a typical company's, only very large monorepos need a custom VCS, and Scion is not recommended for others to copy. Part of the merge growth came from internal rollout of new models, and the post has an incentive to showcase capability.

title: Maintaining software with the GPT-6 family
what_they_do: OpenAI Core Experimentation 团队用 Codex 做软件维护：删死代码（模型自己查历史 PR、Slack、项目追踪和生产 profiling 证明代码不可达，并写出删除理由加速评审）、清理过期实验和 feature flag（按 CPU 成本排序，对标记为“Permanent”的 flag 交人工判断）、修 flaky test、优化 CI。评审分发给各相关团队。比较了不同模型/推理档位的成本与发现数，并用差异分析改 prompt 让便宜模型逼近贵模型。文章也承认部分提议“增加的复杂度大于收益”，优先级排序和度量仍是必要环节。
numbers: Once we saw how well Astra was doing, five engineers collaborated to run variations of that prompt across repositories, and we merged more than 1,400 pull requests, deleting over 800k lines of code.
We did the bulk of this part-time over two weeks while primarily working on other projects.
For example, one service’s container image shrank from 3.31GB to 1.72GB, a 48% reduction, and another set of cleanups removed about 400 visual snapshot variants from our test suite.
After review, we removed the flag, with an estimated 0.42% CPU saving in the main affected service.
In this comparison, GPT-6.1 Sol Ultra produced 92% as many findings as GPT-6 Astra Ultra at 14% of the API cost.
We saw median CI completion time fall from roughly 10 minutes to 4.5 minutes, while the 90th percentile fell from 12.5 minutes to 6 minutes.
In a later fix, adding a missing mock cut a 63-test resolver suite’s runtime from 592.6 seconds to 29.8 seconds—a 95% reduction, with all 63 tests retained.
However, some proposals added more complexity than their expected benefit justified, so prioritization and measurement remained an important part of our workflow.
denominator_notes: 1,400+ PR / 80 万行删除是 5 名工程师两周兼职完成；未给出被拒/回滚的 PR 比例。模型对比的“findings”是作者人工核验后的接受数，在约 6,000 文件、100 万行的子目录上测得。CI 时间改善来自约 30 个 CI 优化 PR。
transferable: 维护类工作（死代码、过期 flag、flaky test、CI 提速）是非实验室组织最容易复制的 agent 场景：要求 agent 附证据和删除理由、按团队分发评审、从小范围试点逐步扩大、把评审意见回灌进下一版 prompt、对比不同模型档位的单位发现成本。前提：有生产 profiling/调用数据可供 agent 取证。
caveats: 作者团队成员自述；选取的是成功案例；OpenAI 内部模型成本不同于外部。
headline: OpenAI 五名工程师兼职两周用 Codex 删掉 80 万行死代码，要求 agent 附上不可达证据
headline_en: Five OpenAI engineers, part-time for two weeks, used Codex to delete 800,000 lines of dead code, requiring agents to attach proof of unreachability.
what_they_do_en: OpenAI's Core Experimentation team used Codex for software maintenance: deleting dead code (the model searched past PRs, Slack, project trackers, and production profiling to prove code was unreachable, and wrote a deletion rationale to speed review); cleaning up stale experiments and feature flags (sorted by CPU cost, with flags marked "Permanent" left to human judgment); fixing flaky tests; and optimizing CI. Reviews were routed to the owning teams. They compared cost and findings across models and reasoning levels, and used diff analysis to tune prompts so cheaper models approached the expensive ones. The post also admits some proposals "added more complexity than they were worth," so prioritization and measurement remain necessary.
denominator_notes_en: 1,400+ PRs / 800,000 lines deleted were done by 5 engineers part-time over two weeks; no rate of rejected or reverted PRs is given. "Findings" in the model comparison are counts accepted after the authors' manual verification, measured on a subdirectory of about 6,000 files and 1 million lines. CI time improvements came from about 30 CI optimization PRs.
transferable_en: Maintenance work (dead code, stale flags, flaky tests, faster CI) is the easiest agent use case for non-lab organizations to copy: require agents to attach evidence and a deletion rationale, route reviews by team, start with a small pilot and expand, feed review comments back into the next prompt version, and compare cost per finding across model tiers. Prerequisite: production profiling/call data the agent can use as evidence.
caveats_en: Self-report by members of the authoring team; success cases selected; OpenAI's internal model costs differ from external pricing.

title: How the Claude Code team does code review
what_they_do: Claude Code 团队把代码评审从「末端闸门」变成持续进行的多层检查：提交前让 Claude 运行测试/构建/截图自证，再由新上下文的 subagent 审 diff；每个 PR 由多个 agent 并行找 bug、另一组 agent 投票确认才发评论（风格类过滤掉），每条发现必须修复或附理由关闭；安全审查可阻断合并；人工审批按风险分层（低风险自动检查全绿后无需人批、中风险 1 人、高风险 2 人），风险等级由分类器按变更而非作者判定，只有受信作者能走轻量路径，bot 批准不能替代人，新提交使批准失效，指挥 agent 的人计为必需评审人之一。改进 reviewer 的方法：用历史事故/回滚 PR 建 eval 每日跑，按作者对评论的处置统计噪声，限制评审轮数（3 轮后让作者重新考虑方案、后续只审增量 diff）。知识共享改为让 Claude 按需生成模块讲解；团队规范「你合进去的你负责修」。
numbers: We've said before that Claude writes about 90 percent of Claude Code's own code.
From June to September, merged pull requests to Claude Code's codebase more than doubled while the share that had to be reverted fell by more than 40 percent.
In Anthropic's monorepo, changes landing per day went from about 2,500 in May to more than 30,000 in September this year.

He estimates it makes the final result two to three times better, and writes, "Verification looks different for each domain. It might be as simple as running a bash command, or running a test suite, or testing the app in a browser or phone simulator."
When we launched the research preview, the share of internal PRs getting substantive review comments went from 16% to 54%.
One CLI PR went through more than fifty rounds of review and fixes overnight before its author stopped it.
When we ran git blame on what the reviewer kept flagging, about 59% of it was code that had been there since the reviewer's first pass.
After three rounds, the reviewer asks the author to step back and reconsider the approach.
denominator_notes: 「约 90%」指 Claude Code 自身代码由 Claude 编写，未定义口径（行/PR）。「合并 PR 翻倍、回滚占比降 40%+」是 Claude Code 仓库 6–9 月的对比，回滚率是比例而非绝对数，期间同时存在其他变化（模型升级等），不能完全归因于评审流程。16%→54% 是「收到实质评论的 PR 比例」，衡量的是评论覆盖而非真实缺陷检出。59% 是重复轮次中被标记代码早已存在的比例，用来说明多轮评审收益递减。人类时间指标（每 PR 审批数中位数/P95、等待时长）只给了定义未给数值。
transferable: 几乎可整体迁移（文中也给了落地清单）：PR 模板加 Testing/Risk/How to revert；先在一个仓库上 AI reviewer 并调 REVIEW.md 再推广；评审线程全部解决才可合并；风险分层写成文档、由变更决定等级、从严开始凭证据放宽；CODEOWNERS 保护 auth/billing/CI/安装器；bot 批准不替代人；新提交使批准失效；用事故/回滚建 reviewer eval；以人类时间为目标、以回滚/事故率为护栏；限制评审轮数。前提是有快速回滚（feature flag、分阶段发布）和足够的 CI。
caveats: 产品团队自述，同时推广 Code Review 产品；Claude Code 团队是最早期、最熟练的用户且其代码就是 agent 工具本身，内部员工先用（dogfooding）能提前暴露回归，一般企业不具备同等条件；文中承认还没有根据回滚/事故指标自动收紧审批的熔断机制。
headline: Claude Code 团队把评审拆成提交前自证、多 agent 找 bug 和按变更风险分级的人工审批
headline_en: The Claude Code team splits review into pre-submit self-verification, multi-agent bug hunting, and human approval tiered by change risk.
what_they_do_en: The Claude Code team turned code review from an end-of-line gate into continuous layered checks. Before submitting, Claude runs tests/builds/screenshots to verify its own work, then a subagent with fresh context reviews the diff. On every PR, several agents hunt for bugs in parallel and another set votes to confirm before a comment is posted (style nits are filtered out); every finding must be fixed or closed with a reason. Security review can block a merge. Human approval is risk-tiered: low risk needs no human once automated checks are green, medium needs 1 person, high needs 2. A classifier assigns risk based on the change, not the author; only trusted authors get the lightweight path; bot approval cannot replace a human; new commits invalidate approvals; and the person directing the agent counts as one of the required reviewers. Improving the reviewer: build an eval from past incidents/reverted PRs and run it daily, measure noise by how authors dispose of comments, and cap review rounds (after 3 rounds the author reconsiders the approach, and later rounds review only the incremental diff). Knowledge sharing now means having Claude generate module walkthroughs on demand. Team norm: "you merged it, you fix it."
denominator_notes_en: "About 90%" means Claude Code's own code is written by Claude, with no defined basis (lines or PRs). "Merged PRs doubled, revert share down 40%+" compares the Claude Code repo from June to September; revert rate is a proportion, not an absolute count, and other changes (model upgrades, etc.) happened in the same period, so it cannot be fully attributed to the review process. 16% to 54% is "share of PRs receiving substantive comments," which measures comment coverage, not actual defect detection. 59% is the share of flagged code in repeat rounds that already existed, used to show diminishing returns from multiple rounds. Human-time metrics (median/P95 approvals per PR, wait time) are defined but no values are given.
transferable_en: Almost entirely transferable (the post includes a rollout checklist): add Testing/Risk/How to revert to the PR template; pilot an AI reviewer on one repo and tune REVIEW.md before expanding; require all review threads resolved before merge; document risk tiers, let the change determine the tier, start strict and relax on evidence; protect auth/billing/CI/installer with CODEOWNERS; bot approval does not replace a human; new commits invalidate approvals; build a reviewer eval from incidents/reverts; target human time and use revert/incident rate as guardrails; cap review rounds. Prerequisites: fast rollback (feature flags, staged rollout) and sufficient CI.
caveats_en: Product team self-report that also promotes the Code Review product. The Claude Code team is the earliest and most skilled user, its code is the agent tool itself, and employee dogfooding surfaces regressions early; typical companies lack these conditions. The post admits there is not yet a circuit breaker that automatically tightens approval based on revert/incident metrics.

title: How Meta Built Forum With AI-Native Engineering
what_they_do: Meta 一个小团队从零开发新应用 Forum，把 agent 当作工程流程参与者：成功标准不是代码量，而是“能构建、过测试、过评审”的可验证产出；从 human-in-the-loop 向 human-on-the-loop 推进（agent 自己跑计划-实现-构建-测试-修正循环，工程师设目标、盯运行、批结果）。配套：把规划写成机器可读规格；把构建状态、单测、UI 规格比对接进 agent 循环，PR 附测试计划和录屏验证；用导航 agent 模拟真人操作做回归和压力测试（发现并修复内存问题）；上线后 agent 根据用户反馈做根因分析。运行机制由 rules（同一错误重复两次以上就写成规则）、skills、agents、commands、hooks 组成；最大收益来自改代码与工具而非改 prompt（给 agent 查询界面状态的工具而非描述）；用独立的 sandbox 构建变体让设计师等非工程师用 AI 原型而不污染生产包。失败教训：跨会话丢上下文、“通过的 PR 仍在偷工减料”、远程 iOS 模拟器不稳定。
numbers: Velocity: Forum reached core feature parity with Facebook Groups in eight weeks, with AI handling much of the routine implementation so engineers could focus on architecture, product decisions, and quality.
Quality, found early: The autonomous stress-testing loop caught and fixed the aforementioned memory issue during development rather than post-launch, roughly halving memory use and page faults.
denominator_notes: 8 周达到与 Facebook Groups 核心功能对等，未给出团队人数或对照项目；内存“约减半”是压力测试场景下的结果。“What Worked / What Did Not”两张表是图片，内容已人工阅读。
transferable: 对 TLM 最可操作的一篇：(1) 用“可验证产出”而不是代码量定义成功；(2) 投资验证器（构建、测试、UI 比对、录屏）——没有自动化“完成”信号就只是“人在看着生成器”；(3) 重复两次的错误写成规则；(4) 新代码库/模块化架构更适合 agent；(5) 质量信号必须严格到能抓住“通过但偷工”的 PR。前提：能接受为 agent 可读性重构代码。
caveats: 全新代码库、小团队、内部新产品，条件有利；无缺陷率、评审时长等数据。
headline: Meta Forum 团队以「能构建、过测试、过评审」定义完成，并把犯过两次的错写成 agent 规则
headline_en: Meta's Forum team defines done as "builds, passes tests, passes review," and turns any mistake made twice into an agent rule.
what_they_do_en: A small Meta team built a new app, Forum, from scratch and treated agents as participants in the engineering process. Success was measured not by code volume but by verifiable output: "builds, passes tests, passes review." They moved from human-in-the-loop toward human-on-the-loop (the agent runs its own plan-implement-build-test-fix loop; engineers set goals, watch runs, and approve results). Supporting pieces: planning written as machine-readable specs; build status, unit tests, and UI spec comparison wired into the agent loop, with PRs carrying a test plan and screen-recording verification; a navigation agent that simulates real users for regression and stress testing (it found a memory issue that was then fixed); after launch, agents do root-cause analysis on user feedback. The operating mechanism consists of rules (any mistake repeated more than twice becomes a rule), skills, agents, commands, and hooks. The biggest gains came from changing code and tools rather than prompts (give the agent a tool to query UI state instead of a description). A separate sandbox build variant lets designers and other non-engineers prototype with AI without polluting the production bundle. Failures: context lost across sessions, "PRs that pass but still cut corners," and unstable remote iOS simulators.
denominator_notes_en: Reached parity with Facebook Groups core features in 8 weeks; no team size or comparison project given. Memory "roughly halved" is a stress-test result. The "What Worked / What Did Not" tables are images and were read manually.
transferable_en: The most actionable piece for a TLM: (1) define success by verifiable output, not code volume; (2) invest in verifiers (builds, tests, UI comparison, screen recordings), because without an automated "done" signal you are just "a human watching a generator"; (3) turn any mistake repeated twice into a rule; (4) new codebases and modular architectures suit agents better; (5) quality signals must be strict enough to catch PRs that "pass but cut corners." Prerequisite: willingness to refactor code for agent readability.
caveats_en: Greenfield codebase, small team, new internal product: favorable conditions. No defect rate, review time, or similar data.

title: Automating engineering operations at Microsoft with a Smart DRI Agent
what_they_do: Microsoft Digital 与 HR 工程团队从黑客松起步，做了给值班负责人（DRI）用的 Smart DRI Agent：事故进来时自动汇总遥测（日志、trace、异常）、匹配排障指南、检索相似历史事故（Azure AI Search + 自定义相似度逻辑），在 Teams 里给出排查建议，并主动推送早间摘要；把各团队差异做成可配置模板。团队强调没有强的 live site 文化，这个 agent 就没用；下一步才考虑让 agent 执行缓解（需 DRI 签字）。
numbers: The tool, called Smart DRI Agent, now supports over 40 teams at Microsoft, delivering more than 7,800 AI-assisted interactions and nearly 6,000 proactive incident notifications. This has saved the company an estimated 600 engineering hours per month, with bigger gains projected in the future.
denominator_notes: 每月 600 工程小时是估算，方法未说明；7,800 次交互、近 6,000 次通知的统计期未说明。
transferable: 值班助手是低风险高回报的起点：先只读汇总上下文和相似事故，再考虑执行动作；团队差异用模板/配置而非硬编码；检索效果要用真实事故验证。前提：有排障指南和事故历史可索引。
caveats: 内部宣传稿，节省时间为估算；无 MTTR 前后对比。
headline: Microsoft 的 Smart DRI 值班助手先只读汇总遥测和相似历史事故，执行缓解要 DRI 签字，且没有 live site 文化就用不起来
headline_en: Microsoft's Smart DRI on-call assistant starts read-only, summarizing telemetry and similar past incidents; mitigation needs DRI sign-off, and it fails without live-site culture.
what_they_do_en: Starting from a hackathon, Microsoft Digital and HR engineering teams built the Smart DRI Agent for on-call owners (DRIs). When an incident comes in, it automatically summarizes telemetry (logs, traces, exceptions), matches troubleshooting guides, retrieves similar past incidents (Azure AI Search plus custom similarity logic), offers investigation suggestions in Teams, and proactively pushes a morning digest. Team-specific differences are handled with configurable templates. The team stresses that without a strong live-site culture the agent is useless; only as a next step are they considering letting the agent execute mitigations (with DRI sign-off).
denominator_notes_en: 600 engineering hours per month is an estimate with no stated method; the measurement period for 7,800 interactions and nearly 6,000 notifications is not stated.
transferable_en: An on-call assistant is a low-risk, high-return starting point: begin read-only with context summaries and similar incidents, and only then consider executing actions. Handle team differences through templates/config rather than hard-coding. Validate retrieval quality against real incidents. Prerequisite: troubleshooting guides and incident history that can be indexed.
caveats_en: Internal promotional piece; time savings are estimates; no before/after MTTR comparison.

title: How an Anthropic BDR in Japan runs his day with Claude Managed Agents
what_they_do: Anthropic 日本 BDR 把日常工作拆成 5 个单一职责的定时 agent（线索分配、线索分级+CRM 更新+首封邮件、每小时回信草稿、商机记录更新、会后纪要与跟进）外加 1 个 coordinator，在 Managed Agents 上运行：共享一个 memory store，agent 比对自己的草稿与他实际发出的邮件并把差异记为写作笔记；凭证放托管 vault、按 agent 最小授权；只有他本人能在专用 Slack 频道提交改指令请求，由 coordinator 每约 15 分钟执行且每次改动有版本。需要后续动作的事项交给 Claude Tag 跟进并设置提醒；按判断难度给不同 agent 配 Sonnet/Opus 与 effort，高频回信 agent 用 Sonnet + Opus advisor 控成本。
numbers: Looking at the weekly log of what the Nakama gets through and counting each task as the time it would have taken me to do manually, the fleet saves me around 60 hours of work.
It took a few hundred cheap rounds of drafting, fixing, and saving to get the drafts to sound like me.
denominator_notes: 「约 60 小时」按「每项任务若手工需要的时间」累计估算（文中未明确是每周还是累计，表述为 weekly log），属于理论节省而非实测工时变化。
transferable: 可借鉴的 agent 运维设计：一个 agent 一个职责、按需定时运行；共享记忆存储让一次纠正全队生效；凭证集中托管+按职责授权+一键撤销；只有 owner 能改指令、改动有版本、试验改动不影响已部署版本；按任务判断难度分配模型与 effort。前提是有托管 agent 平台或同等的调度/版本/密钥管理设施。
caveats: 员工自述+产品推广（Managed Agents/Claude Tag 均为 beta）；节省时间为估算；单人个案，未报告错误或客户投诉情况。
headline: Anthropic 日本 BDR 把日常工作拆给 5 个单职责 agent，共享记忆、凭证最小授权、指令改动有版本
headline_en: An Anthropic Japan BDR split his daily work across 5 single-purpose agents with shared memory, least-privilege credentials, and versioned instruction changes.
what_they_do_en: An Anthropic Japan BDR split his daily work into 5 single-purpose scheduled agents (lead assignment; lead scoring + CRM update + first email; hourly reply drafts; opportunity record updates; post-meeting notes and follow-up) plus 1 coordinator, running on Managed Agents. They share a memory store, and agents compare their drafts against the emails he actually sent and record the differences as writing notes. Credentials live in a managed vault with least-privilege access per agent. Only he can submit instruction-change requests, in a dedicated Slack channel; the coordinator applies them roughly every 15 minutes and every change is versioned. Items needing follow-up are handed to Claude Tag with reminders. Agents get Sonnet or Opus and an effort level according to how hard their judgment calls are; the high-frequency reply agent uses Sonnet with an Opus advisor to control cost.
denominator_notes_en: "About 60 hours" is summed from "how long each task would have taken by hand" (the post does not say whether this is weekly or cumulative; it is described as a weekly log). It is theoretical savings, not a measured change in hours worked.
transferable_en: Borrowable agent-ops design: one agent per responsibility, scheduled as needed; a shared memory store so one correction applies to the whole team; centrally managed credentials with per-role access and one-click revocation; only the owner can change instructions, changes are versioned, and experimental changes do not affect the deployed version; assign model and effort by how hard the task's judgment is. Prerequisite: a managed agent platform or equivalent scheduling/versioning/secret management.
caveats_en: Employee self-report plus product promotion (Managed Agents and Claude Tag are both beta). Time savings are estimates. A single-person case with no reporting on errors or customer complaints.

title: How employment is changing at Anthropic
what_they_do: Anthropic 经济学团队用内部雇佣、AI 使用遥测、产出指标、员工调查、日历、Slack 网络和招聘评分卡数据（加 17 个访谈）研究公司内部工作的变化：初级技术岗占比和招聘明显下降，经理也在写代码，工程师:PM 约 17:1；非技术员工大量用编码 agent 自建工具，行政岗未随规模扩张；部门间内部流动增加，整团队被重新部署（如产品文案团队转做 agent prompt 和 eval）。生产率：工程师采用编码 agent 后代码量显著上升（交错采用、个人固定效应），同人同月同目录的 agent 代码与人写代码在删除/回滚率上无差异；销售、法务、应付账款产出也上升。瓶颈变成人的注意力：交互会话约 80% 时间在等人，「元工作」（写 spec、让 agent 互审、监控管道）占比翻倍，会议时间反而增加；人的决策需要留在 agent 可见的公开渠道。招聘更看重自主性、判断力与创造性使用 AI，而非领域专长；公司建立了岗位受冲击预警系统并优先内部再部署。
numbers: By August interactive AI agent hours outnumbered employees’ six to one.
It contextualizes these quantitative data with 17 employee interviews.
At five years old, Anthropic takes in between 2–4 times as much revenue per employee as Meta and Google as they crested in their own rapid growth.
Around a third of ML and a fifth of SWE managers reported hiring less due to AI.
Figure 1 shows that the share of junior-level employees in technical departments at Anthropic slipped from 21% to 14% since early 2025.
The proportion of junior technical hires fell even faster, from 27% to 9%.
At the same time, the overall employment share of technical departments within Anthropic has fallen, from 61% to 56% in the last year.
Coding-focused AI agent sessions for non-technical employees (identified as those with no code commits at baseline, excluding new hires) leapt from 2 per month in August 2025 to 90 in May 2026.
Part of this is due to a thinning share of non-engineers: the ratio of engineers to product managers, for example, sits at around 17 to 1 and has increased since 2025.
The number of commits from managers has also doubled.
These changes have already involved reallocation: employees working at the company for at least a year were 50% more likely to move across departments each month in 2026 than they were in 2025.
Based on agent session telemetry, in March 2026, the sum of autonomous and interactive agent work hours leapt past human work hours for the first time.

Consistent with prior reports surveying Anthropic engineers and describing automation of model training and research, code commits per engineer have risen the fastest, coming in at 5x their velocity as six months ago.
We follow 192 engineers over time as they adopt coding agents, compared to 74 engineers who do not adopt agents during the period studied.
But we find no difference in rates of lines of code subsequently removed or reverted.
One account executive explained that Claude automations handled email drafting and customer management software integrations, replacing around 20% of their prior work tasks.

An internal employee survey asked whether work processes at Anthropic made respondents as productive as possible: 44% of employees agreed in late 2024; 58% by November 2025 (in April 2026, 75% answered yes, but the question weakened by dropping “as possible”).
As of August, employees at Anthropic expected that AI will be able to do 75% of their work by 2030, compared to 28% for other Americans.
The share of tasks above the 90th percentile of difficulty for the old model rises sharply by around 30% (from 10% to 13% of all tasks) and stays elevated in the weeks following model releases.

In the April 2026 survey, an open-ended question about how AI has impacted day-to-day work, 27% described productivity gains from Claude tools and 20% described their role shifting from actually doing work to managing Claudes.
Claude sessions amount to around 80% idly waiting for human input.
Written standing instructions for agents grew from a few hundred in July 2025 to 8,500 a year later.
Figure 7 shows that this kind of meta-work leapt from 10% of the average employee’s interactive Claude sessions in fall 2025 to 22% in spring 2026.
Based on calendar data, the median employee spends 20% more time in meetings than a year ago.
But even among employees in technical individual contributor roles, meeting time is up 16% over the past year.
In 2024, hiring managers noted candidates' track record on AI tooling in around 5% of assessments for technical roles, and 7% for non-technical roles.
denominator_notes: agent 小时 6:1 只计员工发起的交互会话（含 subagent），agent 时间=运行时（推理+工具，剔除>30 分钟等待），人类时间按人头×40 小时/周估算，二者口径不同。初级占比 21%→14%、初级招聘 27%→9% 的时间起点为 2025 年初，未给绝对人数。「5x 提交速度」相对 6 个月前，提交数不等于产出价值。192 vs 74 工程师对比为非随机采用（文中承认选择偏差，且转向全自主 agent 的人此前已在上升轨道）。质量代理指标（90 天内删除、bug-fix 删除、回滚、lint 抑制等）只覆盖可观测维度。调查题目措辞在 2026 年 4 月变化，44%/58%/75% 不完全可比。会议时间增加部分源于公司扩张与非技术岗增长。招聘评分卡比例来自自动编码器分析。
transferable: 可借鉴的组织做法：用遥测量化「agent 小时/人类小时」「元工作占比」「会话等人时间」来发现人类注意力瓶颈；把决策和讨论放到 agent 可见的公开渠道；招聘标准转向自主性、判断力与 AI 使用记录；建立岗位受冲击的早期预警指标并优先内部再部署；用交错采用+个人固定效应评估工具效果，同时检查回滚/删除率等质量代理。前提是有统一身份的 agent 会话遥测和 HR/产出数据打通，并重视隐私。
caveats: 作者为 Anthropic 员工（Anthropic Institute），研究对象是自己公司；营收高增长、股权激励普遍、内部 token 预算极高等条件不可复制（文中自己指出）；初级岗位收缩的社会影响结论需谨慎外推。
headline: Anthropic 内部数据显示，agent 普及后瓶颈变成人的注意力，初级技术招聘占比从 27% 降到 9%
headline_en: Anthropic's internal data shows that as agents spread, human attention became the bottleneck, and junior technical hires fell from 27% to 9%.
what_they_do_en: Anthropic's economics team studied how work inside the company has changed, using internal employment data, AI usage telemetry, output metrics, employee surveys, calendars, Slack network data, and hiring scorecards (plus 17 interviews). Findings: the share of junior technical roles and junior hiring fell noticeably; managers are also writing code; the engineer:PM ratio is about 17:1; non-technical staff build their own tools with coding agents in large numbers, and administrative headcount did not grow with company size; internal moves between departments increased, and whole teams were redeployed (e.g., the product copy team moved to agent prompts and evals). Productivity: engineers' code volume rose significantly after adopting coding agents (staggered adoption, individual fixed effects), and agent-written vs. human-written code by the same person, in the same month, in the same directory showed no difference in deletion/revert rates; output also rose in sales, legal, and accounts payable. Human attention became the bottleneck: about 80% of interactive session time is spent waiting on a human, the share of "meta-work" (writing specs, having agents review each other, monitoring pipelines) doubled, and meeting time actually increased; human decisions need to stay in public channels agents can see. Hiring now weights autonomy, judgment, and creative use of AI over domain expertise. The company built an early-warning system for roles under pressure and prioritizes internal redeployment.
denominator_notes_en: The 6:1 agent-hours figure counts only employee-initiated interactive sessions (including subagents). Agent time = runtime (inference + tools, excluding waits >30 minutes); human time is estimated as headcount x 40 hours/week, so the two bases differ. Junior share 21% to 14% and junior hiring 27% to 9% start from early 2025, with no absolute headcounts. "5x commit velocity" is relative to 6 months earlier, and commit count is not output value. The 192 vs. 74 engineer comparison reflects non-random adoption (the post acknowledges selection bias, and those who moved to fully autonomous agents were already on an upward trajectory). Quality proxies (deleted within 90 days, bug-fix deletions, reverts, lint suppressions, etc.) cover only observable dimensions. Survey wording changed in April 2026, so 44%/58%/75% are not fully comparable. Part of the increase in meeting time comes from company growth and more non-technical roles. Hiring scorecard proportions come from autoencoder analysis.
transferable_en: Borrowable organizational practices: use telemetry to quantify "agent hours / human hours," "meta-work share," and "session time waiting on a human" to find human-attention bottlenecks; keep decisions and discussion in public channels agents can see; shift hiring criteria toward autonomy, judgment, and a track record of AI use; build early-warning indicators for roles under pressure and prioritize internal redeployment; evaluate tools with staggered adoption plus individual fixed effects while checking quality proxies like revert/deletion rates. Prerequisites: agent session telemetry tied to a unified identity and joined with HR/output data, with serious attention to privacy.
caveats_en: Authors are Anthropic employees (Anthropic Institute) studying their own company. Conditions such as rapid revenue growth, widespread equity compensation, and very high internal token budgets are not replicable (the post says so itself). Be cautious extrapolating conclusions about the social impact of shrinking junior roles.

title: The AI expectations gap
what_they_do: Anthropic 在 2026 年 8 月对 1,334 名员工做内部问卷，并与 Morning Consult 的近 1.1 万名美国成年人样本对比 AI 能力、扩散、自主程度、省时幅度与就业预期。内部部分给出员工自报的省时幅度（59% 认为适合 AI 的任务只需四分之一或更少时间）、对自己工作被 AI 覆盖比例的预期，以及员工估计「构建前沿模型的工作中由 AI 完成的比例」（中位数今天 51%）。结论是两组人对「AI 如何影响就业」的推理模型相似，差异主要来自对 AI 能力的亲身体验不同。
numbers: Among US adults who use AI at work, 26% say a task takes a quarter of the time or less with AI, compared to 59% of Anthropic staff.
When it comes to their own job, over half of Anthropic staff expect AI to be able to do at least 80% of their current work by 2030, compared with 5% of US workers.
Anthropic staff report much larger expected savings, with 85% saying that it takes half the time or less.
Among US adults who use AI at work, the typical answer is half the time, and 29% say the task takes just as long or longer, while only 5% of staff say so.

As discussed further in How Employment is Changing at Anthropic, Anthropic employees increased productivity on some dimensions after adopting agentic tools: the lines of code engineers added tripled in the month after adopting coding agents and sales representatives closed more deals with clients after adopting AI agents.
Among surveyed Anthropic staff, the median answer today is 51%, 80% by the end of 2027 and 95% by the end of 2030.
Still, staff on research teams, who are closest to the work of building models, put AI's share today somewhat higher: 60% on average, against 53% for all other survey respondents.
The staff survey was an internal poll that ran from August 9 to 12 and drew 1,334 respondents from every part of the company.

Favaro and Clark (2026) report that more than 80% of the code merged into Anthropic's codebase is now written by Claude, but building a frontier model also involves research direction, experiment design and evaluation, and more.
denominator_notes: 员工样本 1,334 人、未加权、自愿作答（2026-08-09 至 08-12）；省时问题是「对一个适合 AI 的任务，算上检查和修改时间，用 AI 要多久」，为自报感知而非测量；「AI 完成模型构建工作的比例」是个人估计，文中明确声明不是公司测量或预测。
transferable: 可借鉴的是调查设计：在组织内用同一套题测量员工自报的省时幅度（明确包含检查/修复时间）与对自身岗位暴露度的预期，并与外部基准对比，用来识别「使用深度」差异；但不应把自报省时当生产率证据。
caveats: lab 员工高度自选择、对 AI 极度乐观且持有公司股权，结论不能代表一般企业员工；多数为预测类问题，对「现在怎么做」的实践信息有限。
headline: Anthropic 员工自报省时远高于美国职场人（59% 对 26%），但这是感知，不是生产率
headline_en: Anthropic employees report far larger time savings than US workers (59% vs. 26%), but this is perception, not productivity.
what_they_do_en: In August 2026 Anthropic surveyed 1,334 employees and compared them with a Morning Consult sample of nearly 11,000 US adults on AI capability, diffusion, autonomy, time savings, and employment expectations. The internal portion reports employees' self-reported time savings (59% say AI-suitable tasks take a quarter of the time or less), their expectations for how much of their own work AI will cover, and their estimate of "the share of work on building frontier models done by AI" (median 51% today). The conclusion: both groups reason about "how AI affects jobs" in similar ways; the gap comes mainly from different firsthand experience of AI capability.
denominator_notes_en: Employee sample of 1,334, unweighted, voluntary (2026-08-09 to 08-12). The time-savings question asks "for an AI-suitable task, including time to check and revise, how long does it take with AI," so it is self-reported perception, not measurement. "Share of model-building work done by AI" is a personal estimate, and the post states explicitly that it is not a company measurement or forecast.
transferable_en: The survey design is what's borrowable: inside your organization, use the same questions to measure self-reported time savings (explicitly including checking/fixing time) and expectations of exposure for one's own role, and compare against an external benchmark to spot differences in depth of use. But do not treat self-reported time savings as productivity evidence.
caveats_en: Lab employees are heavily self-selected, extremely optimistic about AI, and hold company equity, so the results do not represent typical company employees. Most questions are forward-looking, offering little practical information on "how to do it now."

title: The Thin Orchestrator: How We Made Our AI Agents More Reliable by Giving the Router Less to Do
what_they_do: Meta 用 agent 自动化推荐系统数据列接入（跨 3 个代码库、3 种语言、最多 6 个流水线阶段）。最初的“全知单 agent”在演示中可用、上线后幻觉、跨子系统串用规则；改为“薄编排器”：1,300 行确定性路由代码不做任何领域推理，只做意图分类、收集字段、可靠性检查和派发，14 个领域专家子 agent 各自隔离上下文；用工作流模板（状态机）复用同一组子 agent 支持新场景；知识文件运行时按需加载。
numbers: We built a 1,300-line orchestrator that routes 20+ workflows to 14 specialized AI agents.
Its success rate was 70-80% with manual prompt engineering per task: An engineer had to craft a custom system prompt for each specific job. Without that handholding, success dropped to 10-20%.
Configuration prep for a new column took three to four days by hand and about a day with our earlier config-driven system. The thin orchestrator system does it in under an hour.
For broader context: About two-thirds of the system’s changes land without significant human edits.
denominator_notes: 70–80% vs 10–20% 是另一种单 agent 方案在有/无逐任务定制 prompt 时的成功率；“约三分之二无需大幅人工修改即落地”未定义“大幅”，也未给出总变更数。
transferable: 企业内部 agent 的架构建议：路由/流程控制用确定性代码，领域推理交给上下文隔离的专家子 agent，新场景优先写新的工作流模板而不是新 agent，知识文件运行时加载便于即时更新。适用于跨多仓库、多步骤的工程自动化。
caveats: 单一领域（数据管道配置）经验；引用的外部预印本数据不是 Meta 的。
headline: Meta 用 1,300 行确定性路由代码加 14 个上下文隔离的专家子 agent，替换上线后幻觉的全知单 agent
headline_en: Meta replaced an all-knowing single agent that hallucinated in production with 1,300 lines of deterministic routing code and 14 context-isolated specialist subagents.
what_they_do_en: Meta uses agents to automate onboarding data columns into recommendation systems (across 3 codebases, 3 languages, up to 6 pipeline stages). The original "all-knowing single agent" worked in demos but hallucinated in production and applied rules from one subsystem to another. They switched to a "thin orchestrator": 1,300 lines of deterministic routing code that does no domain reasoning, only intent classification, field collection, reliability checks, and dispatch, with 14 domain-specialist subagents each in isolated context. Workflow templates (state machines) reuse the same set of subagents for new scenarios, and knowledge files are loaded on demand at runtime.
denominator_notes_en: 70-80% vs. 10-20% is the success rate of a different single-agent approach with and without per-task custom prompts. "About two-thirds landed without significant human modification" does not define "significant" or give total change count.
transferable_en: Architecture advice for internal enterprise agents: use deterministic code for routing and flow control, hand domain reasoning to context-isolated specialist subagents, write a new workflow template for a new scenario before writing a new agent, and load knowledge files at runtime so they can be updated immediately. Fits multi-repo, multi-step engineering automation.
caveats_en: Experience from a single domain (data pipeline configuration); the cited external preprint data is not Meta's.

title: How we built ChatGPT’s novel ad stack for user trust and relevance
what_they_do: 主体是广告系统架构；与内部实践相关的只有结尾一段：一年前只有几个人在想这件事，团队和开发流程从一开始就围绕 Codex 搭建，为 Codex 建了安全交付代码的护栏，并给 Codex 接了数据基础设施插件，缩短“洞察→改进落地”的循环。
numbers: A year ago, we had no ads system and only a few people thinking about this problem space.
denominator_notes: 没有给出团队规模、Codex 代码占比或护栏的具体形式；营收数字是业务指标，与工程实践无直接关系，未列入。
transferable: 可借鉴“新团队从第一天按 agent-first 设计开发流程 + 给 agent 接数据平台插件做分析闭环”的做法；但文章细节不足，只能作为方向性佐证。
caveats: 一段话的定性描述，无数据；产品宣传文章。
headline: OpenAI 广告团队从第一天就围绕 Codex 设计开发流程，并给 agent 接上数据平台插件
headline_en: OpenAI's ads team designed its development process around Codex from day one and connected agents to data platform plugins.
what_they_do_en: The post is mostly about ads system architecture; only the closing paragraph concerns internal practice: a year ago only a few people were thinking about this, the team and its development process were built around Codex from the start, they built guardrails for Codex to ship code safely, and they connected Codex to data infrastructure plugins to shorten the loop from insight to shipped improvement.
denominator_notes_en: No team size, Codex share of code, or specifics on the guardrails. Revenue figures are business metrics unrelated to engineering practice and are not included.
transferable_en: Borrowable: "design a new team's development process agent-first from day one, and connect agents to data platform plugins to close the analysis loop." But the post lacks detail and is only directional evidence.
caveats_en: One paragraph of qualitative description, no data; product promotion piece.

org: The PHP Foundation / PHP security team
title: Today's PHP Security Release, and How We're Strengthening PHP Security
what_they_do: PHP 基金会复盘两个严重 RCE：根因早在 2024 年审计中已露头，但安全团队以共识制决策、修复方案各有权衡而反复停滞，原文称之为「结构性失败」；直到 AI 辅助的外部审计（Calif、OpenAI、Wiz 等）给出完整利用链才成为最高优先级。组织层面：新建生态安全团队、设「AI 安全驻场工程师」、引入 AI 模型扫描与报告验证工具、搭与 CI 一致的复现环境；AI 用于验证报告和按根因归并，但每个决定和补丁都由人负责；决策机制改为多数决并鼓励折中。
numbers: As Alexandre Daubois described last week in How the PHP Security Team Handles Your Reports, the team has published 15 CVEs since July 1st and worked through more than 100 reports that turned out to be invalid, duplicates, or not reproducible.
denominator_notes: 15 个 CVE 与 100+ 无效/重复报告的时间窗为 2026-07-01 起。
transferable: AI 让漏洞/缺陷报告量暴增后，瓶颈变成「决策与修复」而非「发现」：组织需要为报告建立 AI 辅助的验证、去重、复现流水线，同时调整决策机制（避免共识制卡死）和升级路径，让卡在权衡上的严重问题尽快到达有权拍板的人。
caveats: 开源基金会视角，结尾为募资呼吁；AI 报告量的增长幅度未给出前后对比数字。 HN 上 1,561 分的帖子链接的是 php.net 安全公告（https://www.php.net/archive/2026.php#2026-10-21-5），本条为 Simon 链接的基金会复盘文章。
headline: PHP 基金会复盘两个严重 RCE：根因早被发现却卡在共识制决策，AI 让发现变容易后，瓶颈在拍板与修复
headline_en: PHP Foundation postmortem on two critical RCEs: root causes surfaced early but stalled under consensus decisions; with AI-driven discovery, deciding and fixing is the bottleneck.
what_they_do_en: The PHP Foundation reviewed two critical RCEs. The root cause had already surfaced in a 2024 audit, but the security team decided by consensus and each fix involved trade-offs, so work stalled repeatedly; the source calls this a "structural failure." It only became top priority when AI-assisted external audits (Calif, OpenAI, Wiz, and others) produced complete exploit chains. Organizational changes: a new ecosystem security team, an "AI security engineer in residence," AI model scanning and report validation tools, and a reproduction environment that matches CI. AI is used to validate reports and group them by root cause, but a human owns every decision and patch. Decision-making moved to majority vote, with compromise encouraged.
denominator_notes_en: The time window for 15 CVEs and 100+ invalid/duplicate reports starts 2026-07-01.
transferable_en: Once AI makes vulnerability/defect reports surge, the bottleneck becomes deciding and fixing, not finding. Organizations need an AI-assisted pipeline to validate, dedupe, and reproduce reports, and must also adjust decision-making (avoid consensus deadlock) and escalation paths so serious issues stuck on trade-offs reach someone with authority to decide quickly.
caveats_en: Open-source foundation perspective, ending with a fundraising appeal; no before/after figures for the growth in AI reports. The 1,561-point HN post linked to the php.net security advisory (https://www.php.net/archive/2026.php#2026-10-21-5); this entry covers the foundation postmortem Simon linked.

title: What FDE means at OpenAI
what_they_do: OpenAI 前线部署工程（FDE）团队负责人讲团队运作：以“先拿到结果、再规模化”为原则，FDE 不要求行业背景但必须自学（如嵌入芯片验证团队）；Codex 能力上来后，把各项目的定制应用改为基于 Codex 通用 harness 的 plugin/skill，删掉约 90% 定制代码，第二个团队接入从两个月缩到一天；模型做不到的场景就和 Research 一起定义能力差距。团队自我定位是“每隔几个月让自己过时”。
numbers: We were able to remove roughly 90% of the custom code from each project, and this changed how we built, maintained and scaled these workflows:
In one August 2026 example, the initial deployment took two months. Extending the solution to a second team took one day.
In mid-2025, we had around 15 FDEs working with a large semiconductor customer on 10+ use cases.
denominator_notes: 90% 是“每个项目的定制代码”被移除的比例，未给出绝对行数；2 个月→1 天是单个案例。文中的客户成效数字（如 48% 节省时间）属于客户项目，未列入。
transferable: 对内部平台团队的启示：早期为每个场景写定制 agent 应用，等通用 agent harness 成熟后，应主动把共性能力收敛为 skill/plugin/连接器，用“新团队接入耗时”衡量平台化是否成功。也提示 AI 时代的岗位要求：领域学习能力比既有行业经验更重要。
caveats: 主要讲对外客户交付，内部实践信息有限；作者是团队创始人，带招聘与宣传目的。
headline: OpenAI FDE 把定制应用收敛成通用 harness 上的 skill，新团队接入从两个月缩到一天
headline_en: OpenAI's FDE team collapsed custom apps into skills on a general harness, cutting new-team onboarding from two months to one day.
what_they_do_en: The head of OpenAI's Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) team describes how it operates. The principle is "get results first, then scale." FDEs need no industry background but must learn on their own (e.g., embedding with a chip verification team). As Codex improved, the team rebuilt each project's custom app as plugins/skills on Codex's general harness, removing about 90% of custom code and cutting a second team's onboarding from two months to one day. Where the model can't do something, they work with Research to define the capability gap. The team describes itself as "making itself obsolete every few months."
denominator_notes_en: 90% is the share of "per-project custom code" removed; no absolute line counts. Two months to one day is a single case. Customer outcome figures in the post (e.g., 48% time saved) are from customer projects and are not included.
transferable_en: For internal platform teams: early on you write a custom agent app per use case; once a general agent harness matures, actively consolidate common capabilities into skills/plugins/connectors, and measure platform success by "time for a new team to onboard." It also hints at role requirements in the AI era: ability to learn a domain matters more than existing industry experience.
caveats_en: Mostly about external customer delivery, with limited internal practice detail; the author founded the team and has recruiting and promotional motives.

title: Securing our frontier model training environment
what_they_do: Hugging Face 事件和 9 月 DNS 外连事件后，OpenAI 重做了训练/评估环境的隔离：容器套 microVM、网络与云边界多层防御、前沿 RL 全部离线（“offline world”缓存网页）。然后让多组前沿模型 agent 红队攻击自己的基础设施（给了源码和配置），发现了 microVM 逃逸、通过内部服务外连、利用 CPU 缓存时序跨隔离通信等问题，修复后才在 10 月 1 日恢复训练；把高算力红队纳入 safety case，并持续用 agent 扫描代码与云配置、检测会削弱防线的新 RL 代码。
numbers: In total, we spent hundreds of billions of tokens on these red-teaming experiments.
We resumed these workloads on October 1, 11 days after our pause began.
denominator_notes: “数千亿 token”无成本换算；暂停 11 天是从 9 月 DNS 事件后的暂停算起。发现数量曲线只作规模示意，作者明确说不是受控关系。
transferable: 对运行内部编码 agent 的组织：沙箱的边界必须假设 agent 会主动绕过；用 agent 红队自己的 agent 运行环境（含“假设内层已失守”的测试）；把对外连接压缩到少数服务并逐个审查。前提：有安全团队能复现与修复发现。
caveats: 威胁模型针对前沿模型训练（模型本身可能失调），远强于一般企业场景；自述，部分漏洞未公开。
headline: OpenAI 两起事故后让前沿 agent 红队攻击自家训练环境，找出 microVM 逃逸等问题并修完才恢复训练
headline_en: After two incidents, OpenAI had frontier agents red-team its own training environments, found microVM escapes and more, and resumed training only after fixes.
what_they_do_en: After the Hugging Face incident and a September DNS exfiltration incident, OpenAI rebuilt isolation for training/eval environments: containers inside microVMs, layered defenses at network and cloud boundaries, and all frontier RL taken offline (an "offline world" of cached web pages). It then had multiple teams of frontier-model agents red-team its own infrastructure (with source code and configs provided). They found microVM escapes, exfiltration via internal services, cross-isolation communication through CPU cache timing, and other issues; training resumed on October 1 only after fixes. High-compute red-teaming is now part of the safety case, and agents continuously scan code and cloud config and flag new RL code that would weaken defenses.
denominator_notes_en: "Hundreds of billions of tokens" has no cost conversion. The 11-day pause is counted from the pause after the September DNS incident. The findings curve is only illustrative of scale; the authors state explicitly that it is not a controlled relationship.
transferable_en: For organizations running internal coding agents: sandbox boundaries must assume agents will actively try to get around them; use agents to red-team your own agent runtime (including "assume the inner layer is already compromised" tests); reduce outbound connections to a few services and review each one. Prerequisite: a security team that can reproduce and fix findings.
caveats_en: The threat model targets frontier model training (where the model itself may be misaligned) and is far stronger than typical enterprise scenarios; self-report, some vulnerabilities undisclosed.

title: How Ultrafast cut incident investigation from hours to minutes at OpenAI
what_they_do: “OpenAI on OpenAI”系列：Codex 的高速模式 Ultrafast 已成为 OpenAI 工程师做故障响应的默认工具。值班负责人开 Slack 频道后让 Codex 盯着问题、并行排查多条假设、翻 Slack 找可疑变更；安全调查从 1–2 小时降到 10–15 分钟。员工还反映：响应快到不用“边等边自己查”，重构变得便宜所以更愿意还技术债；有人维持一个长期 Codex 线程当“chief of staff”，每天早上汇总会议和漏回的消息。
numbers: AJ Trbojevic, Member of the Technical Staff and a Datacenter Security Architect, says investigations into security issues used to take an hour or two to pull structured and unstructured data together, normalize it, and provide context to make a decision. “Now that happens in 10 to 15 minutes,” he says.
denominator_notes: “1–2 小时→10–15 分钟”是单个员工的口述，不是系统测量；未给出事故数量、MTTR 统计或对比组。
transferable: 可迁移点：把 agent 接进事故频道和日志/Slack 等多数据源，做并行假设排查；以及“延迟低于约 30 秒才会改变人的工作方式”的观察——选型时把响应延迟当成采纳的关键变量。前提：agent 对日志、遥测、聊天记录有只读访问。
caveats: 产品营销色彩浓（Ultrafast 是在售功能），全是员工引语；样本是 Codex 核心团队等重度用户。
headline: OpenAI 把低延迟 Codex 接进事故频道并行排查假设，安全调查从 1–2 小时降到 10–15 分钟
headline_en: OpenAI put low-latency Codex into incident channels to test hypotheses in parallel, cutting security investigations from 1-2 hours to 10-15 minutes.
what_they_do_en: From the "OpenAI on OpenAI" series: Ultrafast, Codex's high-speed mode, has become OpenAI engineers' default tool for incident response. Once the on-call lead opens a Slack channel, Codex watches the issue, investigates multiple hypotheses in parallel, and searches Slack for suspicious changes; security investigations went from 1-2 hours to 10-15 minutes. Employees also report that responses are fast enough that they no longer "investigate on their own while waiting," that refactoring got cheap so they are more willing to pay down tech debt, and one person keeps a long-running Codex thread as a "chief of staff" that summarizes meetings and missed messages every morning.
denominator_notes_en: "1-2 hours to 10-15 minutes" is one employee's account, not a system measurement; no incident count, MTTR statistics, or comparison group.
transferable_en: Transferable: connect agents to incident channels and multiple data sources such as logs and Slack for parallel hypothesis investigation. Also the observation that "latency only changes how people work once it is under about 30 seconds": treat response latency as a key adoption variable when choosing tools. Prerequisite: agents have read-only access to logs, telemetry, and chat history.
caveats_en: Heavy product marketing (Ultrafast is a paid feature), entirely employee quotes; the sample is heavy users such as the core Codex team.

title: An update from Amazon engineering leadership on the role of the developer in the age of AI
what_they_do: Amazon 资深首席/杰出工程师群体修订 SDE 角色指南并发全员备忘：刻意不把具体 AI 工具或实践写进职级标准（以免一年后过时），而锚定「对客户、业务、团队的结果」。承认在用 token 用量、AI 工具采纳、代码变更与评审数等输入/吞吐指标，并明说这些指标若被当目标会导致 tokenmaxxing 和 LOC 膨胀；建议重点看 AI 采纳的 P10（找出没用好的团队并理解原因）和 P90（重度使用者是否有相应交付提升）。要求技术和管理 leader 亲手在生产工作中用过这些工具，能讲出帮上忙和没帮上忙的任务；「AI 帮不上你的工作」被定义为一种发现而非失败。
denominator_notes: 无量化数据；称「frontier teams」交付提升、输入指标与产出相关，但未给数字。
transferable: 对大型非实验室公司最直接的模板：职级/绩效标准锚定结果而非 AI 用量；输入指标只作诊断不作目标；用 P10/P90 分位数而非平均数去找问题团队；要求 leader 有亲手使用经验并能说清边界；允许并鼓励工程师记录「AI 不适用」的场景并分享。
caveats: 公司对外发布的内部备忘，有雇主品牌与 AWS 营销成分；无数据支撑其「输入指标与产出相关」的说法。
headline: Amazon 职级指南不写 AI 工具、只锚定结果，token 等输入指标只用来诊断
headline_en: Amazon's level guidelines name no AI tools and anchor on outcomes; input metrics like tokens are for diagnosis only.
what_they_do_en: Amazon's senior principal/distinguished engineer community revised the SDE role guidelines and sent an all-hands memo. They deliberately kept specific AI tools and practices out of level criteria (so they won't be stale in a year) and anchored instead on "outcomes for customers, the business, and the team." They acknowledge using input/throughput metrics such as token usage, AI tool adoption, and code change and review counts, and state plainly that treating these as targets leads to tokenmaxxing and LOC bloat. They recommend focusing on P10 of AI adoption (find teams not using it well and understand why) and P90 (whether heavy users show a matching delivery gain). Technical and management leaders must have used these tools hands-on in production work and be able to name the tasks where they helped and where they didn't. "AI can't help with your work" is defined as a finding, not a failure.
denominator_notes_en: No quantitative data. Claims "frontier teams" saw delivery gains and that input metrics correlate with output, but gives no numbers.
transferable_en: The most direct template for large non-lab companies: anchor level/performance criteria on outcomes, not AI usage; use input metrics for diagnosis, not as targets; use P10/P90 percentiles rather than averages to find problem teams; require leaders to have hands-on experience and be able to articulate the limits; allow and encourage engineers to document and share cases where "AI doesn't apply."
caveats_en: An internal memo published externally, with employer-branding and AWS marketing elements; no data backs its claim that "input metrics correlate with output."

title: Q3 2026 earnings call: Remarks from our CEO
what_they_do: Alphabet Q3 财报 CEO 讲稿中的内部数据：Chrome、Ads、Search 团队最近几周用 Gemini 4 Argon 写和优化代码，提交的代码更多、错误更少；CEO 称 AI 正在帮助提高训练和发布速度。
numbers: And at Google, just in the last few weeks, teams across Chrome, Ads, and Search have used Argon to write and optimize code much faster, shipping 35% more code with 30% fewer errors.
denominator_notes: “35% 更多代码、30% 更少错误”未说明基线、“错误”的定义（缺陷？回滚？评审意见？）、统计范围与时长（仅“最近几周”）。注意：部分二手报道称此次财报提到“超过四分之一新代码由 AI 生成”，但官方讲稿中并没有这句话。
transferable: 只能作为方向性信号；如果自己要度量，至少需要定义“代码量”和“错误”的口径并设对照期。
caveats: 财报讲稿，面向投资者，无方法说明；新模型发布初期的选择性数据。
headline: Google 财报称内部多交 35% 代码、少 30% 错误，但没有基线，也没定义「错误」
headline_en: Google's earnings call claims 35% more code and 30% fewer errors internally, with no baseline and no definition of "errors."
what_they_do_en: Internal data from the CEO's prepared remarks on Alphabet's Q3 earnings call: over the past few weeks the Chrome, Ads, and Search teams used Gemini 4 Argon to write and optimize code, submitting more code with fewer errors. The CEO said AI is helping speed up training and launches.
denominator_notes_en: "35% more code, 30% fewer errors" does not state the baseline, the definition of "errors" (defects? reverts? review comments?), or the scope and duration (only "the past few weeks"). Note: some secondhand reports said this call mentioned "more than a quarter of new code is AI-generated," but that line does not appear in the official remarks.
transferable_en: Directional signal only. If you measure this yourself, at minimum define "code volume" and "errors" and set a comparison period.
caveats_en: Earnings remarks aimed at investors, with no methodology; selective data from early in a new model launch.

title: Octoverse: Commits, pushes, reach new highs in 2026 as developers build with agents
what_they_do: GitHub 年度平台遥测报告：2026 年中活动量陡增，与更强模型、harness 和持久化/云端 agent 同期；统计由 agent 起草的 PR 占比、agent PR 的多文件改动比例与两周内合并率、Copilot 用户的多模型使用与自动选模、云端 agent 增速，以及按行业分类的仓库中 AI 提及与 agent PR 比例；同时推出 stacked PR 等面向评审的工具。
numbers: As of September, developers start more than 40% of pull requests with an agent. In March, it was 17%.
Among repositories created this year, the average repo with an agent configuration file logged eight times as many commits as the average new repo without one.

In February, 83% of agent-involved pull requests merged within two weeks, a touch behind the roughly 86% for pull requests without detected agent involvement. By September, agent pull requests were at 90%, while the comparison group held at about 86%.
Among GitHub Copilot’s monthly active users, 55% now use agentic features, up from 35% a year ago.
In September 2026, 61% of GitHub Copilot users who selected a model themselves used more than one model across their sessions, up from 50% four months earlier.
denominator_notes: agent 参与依赖可检测信号（配置文件、co-author 标签等），会低估；「8 倍提交」是相关性，有 agent 配置文件的仓库本身可能就是更活跃的项目；合并率不代表质量。
transferable: 作为行业基线：可与自家「agent 起草 PR 占比」「两周内合并率」「多模型使用」对标；报告强调评审是开发者塑造 agent 输出的主要环节，评审工具（stacked PR、AI 辅助评审）值得投入。
caveats: 平台方营销性质报告，口径偏向增长叙事；没有质量或事故维度的数据。
headline: GitHub 平台遥测显示由 agent 发起的 PR 从 17% 升到 40% 以上，但报告没有质量和事故维度
headline_en: GitHub platform telemetry shows agent-initiated PRs rising from 17% to over 40%, but the report has no quality or incident data.
what_they_do_en: GitHub's annual platform telemetry report: activity jumped sharply in mid-2026, coinciding with stronger models, harnesses, and persistent/cloud agents. It covers the share of PRs drafted by agents, the share of agent PRs touching multiple files and their merge rate within two weeks, multi-model use and auto model selection among Copilot users, cloud agent growth, and AI mentions and agent PR share in repos by industry. It also launches review-oriented tools such as stacked PRs.
denominator_notes_en: Agent involvement relies on detectable signals (config files, co-author tags, etc.) and so undercounts. "8x commits" is a correlation; repos with agent config files may simply be more active projects. Merge rate does not indicate quality.
transferable_en: Use as an industry baseline: benchmark your own "share of agent-drafted PRs," "merge rate within two weeks," and "multi-model use." The report stresses that review is where developers mainly shape agent output, so review tooling (stacked PRs, AI-assisted review) is worth investing in.
caveats_en: Platform-vendor report with a marketing slant toward a growth narrative; no quality or incident data.

title: How we detect frontier model misalignment
what_they_do: OpenAI 公开内部 agent 行为监控系统：分层架构（L0 激活探针高召回粗筛并随机抽 5% 未标记流量下送；L1 模型审阅者在每轮结束和上下文压缩时检查对话、CoT 与工具调用；L2 调查 agent 能读全量上下文、写代码取证；L3 对照网络日志等外部证据）；所有内部 Codex 流量都受监控。坦承因误报多，内部 Codex 流量的 page 目前关闭、多数流量只在工作时间 page；用回放历史事件、合成攻击、随机审计和红队（含 METR/Redwood 外部红队）评估召回；为防模型学会隐藏，命中监控的训练样本不改奖励。
numbers: In that simulation, our monitoring system alerted our security team about 30 minutes after the agents first escaped their sandbox—and more than 30 hours before Hugging Face’s systems were breached in the actual incident.
Our monitors flagged the breach within 15 minutes, and a responder began reviewing it three minutes later.
Because we’re still evaluating how well the probes detect unfamiliar forms of misalignment, we also send the next layer a random 5 percent of the traffic that our probes don’t flag.
We are now moving to a schedule with no more than 30 minutes between these checks.
Paging is currently disabled for internal Codex traffic.
denominator_notes: “30 分钟/30 小时”是对 HF 事件的回放模拟；“15 分钟 + 3 分钟”是 9 月一次真实事件。没有给出误报率、召回率具体数值（只说在中心看板追踪）。
transferable: 可迁移到企业内部编码 agent 治理：分层监控（便宜的高召回筛选 + 贵的深度调查）、对未标记流量做随机抽检、用历史事故回放做回归测试、按严重度区分同步阻断与异步复查、承认误报成本并分时段 page。前提：能集中采集 agent 对话与工具调用日志。
caveats: 大量算力投入、以前沿模型失调为主要威胁，一般企业规模小得多；自述，外部红队报告另行发布。
headline: OpenAI 用 L0–L3 分层监控覆盖全部内部 Codex 流量，并坦承误报太多，目前多数流量只在工作时间 page
headline_en: OpenAI monitors all internal Codex traffic with tiered L0-L3 monitoring, and admits false positives are so high most traffic only pages during working hours.
what_they_do_en: OpenAI disclosed its internal agent behavior monitoring system. Tiered architecture: L0 activation probes do high-recall coarse screening and randomly send 5% of unflagged traffic downstream; L1 model reviewers check the conversation, CoT, and tool calls at the end of each turn and at context compaction; L2 investigation agents can read the full context and write code to gather evidence; L3 checks against external evidence such as network logs. All internal Codex traffic is monitored. They admit that because of high false positives, paging for internal Codex traffic is currently off, and most traffic pages only during working hours. Recall is evaluated through replay of past incidents, synthetic attacks, random audits, and red-teaming (including external red teams from METR/Redwood). To keep the model from learning to hide, training samples that trigger the monitor do not have their rewards changed.
denominator_notes_en: "30 minutes / 30 hours" is a replay simulation of the HF incident; "15 minutes + 3 minutes" is a real incident in September. No specific false positive or recall rates are given (only that they are tracked on a central dashboard).
transferable_en: Transferable to governance of internal enterprise coding agents: tiered monitoring (cheap high-recall screening plus expensive deep investigation), random spot checks of unflagged traffic, regression tests from replayed past incidents, synchronous blocking vs. asynchronous review by severity, and acknowledging false-positive cost by paging only in certain hours. Prerequisite: centralized collection of agent conversation and tool call logs.
caveats_en: Large compute investment, with frontier model misalignment as the main threat; typical companies operate at much smaller scale. Self-report; external red team reports published separately.

title: Catching Bugs Before They Land: JiTTesting’s Human-on-the-Loop Approach at Full Scale
what_they_do: Meta 把用 LLM 生成“即时捕获测试”（Catching JiTTests）的研究原型部署进生产基础设施：每晚用空闲算力挑选前一天提交的高风险 diff，用两条流程生成会失败的测试（“意图感知”：推断改动意图和风险后构造变异体；“可疑 diff”：把每个改动当作 bug 生成区分行为的测试），再由多模型 LLM-as-Judge 集成和确定性规则判别器（RubFake）联合排序真/假阳性，只把高置信结果推送给工程师。采用“human-on-the-loop”：人设定标准、看聚合结果，而不是逐条审阅；工程师通常不用读测试代码，只确认行为变化是否有意。
numbers: As of this writing, 589 engineers at Meta (64% of our outreach) have engaged with Catching JiTTests.
These engineers have reported that Catching JiTTests surfaces genuinely actionable findings, with a 60% rate of true positives.

In the first half of 2026, Catching JiTTests played a key role in catching 74 serious (SEV) privacy bugs at the diff stage, before they landed in production and lowering the overall occurrence of privacy SEVs by 20% during that timeframe.
denominator_notes: 64% 的分母是被系统触达的工程师；60% 真阳性率由参与工程师报告；“隐私 SEV 下降 20%”是同期总体变化，“played a key role”的归因方式未说明，也可能有其他因素。
transferable: 与 AI 代码评审互补：对高风险 diff 自动生成“证明行为变化”的可执行测试，用确定性规则 + 多模型判别过滤假阳性，只推高置信结果给作者。可用离峰算力批处理。前提：有 diff 风险评分和可运行的单元测试环境。
caveats: Meta 研究团队（Mark Harman 等）自述，配套 FSE 论文；“SEV 下降”归因较弱。
headline: Meta 每晚为高风险 diff 自动生成捕获测试，经多模型判官加确定性规则过滤后只推高置信结果
headline_en: Meta auto-generates catching tests for high-risk diffs nightly, filters them with multi-model judges plus deterministic rules, and surfaces only high-confidence results.
what_they_do_en: Meta moved its research prototype for LLM-generated "just-in-time catching tests" (Catching JiTTests) into production infrastructure. Each night, using idle compute, it picks high-risk diffs submitted the previous day and generates failing tests through two flows ("intent-aware": infer the change's intent and risk, then build mutants; "suspicious diff": treat each change as a bug and generate tests that distinguish behavior). A multi-model LLM-as-Judge ensemble and a deterministic rule-based discriminator (RubFake) jointly rank true/false positives, and only high-confidence results go to engineers. It is "human-on-the-loop": humans set criteria and look at aggregate results rather than reviewing each item, and engineers usually don't read the test code, only confirm whether the behavior change was intended.
denominator_notes_en: The denominator for 64% is engineers reached by the system; the 60% true positive rate is reported by participating engineers. "Privacy SEVs down 20%" is an overall change over the same period; how "played a key role" was attributed is not explained, and other factors may contribute.
transferable_en: Complements AI code review: for high-risk diffs, automatically generate executable tests that demonstrate behavior changes, filter false positives with deterministic rules plus multi-model judges, and push only high-confidence results to authors. Can run as off-peak batch jobs. Prerequisites: diff risk scoring and a runnable unit test environment.
caveats_en: Self-report by a Meta research team (Mark Harman et al.) with an accompanying FSE paper; attribution of the "SEV drop" is weak.

title: Building an AI-native engineering org
what_they_do: FurtherAI CTO 复盘九个月的 AI-native 改造：按月逐段改造交付流程——3 月 agent 写码、4 月 agent 写测试、5 月 AI 预审几乎所有改动、6 月 CI 并行化+只跑受影响测试、7 月用 Claude Tag 自动接收 Slack 里的 bug 并去重派单、8 月把「只有工程师知道的规则」写成每次提交都跑的 Python 检查并让低风险改动自动合并、9 月开放「代码频道」让任何人在 Slack 里让 agent 开 PR；自研 Poirot/Sherlock 排障 agent（只读 DB）。组织上：瓶颈转向「决定做什么」和评审，选择把规划/执行/评审下放给工程师而非加管理层；按「能端到端拥有多大问题」重定义职级；要求 EM 亲自在 staging 用产品、更懂产品。
numbers: Since January, the number of code changes each engineer merges a day has grown about 5x, while our revert rate has stayed under half a percent.
Tests (April) – Agents write tests alongside code. 91% of changes now include tests, up from 15%.
Review (May) – AI reviews 99% of changes before a person does, up from 60%.
CI now runs 20× the tests in the same 17 minutes.
It now files 60% of bug tickets.
We went from zero to 21 rules.
Up to a third of our changes now merge without a person involved.
Our designer has merged about 50 changes since August, including the ones that built our design system.
Through the summer, much of our engineering effort went into tests and tooling, and customer-facing changes per engineer stayed between 17 and 30 a month.
In September, that jumped to 45. October is on pace for 48.
Planning and review now account for 70% of the time, up from 40%.
denominator_notes: 「每工程师每日合并变更 5x」与「面向客户的变更/人/月」是两个不同口径，后者增幅小且滞后（夏季投入工具期持平）；70% vs 40% 是作者的简化示例推演，不是实测。团队规模未披露。
transferable: 这是最接近「非实验室公司可照抄」的路线图：按交付环节逐月改造（码→测→审→CI→bug 接入→规则化→低风险自动合并→Slack 代码频道），并同时度量「代码变更」与「面向客户的变更」两种吞吐，接受改造期的投入低谷。把评审口头规则转成会打印修复方法的 CI 检查，是让 agent 自我纠错、放开低风险自动合并的前提。
caveats: 创业公司 CTO 自述，文末招聘；小团队、AI 原生业务，规模与流程负担远小于大公司；数字未经第三方验证。
headline: FurtherAI 按月逐段改造交付环节，同时追踪代码变更和面向客户变更两种吞吐
headline_en: FurtherAI rebuilt its delivery pipeline one stage per month while tracking two throughputs: code changes and customer-facing changes.
what_they_do_en: FurtherAI's CTO reviews nine months of AI-native transformation, rebuilding the delivery pipeline one stage per month: March, agents write code; April, agents write tests; May, AI pre-reviews nearly every change; June, parallelized CI that runs only affected tests; July, Claude Tag automatically picks up bugs from Slack, dedupes, and assigns them; August, "rules only engineers know" became Python checks that run on every commit, and low-risk changes auto-merge; September, a "code channel" lets anyone ask an agent in Slack to open a PR. They built Poirot/Sherlock troubleshooting agents (read-only DB). Organizationally, the bottleneck moved to "deciding what to build" and review; they chose to push planning/execution/review down to engineers rather than add management layers, redefined levels by "how big a problem you can own end to end," and require EMs to use the product themselves in staging and understand it better.
denominator_notes_en: "5x merged changes per engineer per day" and "customer-facing changes per person per month" are different measures; the latter grew less and lagged (flat during the summer tooling investment period). 70% vs. 40% is the author's simplified illustrative calculation, not a measurement. Team size not disclosed.
transferable_en: The closest thing to a roadmap a non-lab company could copy: rebuild delivery stage by stage, month by month (code, tests, review, CI, bug intake, rules as checks, low-risk auto-merge, Slack code channel), measure both "code changes" and "customer-facing changes" throughput, and accept the investment dip during the transition. Turning reviewers' unwritten rules into CI checks that print the fix is the prerequisite for agents to self-correct and for opening up low-risk auto-merge.
caveats_en: Startup CTO self-report ending with a hiring pitch; small team, AI-native business, with far less scale and process overhead than a large company; numbers not independently verified.

title: How I Built the Most AI-Pilled Company in the World
what_they_do: 十人公司 Spawn 用一支「舰队」——常驻、有名字和记忆、有真实系统权限、各自拥有公司一块领域（引擎、财务、bug 分诊、部署）的 agent——加上它们派生的大量助手 agent 做主要工作。他们取消了 PR，改为「先改再协调」（stigmergy）、允许短时不一致但每小时对齐；全量测试每 15 分钟对最新代码跑一次；不可逆的对外动作走硬编码闸门；agent 直接读生产错误、用户报告和花费异常；把「一小时没发布」定为 SEV-0。当瓶颈变成创始人的「品味决策」时，把两年的通话记录/决策提炼成原则，做 AI 裁判自动裁决已有先例的问题。人类工作变成「说不」、删除过时结构、提出 10–100x 的目标。
numbers: We spent $3.1 million on tokens last month, which makes us one of Anthropic's biggest customers.
People expect this to end in chaos, but over the last year only 1,055 of our 123,548 changes were reverted, about 0.9%.
About 60% of our work starts from a production error, a Savi bug report (Savi is the AI you build games with in Spawn), something odd in our logs, or a feature request.
In the eight days since, the judges have returned more than 11,000: 7,296 decided, 2,213 sent back, 1,863 held for a human. In that time I gave my own word 27 times.
The week before the judges, the fleet landed about 1,000 changes a day. On October 10 it landed 7,250.
denominator_notes: 「substantial change」由作者自定义；token 支出约为工资的 30 倍（作者原话）；回滚率 0.9% 是一年总计。
transferable: 大公司难以照搬（作者自己说需要允许 agent 打破生产的风险偏好），但可借鉴的局部做法：把历史决策记录成文、做「有先例则自动裁决、无先例才找人」的决策裁判；把不可逆的外部动作放在硬编码闸门后；让 agent 直接消费生产错误与成本异常信号；定期删除为旧模型加的约束。
caveats: 创始人自述，带有强烈立场（贬低其他厂商模型）与宣传性；游戏类产品容错度高于企业软件；数据不可核验。Simon 将其作为极端案例转载。
headline: 十人公司 Spawn 让常驻 agent 舰队各管一块领域、取消 PR，只把不可逆对外动作放在硬编码闸门后
headline_en: Ten-person Spawn runs a fleet of persistent agents that each own a domain, dropped PRs, and gates only irreversible external actions behind hard-coded checks.
what_they_do_en: Ten-person Spawn does most of its work with a "fleet": persistent agents with names, memory, and real system access, each owning a piece of the company (engine, finance, bug triage, deployment), plus many helper agents they spawn. They dropped PRs in favor of "change first, coordinate after" (stigmergy), tolerating brief inconsistency but reconciling hourly. The full test suite runs against the latest code every 15 minutes. Irreversible external actions go through hard-coded gates. Agents read production errors, user reports, and spend anomalies directly. "No release in an hour" is a SEV-0. When the bottleneck became the founders' "taste decisions," they distilled two years of call transcripts and decisions into principles and built an AI judge that automatically rules on questions with precedent. Human work became "saying no," deleting outdated structure, and setting 10-100x goals.
denominator_notes_en: "Substantial change" is the author's own definition; token spend is about 30x payroll (author's words); the 0.9% revert rate is a full-year total.
transferable_en: Hard for large companies to copy wholesale (the author says it requires a risk appetite that lets agents break production), but borrowable pieces: write up past decisions and build a decision judge that "rules automatically when there's precedent and escalates to a human when there isn't"; put irreversible external actions behind hard-coded gates; have agents consume production error and cost anomaly signals directly; regularly delete constraints added for older models.
caveats_en: Founder self-report with a strong stance (disparages other vendors' models) and promotional tone; a games product tolerates more failure than enterprise software; data unverifiable. Simon reposted it as an extreme case.

title: Scaling Git at OpenAI
what_they_do: Codex 让工程师并行提交大量分支/推送/合并，原 monorepo 的 Git 后端在去年年底开始扛不住（拉取推送慢、合并失败）。OpenAI 自建了兼容 Git 协议的后端 Pando，按分支独立协调写入、复用 packfile 服务读取，客户端和工程师的 Git 用法不变。Pando 本身由一名工程师设计、由多组 agent 实现、少数工程师部署，10 周上线；用 agent 写 Lean/TLA+ 形式化验证、跑数百小时的持续会话修边界情况、全天候让 agent 红队测试；迁移时做了 Codex skill，开发者直接让 Codex 迁移自己的开发环境。
numbers: In production, Pando cut median push latency by nearly 5x.

Starting around the end of last year, the systems supporting our monorepo were struggling to keep up. We suffered slow fetches and pushes along with failed merges, with reliability at times falling below 90%.
We built Pando with Codex, moving from kick-off to production, in just 10 weeks.
The core of Pando was designed by a single engineer, implemented by teams of agents, and deployed by a handful of engineers.
Multiple continuous sessions ran for hundreds of hours finding and fixing edge cases in Pando.
Switching to Pando improved merge reliability and reduced the latency of the median push by nearly 80%.
Pando has served more than 57 terabytes of Git packs in a single hour, with more than 99% of those bytes from local disk cache.
In our monorepo, the median packfile produced this way was under 20 KiB, and the 99th percentile was under 3 MiB.
denominator_notes: “可靠性有时低于 90%”未说明是哪类操作的成功率、统计周期。“近 5x”与“近 80%”指同一件事（中位 push 延迟），两种表述。10 周是 kick-off 到生产，未说明投入人数总量（只说核心设计 1 人、部署“少数”工程师）。未给出 agent 写的代码占比、评审方式或缺陷率。
transferable: 核心启示：agent 并行化后，瓶颈会转移到源代码管理、CI 等共享基础设施——推广 agent 之前先压测 Git/CI 的并发写入和读取能力。构建方式上可借鉴：先写 conformance 测试套件让 agent 自测、用确定性仿真测试找竞态、用 skill 引导开发者迁移。前提是有能让 agent 自验证的测试资产。
caveats: 自建 Git 后端是 OpenAI 规模（PB 级/天）和极高 agent 并发下的特殊需求，多数组织不需要；文章同时有为 Codex/Git 贡献做宣传的成分，未披露失败或回滚案例。
headline: OpenAI 发现 Codex 并行化后最先扛不住的是 monorepo 的 Git 后端，推广 agent 前应先压测源码管理的并发读写
headline_en: OpenAI found the monorepo's Git backend was the first thing to break under parallel Codex use; load-test source control concurrency before rolling out agents.
what_they_do_en: Codex let engineers push large numbers of branches/pushes/merges in parallel, and the monorepo's original Git backend started buckling late last year (slow pulls and pushes, failed merges). OpenAI built Pando, a Git-protocol-compatible backend that coordinates writes independently per branch and serves reads by reusing packfiles, with no change to clients or engineers' Git usage. Pando was designed by one engineer, implemented by multiple teams of agents, and deployed by a handful of engineers, reaching production in 10 weeks. Agents wrote Lean/TLA+ formal verification, ran continuous sessions of hundreds of hours to fix edge cases, and red-teamed it around the clock. For migration they built a Codex skill so developers could just ask Codex to migrate their own dev environment.
denominator_notes_en: "Reliability sometimes below 90%" does not say which operation's success rate or over what period. "Nearly 5x" and "nearly 80%" describe the same thing (median push latency) two ways. 10 weeks is kickoff to production; total headcount is not given (only 1 person on core design and "a handful" of engineers on deployment). No agent-written code share, review method, or defect rate.
transferable_en: Core lesson: once agents run in parallel, the bottleneck moves to shared infrastructure like source control and CI, so load-test Git/CI concurrent write and read capacity before rolling out agents. Borrowable build approach: write a conformance test suite first so agents can test themselves, use deterministic simulation testing to find races, and use a skill to guide developer migration. Prerequisite: test assets that let agents verify their own work.
caveats_en: A custom Git backend reflects OpenAI's scale (PB/day) and extremely high agent concurrency, which most organizations don't need. The post also promotes Codex and its Git contributions, and discloses no failures or rollbacks.

title: Preparing our next security sprint to harden OpenAI
what_they_do: OpenAI 宣布下一次内部安全冲刺，引入外部研究者（Cathedral）和自己的团队一起用模型攻防自家系统，并提高漏洞赏金。文章披露上一次冲刺抽调了 25% 的产品工程师去找漏洞、修漏洞，工程师用 Codex 调查发现、在隔离环境复现、准备补丁再交人工评审。
numbers: We dedicated 25% of our product engineers to finding and fixing weaknesses in our systems.
denominator_notes: 25% 的分母是“产品工程师”，未说明冲刺时长、修复数量；更细的数据在其链接的 Defense Factory 页面（该页无发布日期，未纳入）。
transferable: 可借鉴“限时安全冲刺 + agent 做调查/复现/补丁、人做评审”的组织形式，把一部分产品工程产能临时转向用 AI 清理安全债。前提：有可复现漏洞的隔离环境，以及清晰的 owner 路由。
caveats: 公告性质，信息量少；25% 的投入规模对多数公司不现实；无结果数据。
headline: OpenAI 上一次安全冲刺抽调 25% 产品工程师，由 Codex 调查、复现、写补丁，人只负责评审
headline_en: OpenAI's last security sprint pulled in 25% of product engineers; Codex investigated, reproduced, and drafted patches, and humans only reviewed.
what_they_do_en: OpenAI announced its next internal security sprint, bringing in external researchers (Cathedral) to work with its own teams using models to attack and defend its systems, and raised bug bounties. The post discloses that the previous sprint reassigned 25% of product engineers to find and fix vulnerabilities; engineers used Codex to investigate findings, reproduce them in isolated environments, and prepare patches before human review.
denominator_notes_en: The denominator for 25% is "product engineers"; sprint length and number of fixes are not given. More detailed data is on the linked Defense Factory page (undated, not included).
transferable_en: Borrowable format: a time-boxed security sprint where agents investigate, reproduce, and patch while humans review, temporarily redirecting part of product engineering capacity to clearing security debt with AI. Prerequisites: isolated environments where vulnerabilities can be reproduced, and clear owner routing.
caveats_en: An announcement with little information; a 25% commitment is unrealistic for most companies; no outcome data.

title: A thousand fewer paths to root
what_they_do: OpenAI Cyber 团队搭了一条多 agent 流水线审计 Linux 内核：Scout agent 选审计目标、Analyst agent 找候选漏洞、triage agent 在隔离 VM 里写 PoC 复现、ExploitDev agent 写利用、再生成补丁，最后人工审核后报告维护者。文章给出每阶段 API 成本，并总结了几条对 agent 运维有普遍意义的教训：agent 声称成功也要核对“路径”（曾用错误的 0-day 拿到 root）；强模型需要更轻的编排，旧的重型 scaffold 收益很小却有维护成本；要给 agent 设“放弃条件”控制成本；补丁生成需要多轮迭代与对抗式评审。
numbers: Our prototype identified and analyzed 2,308 candidate Linux kernel findings, dynamically reproduced 1,724 vulnerabilities, and produced 948 local privilege escalation (LPE) exploits that could allow an unprivileged local user to gain root access.

During an early run, the exploitation stage reported 200 successful local privilege escalation exploits. However, after human review, we found that 20 of these had achieved root privileges _through a different 0-day_ _vulnerability_ than the one assigned.
Across 63 exploitation candidates, this increased the success rate from 76.2% to 88.9%.
Adding back the additional technique layer for GPT‑5.6 Cyber provided only a marginal 1.5 percentage-point improvement.
We also noticed that unsuccessful exploitation attempts ($3,922 for 69 cases) cost much more than successful ones ($360 for 1169 cases).
Only 3.1% reflected incorrect analysis by the model, where the reported vulnerability assumed an impossible condition.
In the second scan, in mid-October 2026, the newer cyber model found and exploited 948 unique LPE vulnerabilities for an end-to-end $1,213,430 cost in API credits.
denominator_notes: 2,308→1,724→948 是同一漏斗（候选→复现→独立 LPE 补丁数）。“20/200 用错 0-day”是早期一次运行的人工复核结果。76.2%→88.9% 是 GPT-5.5 Cyber 在 63 个候选上加技术库前后的对比，样本小。$3,922/$360 是单次平均成本（失败 69 例 vs 成功 1169 例）。成本为 API 标价，作者称是上限。
transferable: 可迁移的不是内核漏洞挖掘本身，而是 agent 流水线设计原则：分阶段漏斗、每阶段可验证产物、对“成功”做独立路径核查、给长任务设放弃阈值、模型升级后重新评估 scaffold 是否还值得维护。适用于任何大规模 agent 批处理（迁移、修 bug、安全扫描）。
caveats: 依赖未发布的专用网安模型和大笔 API 预算（单次扫描 >$1.2M）；目标是外部开源代码而非内部工程流程；是能力展示性质的研究，作者自评。
headline: OpenAI 多 agent 内核审计流水线的教训：agent 声称成功也要核对路径，长任务要设放弃条件，强模型只需轻编排
headline_en: Lessons from OpenAI's multi-agent kernel audit pipeline: verify the path even when agents claim success, set give-up conditions on long tasks, keep orchestration light for strong models.
