what_they_do_en: OpenAI's Cyber team built a multi-agent pipeline to audit the Linux kernel: a Scout agent picks audit targets, an Analyst agent finds candidate vulnerabilities, a triage agent writes PoCs to reproduce them in isolated VMs, an ExploitDev agent writes exploits, patches are generated, and finally humans review before reporting to maintainers. The post gives API cost per stage and draws several lessons that apply to agent operations generally: verify the "path" even when an agent claims success (it once got root using the wrong 0-day); strong models need lighter orchestration, and old heavy scaffolds add little benefit but carry maintenance cost; give agents "give-up conditions" to control cost; patch generation needs multiple iterations and adversarial review.
denominator_notes_en: 2,308 to 1,724 to 948 is one funnel (candidates, reproduced, independent LPE patches). "20/200 used the wrong 0-day" is a manual recheck of an early run. 76.2% to 88.9% compares GPT-5.5 Cyber on 63 candidates before and after adding a technique library; small sample. $3,922/$360 is average cost per run (69 failures vs. 1169 successes). Costs are at API list price, which the authors say is an upper bound.
transferable_en: What transfers is not kernel vulnerability hunting itself but agent pipeline design principles: a staged funnel, verifiable artifacts at each stage, independent path checks on "success," give-up thresholds for long tasks, and re-evaluating after model upgrades whether a scaffold is still worth maintaining. Applies to any large-scale agent batch work (migrations, bug fixing, security scanning).
caveats_en: Depends on an unreleased specialized security model and a large API budget (a single scan >$1.2M). Targets external open-source code rather than internal engineering process. Capability-showcase research, self-assessed by the authors.

title: AI usage generates a fragile codebase
what_they_do: 一位 5 月被 Meta 裁员的工程师自述：在 Meta 最后几个月，他至少 90% 的代码由 AI 生成，而这是获得「过得去」绩效评级的最低要求；他认为 AI 并没让产出翻倍。现在另一家大公司的期望是 100% 代码由 AI 生成。他观察到的问题：AI 写浅层测试、过度复杂的代码、人对代码库理解下降、评审被速度压垮，并列出组织可自查的症状（事故增多、恢复变慢、只有用户能看到的错误）。
numbers: Don't get me wrong, I generated at least 90% of my code using AI in my last few months there, which was the minimum for a decent rating.
denominator_notes: 个人经历；「事故增多」等症状为作者归纳，未给出其团队数据。
transferable: 反面教材：把 AI 代码占比/用量写进绩效会催生为指标而用 AI 的行为（与 Amazon 备忘录警告的 tokenmaxxing 一致）；推广时应同时监控事故率、MTTR、测试有效性。
caveats: 单人叙述、带情绪（被裁员）、后半篇为观点。佐证：Pragmatic Engineer 2026-06-16 基于 Meta 内部人士报道称 token 用量被纳入绩效考核、内部有 token 排行榜，并将 5 月底 Instagram 账号接管事故归因于无人工参与的 AI 生成+AI 评审代码（https://newsletter.pragmaticengineer.com/p/why-is-meta-destroying-its-engineering，二手报道）。
headline: 前 Meta 工程师自述 90% AI 代码是拿到像样绩效的底线，把用量写进考核催生了浅测试和脆弱代码
headline_en: A former Meta engineer says 90% AI-written code was the floor for a decent rating, and tying usage to reviews produced shallow tests and fragile code.
what_they_do_en: An engineer laid off from Meta in May writes that in his last months there, at least 90% of his code was AI-generated, and that was the minimum to get a "meets expectations" rating; he does not think AI doubled his output. At another large company now, the expectation is 100% AI-generated code. Problems he observed: AI writes shallow tests and overly complex code, people understand the codebase less, and review is overwhelmed by speed. He lists symptoms organizations can check for (more incidents, slower recovery, errors only users can see).
denominator_notes_en: Personal experience; symptoms like "more incidents" are the author's generalizations, with no data from his team.
transferable_en: A cautionary example: putting AI code share/usage into performance reviews produces AI use for the sake of the metric (consistent with the tokenmaxxing the Amazon memo warns about). When rolling out, also monitor incident rate, MTTR, and test effectiveness.
caveats_en: Single-person account, emotionally charged (laid off), second half is opinion. Corroboration: Pragmatic Engineer on 2026-06-16, citing Meta insiders, reported that token usage was included in performance reviews, that there is an internal token leaderboard, and attributed a late-May Instagram account takeover incident to AI-generated plus AI-reviewed code with no human involvement (https://newsletter.pragmaticengineer.com/p/why-is-meta-destroying-its-engineering, secondhand report).

title: Introducing Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2
what_they_do: （模型发布帖，仅取内部实践部分）Anthropic 称其核心代码库超过 90% 的已合并变更由 Claude 编写（有人类指导）。内部用预发布模型修顽固 bug、跨服务性能优化，并用一组 agent 把一个关键生产服务从 Python 迁到 Rust；一名工程师实验让模型从空目录协调 1,000+ 个 subagent 连续 8 天写/测/审代码，做出可启动的原型操作系统。
numbers: Over 90% of the changes merged into Anthropic’s core codebase are now written by Claude (with human guidance).
A team of agents running an earlier version of Fable 5.2 migrated a critical production service from Python to Rust—the service is now more efficient, more reliable, and starts about 26 times faster.
Starting from an empty folder, the model coordinated over 1,000 subagents, working around the clock for eight days writing, testing, and reviewing code.
denominator_notes: 90% 的分母是「core codebase 的 merged changes」数量，非代码行数；未定义 core codebase 范围、统计时间窗、「written by Claude」判定口径（作者归属？行数占比？）以及人类指导/修改的程度。26 倍是单个服务的启动时间。1,000+ subagent 为单次实验，未给成本/token。
transferable: 可借鉴的是把「Claude 写的合并变更占比」作为组织级 AI 渗透指标来追踪，但需先定义口径（按变更还是行、如何归属）；大规模语言迁移（如 Python→Rust）交给 agent 团队是可尝试的高价值场景，前提是有完备测试与回滚。
caveats: 模型发布营销语境，数据无方法说明、不可复核；lab 内部模型访问与 token 预算不受限，研发人员同时是模型作者，不可直接外推到普通企业。
headline: Anthropic 称核心代码库九成以上合并变更由 Claude 写，服务级语言迁移已交给 agent 团队
headline_en: Anthropic says Claude writes over 90% of merged changes in its core codebase, and service-level language migrations are now handed to agent teams.
what_they_do_en: (Model launch post; only the internal practice portion is used.) Anthropic says more than 90% of merged changes in its core codebase are written by Claude (with human guidance). Internally, the prerelease model was used to fix stubborn bugs and optimize performance across services, and a team of agents migrated a critical production service from Python to Rust. One engineer ran an experiment in which the model, starting from an empty directory, coordinated 1,000+ subagents for 8 straight days writing/testing/reviewing code, producing a bootable prototype operating system.
denominator_notes_en: The denominator for 90% is the count of "merged changes in the core codebase," not lines of code. Not defined: the scope of the core codebase, the time window, how "written by Claude" is determined (authorship? share of lines?), or how much humans guided/modified. 26x is startup time for a single service. The 1,000+ subagent run is a single experiment with no cost/token figures.
transferable_en: Borrowable: track "share of merged changes written by Claude" as an organization-level AI penetration metric, but define the basis first (by change or by line, how attribution works). Handing large-scale language migrations (e.g., Python to Rust) to agent teams is a high-value scenario worth trying, provided you have thorough tests and rollback.
caveats_en: Model launch marketing context; data has no methodology and cannot be verified. The lab has unrestricted internal model access and token budget, and its engineers are also the model's authors, so this does not extrapolate directly to ordinary companies.

title: Safely scaling multi-agent teams with Claude Fable 5.2
what_they_do: Anthropic 内部实验：1,000 个 agent（1 lead + 999 helper）只用通用工具（各自无网络沙箱 VM、Lean 工具链、各自 Git 分支+合并请求、共享 Postgres）在无研究员指导下复现费马大定理形式化证明。lead 在前 10 分钟自建 5 张协调表（公告/分配/笔记/子任务/完成日志），按难度动态重分配人手，最难的子定理拆成 2,418 个任务、最深 10 层的任务树。安全层：沙箱（无消息工具、只能推自己的分支、数据库低权限+语句超时、网关在沙箱外标注身份、内核锁定、去 sudo）、实时 LLM 分类器逐个审查工具调用（拦截一次即全队暂停待人审）、离线监控；随后加了能看思维链和 agent 间通信的并行监控。经验：单机约 100 个 agent 就会资源耗尽；agent 倾向低估自己、过早放弃（开始时把 47/60 判为不可行），人类适时鼓励仍有价值。
numbers: The team took 28.7 hours, used one-third as many output tokens, and wrote a proof one-seventh the length of the original.
Our September formalization took a researcher and dozens of agents 11 days and roughly 6 billion output tokens.
A single shared machine hit its limits at about 100 agents: more than half of our 100-agent runs had to be stopped or restarted because memory, disk, or CPU ran out.
Each SQL statement had a five-second time limit, and writes were refused above 256 MiB.
During the run, the harness sent the lead 19 automatic reminders of how much time remained, each encouraging the lead to keep going.
Across more than a million tool calls, none in this run met the bar to be blocked.
By hour 5.6, 73 helpers had written 756 tasks, and only 16 of those helpers were captains.
The tree grew whenever a piece proved too hard for a single agent, ultimately reaching 2,418 tasks up to 10 levels deep (Figure 5).
Early on, helpers judged 47 of the 60 statements infeasible within the run’s budget, yet the team went on to prove most of them.
denominator_notes: 单次「玩具实验」，非生产工作流；token 比较对象是 9 月那次由研究员+数十 agent 完成的版本；「零拦截」是在一次运行的 100 万+ 工具调用上，且该次只启用了基于动作的监控。
transferable: 对要跑大规模并行 agent 的组织：每个 agent 独立沙箱、不给直接互发消息的通道、通过数据库/Git 这种可审计的共享状态协调；身份在沙箱外标注；对每个工具调用做实时分类器审查+离线复查，出现拦截即暂停等人工。前提是有 VM 级隔离与监控基础设施，且任务可拆分并有自动判定（如编译/测试）。
caveats: 研究性质、用未完全通过对齐评估的内部模型；数学证明有机器可检验的终点，普通业务任务缺少同等的自动 grader；token 成本未给出绝对值。
headline: Anthropic 跑 1,000 个 agent 的做法：各自沙箱、不给私信通道、只经 Git 和数据库协调，分类器一拦截就全队暂停
headline_en: How Anthropic ran 1,000 agents: separate sandboxes, no direct messaging, coordination only through Git and a database, and the whole fleet pauses on any classifier block.
what_they_do_en: An Anthropic internal experiment: 1,000 agents (1 lead + 999 helpers), using only generic tools (each with its own network-less sandbox VM, a Lean toolchain, its own Git branch plus merge requests, and a shared Postgres), reproduced the formal proof of Fermat's Last Theorem without researcher guidance. In the first 10 minutes the lead set up 5 coordination tables (announcements/assignments/notes/subtasks/completion log) and dynamically reallocated helpers by difficulty; the hardest sub-theorem was broken into a task tree of 2,418 tasks up to 10 levels deep. Safety layers: sandboxing (no messaging tool, can only push to its own branch, low-privilege database access with statement timeouts, identity tagged by a gateway outside the sandbox, locked-down kernel, no sudo); a real-time LLM classifier reviewing every tool call (a single block pauses the whole fleet pending human review); and offline monitoring. A parallel monitor that can see chain of thought and inter-agent communication was added later. Lessons: a single machine runs out of resources at about 100 agents; agents tend to underestimate themselves and give up too early (at the start they judged 47/60 infeasible), so timely human encouragement still helps.
denominator_notes_en: A single "toy experiment," not a production workflow. The token comparison is against the September version done by researchers plus dozens of agents. "Zero blocks" covers 1 million+ tool calls in one run, and that run had only action-based monitoring enabled.
transferable_en: For organizations running large-scale parallel agents: give each agent its own sandbox, provide no channel for agents to message each other directly, and coordinate through auditable shared state like a database or Git; tag identity outside the sandbox; review every tool call with a real-time classifier plus offline re-review, and pause for a human on any block. Prerequisites: VM-level isolation and monitoring infrastructure, and tasks that can be decomposed and judged automatically (e.g., compile/test).
caveats_en: Research setting, using an internal model that had not fully passed alignment evaluations. Math proofs have a machine-checkable endpoint; ordinary business tasks lack an equivalent automatic grader. No absolute token cost given.

title: Control Room: A central system to track and stop model workloads across our research infrastructure
what_they_do: OpenAI 在研究基础设施里建了 Control Room：每个做 agentic 推理的研究任务启动时申请 job_id，推理引擎每次出 token 前都向 Control Room 校验，任务一旦被叫停就拒绝继续生成。停止机制放在集中、统一的推理层而不是多变的研究代码里，并且 fail-closed（Control Room 挂了就全部拒绝）。还用 agent 和程序定期扫描，防止有人跑绕过 Control Room 的推理引擎；所有前沿 RL 任务都有监控模型，发现问题可自动叫停。
numbers: This works together with our [misalignment monitoring systems], and halts model output within 35 seconds of a decision to intervene to stop or pause a job.
The maximum time between the moment when Control Room receives an instruction to stop a job, and the moment when further progress is no longer possible, is 35 seconds.
denominator_notes: 35 秒是“收到停止指令”到“无法再产出”的最长时间，来源是推理授权缓存层；不含从发现问题到做出停止决定的时间。未给出被叫停任务数量或误停率。
transferable: 非实验室组织运行大量内部 agent（尤其长时运行、可调用工具的）时，可以借鉴“在集中的推理/网关层做 kill switch + job 身份 + fail-closed”，而不是指望每个 agent 应用自己实现停机逻辑。前提是所有 agent 流量都走统一的模型网关。
caveats: 面向模型训练/评估的研究基础设施，安全动机（防失控模型）比一般企业强得多；只在研究侧部署，外部服务栈另有机制。自述，无外部审计数据。
headline: OpenAI 把 kill switch 放在统一推理层：每个 agentic 任务带 job_id、出 token 前先校验，Control Room 挂了就全部拒绝
headline_en: OpenAI's kill switch lives in the unified inference layer: each agentic job's job_id is checked before every token, and it fails closed.
what_they_do_en: OpenAI built Control Room into its research infrastructure: every research job doing agentic inference requests a job_id at startup, the inference engine checks with Control Room before emitting each token, and once a job is stopped it refuses further generation. The stop mechanism sits in a centralized, unified inference layer rather than in ever-changing research code, and it fails closed (if Control Room is down, everything is refused). Agents and programs also scan periodically to catch anyone running inference engines that bypass Control Room. All frontier RL jobs have a monitoring model that can stop them automatically when it finds a problem.
denominator_notes_en: 35 seconds is the maximum time from "stop command received" to "can no longer produce output," driven by the inference authorization cache layer; it excludes the time from spotting a problem to deciding to stop. No figures on jobs stopped or false-stop rate.
transferable_en: Non-lab organizations running many internal agents (especially long-running, tool-calling ones) can borrow "kill switch + job identity + fail-closed in a centralized inference/gateway layer" instead of relying on every agent app to implement its own shutdown logic. Prerequisite: all agent traffic goes through a unified model gateway.
caveats_en: Research infrastructure for model training/eval, with a much stronger safety motive (guarding against runaway models) than typical enterprises. Deployed only on the research side; the external serving stack has separate mechanisms. Self-report, no external audit data.

title: Artificial Intelligence in the Firm: Bottlenecks in Software Production
what_they_do: 哈佛两位经济学者用工程分析平台 Jellyfish 的专有数据（GitHub、Jira、日历共 4.45 亿条工作事件，655 家公司、72 万员工），按企业采纳 AI 编码助手/agent 的时间差做双重差分。结论：AI 大幅增加代码产出，但 Jira issue/epic 等最终软件产出增幅小得多，对就业无可检测影响；瓶颈转到 code review——等审时间、审阅时长、要求修改次数都上升；79.1% 的企业已用 AI review 工具，但评审仍以人为主。
numbers: AI assistants lead to moderate increases in code output — 12 months after adoption, firms exhibit an increase of 30.4% in lines of code, 16.8% in commits, and 20.9% in pull requests. AI agents lead to larger additional increases in all three measures — 44.0% for lines of code, 36.0% for commits, and 35.7% for pull requests opened.

The effects from AI assistants are near zero, at −1.5% on issues and 3.4% on epics. The effects from AI agents are slightly larger — 13.7% on issues and 18.0% on epics — with the effect of agents on issues resolved being borderline significant.

We find evidence of a bottleneck in this stage: after adoption of AI agents, the average time from the code’s review submission to its approval increases by 56.1%. This change represents both an increase in the time that code waits in a “backlog,” by 59.9%, and an increase in the time after code has begun active review, by 58.5%.

This bottleneck is not eliminated by adoption of AI tools in the review process — 79.1% of firms have adopted AI code review tools, but still largely keep humans in the loop, with the overwhelming majority of reviews and comments being written by humans.
denominator_notes: 样本为使用 Jellyfish 的 655 家软件企业（自选择：愿意买工程度量平台的公司），数据截至 2026-03；采纳时点部分由 GitHub 活动推断。论文 11-09 版数字与 Ars 10-09 报道（基于旧版：LOC +30%、review 时长 +49%）不同，以论文当前版为准。
transferable: 这是本批中最重要的「反面/校准」证据：只看 LOC、commit、PR 会高估 AI 效果，要同时看 issue/epic 完成、PR 等审时长、要求修改比例、评审人力占比。组织若推 agent 而不同步改造评审（风险分级、自动化验证、AI 预审），产出会卡在 review。
caveats: 观察性研究，非随机；数据截止 2026-03，早于多个更强模型；作者为求职论文（Job Market Paper），有长期预测模型部分假设较强。HN 讨论与 Ars 读者评论多为对「被迫用 AI、评审被淹没」的共鸣。
headline: 哈佛基于 655 家公司的研究发现，AI agent 让代码量大增，但 issue 完成增幅小得多，瓶颈卡在代码评审
headline_en: A Harvard study of 655 companies finds AI agents sharply increase code volume but issue completion much less, with the bottleneck in code review.
what_they_do_en: Two Harvard economists used proprietary data from the engineering analytics platform Jellyfish (445 million work events across GitHub, Jira, and calendars; 655 companies, 720,000 employees) and ran a difference-in-differences analysis on staggered company adoption of AI coding assistants/agents. Findings: AI greatly increases code output, but final software output such as Jira issues/epics rises much less, with no detectable effect on employment. The bottleneck shifts to code review: time waiting for review, review duration, and change requests all rise. 79.1% of companies already use AI review tools, but review remains mostly human.
denominator_notes_en: The sample is 655 software companies using Jellyfish (self-selected: companies willing to buy an engineering metrics platform), with data through 2026-03; adoption timing is partly inferred from GitHub activity. The paper's 11-09 version has different numbers from the Ars report of 10-09 (based on an older version: LOC +30%, review time +49%); the current paper version takes precedence.
transferable_en: The most important counterweight / calibration evidence in this batch: looking only at LOC, commits, and PRs overstates AI's effect. Also track issue/epic completion, PR review wait time, share of changes requested, and share of reviewer effort. Organizations that push agents without also rebuilding review (risk tiering, automated verification, AI pre-review) will see output stall in review.
caveats_en: Observational, not randomized; data ends 2026-03, before several stronger models. The authors' job market paper, and the long-term forecasting model rests on strong assumptions. HN discussion and Ars reader comments largely echo "forced to use AI, drowning in review."

title: Hide your slop PR descriptions behind <details><summary>
what_they_do: Simon 的大部分改动现在都是 Claude Code 或 Codex 替他开的 PR。agent 写的 PR 描述准确全面却「读起来像 slop」，于是他的做法是：开头一段由人把关的高层说明（常配截图），把完整的 agent 长文折叠进 GitHub Markdown 支持的 <details><summary>，summary 写明模型和 effort 级别（如「Claude Opus 5.5 Medium」），承诺开头一段代表人的判断。
denominator_notes: 个人实践，无数据。
transferable: 团队可将其写进 PR 模板：首段人工撰写意图/影响 + 折叠的 agent 详述 + 标注生成模型。与 Kenton Varda 团队「禁止 AI 写描述」相比是更温和的折中。
caveats: 个人项目经验。
headline: Simon Willison 的 PR 首段由人写意图，agent 长描述折叠进 details 并标注模型
headline_en: Simon Willison's PRs open with a human-written paragraph on intent; the agent's long description is collapsed into details and labeled with the model.
what_they_do_en: Most of Simon's changes are now PRs opened for him by Claude Code or Codex. Agent-written PR descriptions are accurate and thorough but "read like slop," so his approach is: an opening high-level paragraph he vets himself (often with screenshots), the full agent write-up collapsed into <details><summary>, which GitHub Markdown supports, with the summary naming the model and effort level (e.g., "Claude Opus 5.5 Medium"), and a commitment that the opening paragraph represents human judgment.
denominator_notes_en: Personal practice, no data.
transferable_en: Teams can put this into the PR template: a human-written first paragraph on intent/impact, plus a collapsed agent write-up, plus the generating model labeled. A gentler middle ground compared with Kenton Varda's team "banning AI-written descriptions."
caveats_en: Personal project experience.

title: AWS Emulator and the engineer's job when agents write the code
what_they_do: AWS 发布全部由 agent 编写和测试的本地 AWS 模拟器：以 Smithy 公开 API 模型为规格，agent 先从规格派生端到端「fidelity test」并在真实 AWS 上修正到通过（使测试记录真实行为），再构建模拟器直到通过同一测试；agent 团队持续对照真实 AWS 找差距；每个变更都经 merge gate（多个安全 agent 对抗评审 + 通用代码评审 + 禁止 agent 触碰特定代码的确定性检查）。作者自述用 Kiro 重建当年 Alf 复制引擎：没有验证手段时盯了四个晚上无果，有了 spec 和测试环境后约两小时完成。
numbers: Matt began with SQS alone, and when he gave Kiro one prompt describing this approach, it returned a passable first version of an SQS emulator in about 15 minutes.
All of AWS Emulator’s code was written and tested by agents, and it is built from more than 400 API models covering more than 200 AWS services.
Once it had a spec and a test environment, the rebuild took about two hours.
denominator_notes: Simon 的链接帖补充：项目前三周有 29,684 次提交（来自 GitHub 仓库）。「四个月 vs 两小时」是作者个人对比，前者为当年人工首次构建。
transferable: 「先让 agent 从规格生成测试并在真实系统上校准，再让 agent 实现直到通过」是可推广的模式，适用于任何有 API 规格和真实参照系统的内部服务仿真/替代；同时说明工程师的新职责是设计 spec、测试与 merge gate，而不是写代码。
caveats: 厂商发布配套博文，带 Kiro 产品宣传；稳健性、真实使用效果未给数据；仓库有「things-that-do-not-work」目录记录未对齐行为。
headline: AWS 让 agent 先从 API 规格生成并在真实 AWS 上校准测试，再实现模拟器直到通过
headline_en: AWS has agents generate tests from API specs and calibrate them against real AWS, then build the emulator until it passes.
what_they_do_en: AWS released a local AWS emulator written and tested entirely by agents. Using Smithy's public API models as the spec, agents first derive end-to-end "fidelity tests" from the spec and fix them against real AWS until they pass (so the tests record real behavior), then build the emulator until it passes the same tests; agent teams keep comparing against real AWS to find gaps. Every change goes through a merge gate (adversarial review by several security agents, plus general code review, plus deterministic checks that forbid agents from touching specific code). The author describes using Kiro to rebuild the Alf replication engine from years ago: without a way to verify, he stared at it for four evenings with no result; with a spec and a test environment it took about two hours.
denominator_notes_en: Simon's linked post adds: 29,684 commits in the project's first three weeks (from the GitHub repo). "Four months vs. two hours" is the author's personal comparison; the former was the original manual build years ago.
transferable_en: "Have agents generate tests from the spec and calibrate them against the real system, then have agents implement until the tests pass" is a generalizable pattern for emulating/replacing any internal service that has an API spec and a real reference system. It also shows the engineer's new job is designing specs, tests, and merge gates, not writing code.
caveats_en: A vendor companion blog post with Kiro product promotion; no data on robustness or real-world effectiveness; the repo has a "things-that-do-not-work" directory recording behavior that doesn't match.

title: Securing persistent agents like OpenClaw at OpenAI
what_they_do: OpenAI 在全公司部署了常驻（persistent）agent，包括数百个 OpenClaw agent。安全控制：把可信的确定性组件（网关/配置、网络、身份、沙箱）与不可信的 LLM 执行分离到不同容器甚至集群；沙箱用组织管理的网络白名单+显式拒绝（含云元数据地址）、只允许写工作目录、进程隔离、密钥走凭证代理不暴露给 agent，禁用 danger-full-access；所有动作强制 auto-review（第二个 agent 审批，避免人类审批疲劳）；每个 agent 有独立身份（ChatGPT Service Account），可审计、可单独断推理；记录所有配置变更和每一轮对话，日志只有少数安全人员可看。文中附了可直接参考的 requirements.toml / config.toml 配置。
numbers: At OpenAI, we currently have persistent agents deployed across the entire company, including hundreds of OpenClaw agents.

We now have over 500 agents that run proactively in the background doing meaningful work - everything from automatically opening PRs in response to product feedback to continuously running data experiments on new features.
denominator_notes: “数百个 OpenClaw agent”与“超过 500 个后台 agent”口径可能不同（后者可能含非 OpenClaw）；未给出事故数、auto-review 拦截率或生产力测量（只说“巨大提升”）。
transferable: 这是目前最可直接照抄的“企业内部常驻 agent 安全基线”清单：控制面/执行面分离、网络白名单、凭证代理、agent 独立身份、模型审批人、全量审计日志。前提：有统一的 agent 运行平台和身份体系；注意 auto-review 要配合抽样人工复核。
caveats: 同时在推广其开源控制面（OCE）；没有披露这些控制的失效案例或成本。
headline: OpenAI 数百个常驻 agent 的安全基线：控制面执行面分离、网络白名单、凭证代理、独立身份、agent 审批
headline_en: OpenAI's security baseline for hundreds of persistent agents: control/execution plane separation, network allowlists, credential proxy, per-agent identity, agent approval.
what_they_do_en: OpenAI has deployed persistent agents company-wide, including hundreds of OpenClaw agents. Security controls: trusted deterministic components (gateway/config, network, identity, sandbox) are separated from untrusted LLM execution into different containers or even clusters. The sandbox uses an org-managed network allowlist plus explicit denies (including the cloud metadata address), allows writes only to the working directory, isolates processes, routes secrets through a credential proxy so the agent never sees them, and disables danger-full-access. All actions require auto-review (a second agent approves, avoiding human approval fatigue). Each agent has its own identity (ChatGPT Service Account), so it is auditable and its inference can be cut off individually. All config changes and every conversation turn are logged, and only a few security staff can view the logs. The post includes requirements.toml / config.toml configs you can use directly as reference.
denominator_notes_en: "Hundreds of OpenClaw agents" and "more than 500 background agents" may use different bases (the latter may include non-OpenClaw agents). No incident count, auto-review block rate, or productivity measurement (only "huge gains").
transferable_en: The most directly copyable "security baseline for persistent internal enterprise agents" so far: control/execution plane separation, network allowlists, credential proxy, per-agent identity, model approver, full audit logs. Prerequisite: a unified agent runtime platform and identity system. Note that auto-review should be paired with sampled human re-review.
caveats_en: Also promotes its open-source control plane (OCE); discloses no failures or costs of these controls.

title: Making AI adoption stick: What we learned after launching Copilot Cowork at Microsoft
headline: Microsoft 内部推 agent 工具的复盘：开通不等于采用，靠同事的真实 prompt 和持续数月的提醒拉动使用，但因为上线前没设基线，说不清哪项动作起了作用
what_they_do: Microsoft Digital（公司 IT 部门）4 月在全员大会上线 Copilot Cowork（跨 M365 和 web 执行多步任务的 agent）后，没有把上线当终点：组了一个跨 IT、产品、市场的虚拟团队，分头负责宣传、用户反馈、产品需求回传；6 月发起 #HowICowork，请员工贴出自己真实的 prompt 和产出；配套可改的示例 prompt，并做了 Azure DevOps、Chart 等 plugin 把 agent 接进更多日常系统。之后把这些员工案例打包成销售用的客户材料。复盘里他们承认：上线前没有干净的基线，无法证明哪次宣传带来了增长。
numbers: The campaign reached about 58% of our employees, and 45 people shared their own Copilot Cowork prompts and stories.
Over the same period, weekly active Cowork users grew 27%, from about 35,000 to nearly 45,000 employees.
Between mid-August and early October, monthly active users grew from about 60,000 to 70,900.
By early October, Cowork also had 52,400 weekly active users and 27,800 daily active users.
A quick reality check: This data doesn’t prove that any one email or post caused a bump, and we didn’t have a clean baseline from before launch to compare against.
denominator_notes: 58% 是活动触达率，不是使用率；分享案例的只有 45 人。WAU 35,000→45,000 与活动「同期」，作者自己说没有上线前基线、不能归因。MAU/WAU/DAU 都是活跃数，没有说明「活跃」的定义，也没有任何产出或质量指标；员工总数未给出，无法换算渗透率。
transferable: 推 agent 类工具时，把「上线」之后的 2–3 个月当成主战场：先在上线计划里就排好同事案例征集（真实 prompt + 真实产出），比功能清单更能让人想象「我能交给它什么」；同时在上线之前埋好使用遥测和活动标记，才能把宣传节奏和采用曲线对上。前提是有一个能持续运营内部社区、并能把反馈回传给产品方的小团队。另一个可借：把文档写成「人和 AI 都搜得到」的形式，把「找到正确答案」而不只是点击量当成指标。
caveats: Microsoft 是 Cowork 的厂商，Inside Track 本身兼具对外营销（文末有销售引流）；只有采用数据，没有效果数据；增长与自然扩散、产品改进无法区分，作者自己也承认。
headline_en: Microsoft's internal agent rollout review: provisioning isn't adoption; peers' real prompts and months of nudges drove use, but with no pre-launch baseline, impact can't be attributed.
what_they_do_en: After Microsoft Digital (the company's IT organization) launched Copilot Cowork (an agent that runs multi-step tasks across M365 and the web) at an all-hands in April, it did not treat launch as the finish line. It formed a virtual team across IT, product, and marketing, splitting ownership of promotion, user feedback, and routing product requirements back. In June it started #HowICowork, asking employees to post their real prompts and outputs, alongside editable sample prompts, and built plugins such as Azure DevOps and Chart to connect the agent to more everyday systems. These employee stories were later packaged into customer-facing sales material. In the review they admit there was no clean pre-launch baseline, so they cannot show which push drove growth.
denominator_notes_en: 58% is campaign reach, not usage rate; only 45 people shared stories. WAU going from 35,000 to 45,000 was "concurrent" with the campaign, and the authors themselves say there is no pre-launch baseline and it cannot be attributed. MAU/WAU/DAU are activity counts with no definition of "active," and there are no output or quality metrics; total headcount is not given, so penetration cannot be calculated.
transferable_en: When rolling out agent tools, treat the 2-3 months after launch as the main effort. Build peer story collection (real prompts + real outputs) into the launch plan from the start; it does more than a feature list to help people imagine "what I could hand off to it." And instrument usage telemetry and campaign markers before launch so you can line up campaign timing with the adoption curve. Prerequisite: a small team that can keep an internal community running and route feedback back to the product owner. One more borrowable idea: write documentation so "both people and AI can find it," and measure "finding the right answer," not just clicks.
caveats_en: Microsoft is the vendor of Cowork, and Inside Track doubles as external marketing (it ends with a sales funnel). Only adoption data, no impact data. Growth can't be separated from organic spread and product improvements, as the authors acknowledge.

title: Advancing science & engineering with Antigravity’s /teamwork
headline: Google 的多 agent harness 靠「按步骤切分上下文 + 独立证伪器 + 不看原作者推理的审计 agent」跑多日任务，并用它在生产基础设施上拿到可量化收益
what_they_do: 这是一篇产品/科研成果帖，其中有 Google 内部工程用法。/teamwork 的设计：每个专职 agent 只拿到当前步骤需要的文件和工具；协调者把任务交给全新上下文的继任者；critic/auditor 在干净上下文里复核，看不到原作者的推理；候选解交给 Lean、原封不动的测试套件、模拟器、硬件计数器等「证伪器」自动判定。大规模迁移的做法是：按依赖顺序调度模块，每个叶子模块都链接原始、未改动的测试，防止 agent 打桩或改测试。内部落地包括：两周把 Zircon 内核剩余 C++ 改写成约 80 万行 Rust；Borg 调度优化上线 2 个改动；全机队内存优化；TPU kernel 优化中先让 agent 造 23 秒的代理评测，再定期用完整硬件跑校准排序。
numbers: To prevent this, /teamwork partitions context by construction: each specialized agent receives only the exact files and tools it needs for a specific step.

Building on the initial 25% port of the Zircon microkernel, a two-week Argon campaign rewrote the remaining C++ code, adding about 800,000 lines of safe Rust that pass all kernel unit tests and boot on arm64 hardware.

Fleet-wide memory optimization: Building on the initial Argon memory efforts, we analyzed fleet-wide metrics, as well as internal memory saving past successes, and created reusable /teamwork workflows that have identified memory saving opportunities, surpassing our initial savings estimates of 1 PiB.

Borg agentic scheduling: Built on /teamwork and /boost, Borg’s agentic workflow for scheduling optimization shipped 2 successful changes, resulting in a 24% reduction in TPU workload preemption on some hardware types, while preserving workload SLOs and cluster utilization.
denominator_notes: Zircon：「通过全部内核单元测试并能在 arm64 启动」是验收标准，没说是否已合入生产、有无人工评审或后续缺陷。内存：是「已识别的」节省机会超过 1 PiB，不是已释放量（对比 Argon 帖里已释放 300 TiB）。Borg：24% 只在「部分硬件类型」上，总共 2 个改动，没给基线和时间窗。没有任何 token/算力成本数据。
transferable: 想让 agent 跑多日任务，先把三件事做成结构而不是提示：① 每一步只给需要的文件和工具，长任务定期换新上下文接力；② 每类产出都配一个机器可判的证伪器（编译器、原始测试、模拟器），没有证伪器的任务先别交给长时 agent；③ 复核 agent 不读原作者的推理，只看产物。做代码迁移时，按依赖拓扑排期、只用原始测试验收。完整评测太慢时，可以先让 agent 造快速代理指标，再用完整评测定期校准排序（Kendall 相关）。前提：已有可信、可自动跑的测试或评测。
caveats: 厂商自报、挑选案例，主体是科研成果和产品推广；生产收益只列了少数几项，没有失败率、成本和人力投入；Google 规模的基础设施（Borg、TPU、机队级 profiling）多数组织没有。
headline_en: Google's multi-agent harness runs multi-day tasks with per-step context slicing, independent falsifiers, and auditors blind to the author's reasoning, with measurable gains on production infrastructure.
what_they_do_en: This is a product/research results post that includes Google's internal engineering usage. /teamwork design: each specialized agent gets only the files and tools needed for the current step; the coordinator hands the task to a successor with fresh context; critics/auditors review in clean context and cannot see the original author's reasoning; candidate solutions are judged automatically by "falsifiers" such as Lean, the untouched test suite, simulators, and hardware counters. For large migrations: modules are scheduled in dependency order, and each leaf module is linked against the original, unmodified tests so agents can't stub or alter tests. Internal results include: rewriting the remaining C++ in the Zircon kernel into about 800,000 lines of Rust in two weeks; 2 Borg scheduling optimizations shipped; fleet-wide memory optimization; and in TPU kernel optimization, having agents build a 23-second proxy eval first, then periodically recalibrating rankings on full hardware.
denominator_notes_en: Zircon: the acceptance criterion is "passes all kernel unit tests and boots on arm64"; it doesn't say whether it was merged into production, received human review, or had later defects. Memory: "identified" savings opportunities exceed 1 PiB, not amounts actually freed (compare the 300 TiB already freed in the Argon post). Borg: 24% applies only to "some hardware types," 2 changes total, with no baseline or time window. No token/compute cost data at all.
transferable_en: To have agents run multi-day tasks, build three things into structure rather than prompts: (1) give each step only the files and tools it needs, and hand off long tasks to fresh context periodically; (2) pair every kind of output with a machine-checkable falsifier (compiler, original tests, simulator), and don't give tasks without a falsifier to long-running agents yet; (3) review agents don't read the author's reasoning, only the artifact. For code migrations, schedule by dependency topology and accept only against the original tests. When full evals are too slow, have agents build a fast proxy metric first, then periodically recalibrate rankings against the full eval (Kendall correlation). Prerequisite: trustworthy tests or evals that run automatically.
caveats_en: Vendor self-report with cherry-picked cases; mostly research results and product promotion. Only a few production gains are listed, with no failure rate, cost, or headcount. Most organizations don't have Google-scale infrastructure (Borg, TPUs, fleet-level profiling).

title: Intelligent Delivery: Making Every Unit of Compute Serve Better Ads
headline: Meta 广告服务系统让 agent 读源码、设计文档和十年实验日志来提出并跑实验，最自动化的环节里 agent 承担约八成工程工作，每个改动仍由工程师批准
what_they_do: 这是一篇广告算力分配系统的架构帖，其中一节讲内部工程方式：调参空间随新模型、新硬件膨胀，靠专家经验和约束优化都跟不上；改为让 agent 持续监控系统，在长 context window 里读机制源码、设计文档和十年的实验日志，缩小到少数值得测的改动，再设计并运行实验。工程师审批最终改动后才上线，共享知识库为每一步提供输入。
numbers: In the first half of 2026, agents contributed to about 20% of Intelligent Delivery optimizations.

On our most automated mechanism, they now contribute to about 80% of the engineering effort, from understanding the system landscape and forming hypotheses to running experiments and converging on the final change.
This shortens the optimization loop from months to weeks while keeping people firmly in control.
denominator_notes: 20% 是 2026 上半年「agent 参与」的优化占比，「contributed to」没有定义，可能包括部分参与；80% 只指「最自动化的那一个机制」，工程工作量怎么计量没说。「数月→数周」没有具体样本或基线。
transferable: 适合先交给 agent 的是「搜索空间大、有闭环实验环境、有历史实验记录」的调优类工作：把历史实验日志和设计文档整理成 agent 可读的知识库，让 agent 负责缩小候选和跑实验，人只批最终改动。前提是已有端到端的离线/闭环测试环境，能让 agent 安全地跑实验。
caveats: 单一团队自报；没有给出 agent 提出的改动被否决的比例、出错案例或成本；Meta 广告系统的实验基础设施成熟度很高，一般组织难以直接复制。
headline_en: Meta's ads agents read source, design docs, and ten years of experiment logs to run experiments, doing ~80% of one mechanism's engineering; engineers approve every change.
what_they_do_en: This is an architecture post on an ads compute allocation system, with one section on internal engineering practice. The tuning space keeps expanding with new models and hardware, and neither expert experience nor constrained optimization could keep up. Instead, agents continuously monitor the system, read mechanism source code, design docs, and ten years of experiment logs in a long context window, narrow down to a few changes worth testing, and then design and run experiments. Engineers approve the final change before it ships, and a shared knowledge base feeds every step.
denominator_notes_en: 20% is the share of optimizations in H1 2026 with "agent involvement"; "contributed to" is undefined and may include partial involvement. 80% applies only to "the single most automated mechanism," and how engineering effort was measured is not stated. "Months to weeks" has no specific sample or baseline.
transferable_en: Good first candidates for agents: tuning work with "a large search space, a closed-loop experiment environment, and historical experiment records." Organize past experiment logs and design docs into an agent-readable knowledge base, have agents narrow candidates and run experiments, and have humans approve only the final change. Prerequisite: an existing end-to-end offline/closed-loop test environment where agents can run experiments safely.
caveats_en: Single-team self-report; no rate of agent-proposed changes rejected, no failure cases or costs. Meta's ads experiment infrastructure is very mature, and most organizations can't replicate it directly.

title: A weird experiment I've been trying the last few weeks is having Claude take over day-to-day maintenance of our apps.
what_they_do: Claude Code 负责人 Boris Cherny 的 LinkedIn 帖：团队开了一个 Slack 频道 proj-claude-maintains-apps，让 Claude Tag 每天在 iOS、Android、Desktop、web、CLI 和 Agent SDK 上跑一组维护 routine。点名的四个：crash fuzzer（在模拟器里乱点找崩溃，再定位根因并修）、dup unifier（找相似但略有分歧的抽象并提 PR 合并）、dead-code remover（删静态不可达代码；对疑似死代码先加日志，确认没被调用第二天再删）、abstraction police（修漏的抽象）。每个 PR 先过 Claude Code Review 再过人审才合并。某个 routine 出的 PR 不对时，不去手改 PR，而是让 Claude 调这个 routine 的 prompt，有时要调几天。团队说下一步是想办法让这类机械改动更容易合并。
numbers: Over the last few weeks, these routines have opened 388 PRs across our repos, 180 of which we merged after Claude Code Review + human review.
denominator_notes: 180/388 约 46%，是合并率，不是正确率：帖子没说另外 208 个为什么没合（被拒、重复、过时、还是排队没人看都有可能），也没给按 routine 拆分的数字。「the last few weeks」没有确切天数，所以算不出每周产量。没有 token 成本、人审耗时和合并后的回滚数。
transferable: 先挑两三类机械、可自证的维护任务做每日 routine：死代码（先加日志取证再删）、重复抽象、崩溃 fuzz。每类一个 prompt，产出的 PR 走和人写的一样的评审。按 routine 记合并率和拒绝原因，PR 不对就改 prompt 而不是改 PR。前提：有能接住额外 PR 量的自动评审和 CI，以及愿意每天清这批 PR 的 owner；一半以上不合并是要预留的评审成本。
caveats: 厂商员工个人帖，自称是「weird experiment」和「early signs of life」，同时在推广 routines 和 Claude Tag。只有一个团队、一个数字，没有后续结果；合并掉的 180 个有没有引入回归没有交代。
headline: Claude Code 团队让 Claude 每天自动做应用维护：几周开了 388 个 PR，过完自动评审和人审后合并 180 个
headline_en: The Claude Code team has Claude run daily app maintenance: 388 PRs opened in a few weeks, 180 merged after automated and human review.
what_they_do_en: A LinkedIn post by Claude Code lead Boris Cherny. The team set up a Slack channel, proj-claude-maintains-apps, where Claude Tag runs a set of daily maintenance routines across iOS, Android, Desktop, web, CLI, and the Agent SDK. Four are named: a crash fuzzer (taps around the app in a simulator to find crashes, then root-causes and fixes them), a dup unifier (finds similar but slightly divergent abstractions and opens PRs to unify them), a dead-code remover (deletes statically unreachable code; for suspected dead code it adds logging first and removes it the next day if nothing fires), and an abstraction police routine (fixes leaky abstractions). Each PR goes through Claude Code Review and then human review before merging. When a routine produces bad PRs, the team has Claude tune that routine's prompt instead of hand-fixing the PR, which sometimes takes a few days. The stated next step is making this kind of mechanical change easier to merge.
denominator_notes_en: 180 of 388 is about 46%, and it is a merge rate, not a correctness rate. The post does not say why the other 208 were not merged (rejected, duplicate, stale, or simply unreviewed are all possible) and gives no per-routine breakdown. "The last few weeks" has no exact length, so a weekly volume cannot be derived. There is no token cost, human review time, or count of post-merge reverts.
transferable_en: Start daily routines with two or three mechanical, self-proving maintenance tasks: dead code (log first, delete after evidence), duplicate abstractions, crash fuzzing. One prompt per task, and the PRs go through the same review as human-written ones. Track merge rate and rejection reasons per routine, and fix the prompt rather than the PR when output is wrong. Prerequisites: automated review and CI that can absorb the extra PR volume, and an owner willing to clear the queue daily. Budget review time for more than half the PRs not merging.
caveats_en: A vendor employee's personal post, self-described as a "weird experiment" with "early signs of life," which also promotes routines and Claude Tag. One team, one number, no follow-up; nothing is said about whether the 180 merged PRs caused regressions.

title: How the Claude Code team thinks about verification
headline: Claude Code 团队把「验证层」当成独立系统来管：改动碰不到判它的规则，新闸门先 observe 再 enforce，漏掉的 bug 转成规则
what_they_do: Claude Code 团队（约九成代码由 Claude 写和审）讲了自己的验证流程。每个仓库放一个 verify skill，让 Claude 提交前把应用真的跑起来做冒烟测试（浏览器扩展、移动端 MCP、computer use、本地起服务）；提 PR 前先跑测试、构建、lint；检查连续三轮还失败，Claude 就停手叫人。代码 owner 自己写检查；一份 39 条的可靠性清单，每条带一个能从 diff 读出的触发条件，Claude 只查命中的那 3–10 条。不加第二个 reviewer，而是调好主 reviewer 的 REVIEW.md，并且只从 base 分支读，PR 改不了判它的规则；评审结果绑定具体 commit。每个 commit 盖上「怎么验证的」戳（含 none），commit 闸门分 off/observe/enforce 三档，同一 session 被拦两次后放行。用回滚数、合并前被拒数和同尺寸的干净改动对照组来「评审 reviewer」；漏判的 bug 要在至少两个 PR 出现、能从 diff 识别，经三个 agent 尝试证伪、人在 PR 里批准后才写成规则；flaky 测试不许加 sleep 或重试，找不到根因就删掉并写明原因；规则文件定期清理。
what_they_do_en: The Claude Code team (where Claude writes and reviews about 90% of the code) described its verification process. Each repo has a verify skill so Claude actually runs the app as a smoke test before committing (Chrome extension, mobile MCP, computer use, or a local service). Before opening a PR, Claude runs tests, build, and lint; if a check still fails after three rounds, Claude stops and pulls in a human. Code owners write their own checks. A 39-item reliability checklist gives each item a trigger readable from the diff, and Claude checks only the 3 to 10 that match. Instead of adding a second reviewer, they tune the primary reviewer's REVIEW.md, which is read only from the base branch so a PR cannot change the rules judging it; review results are tied to a specific commit. Every commit is stamped with how it was verified (including none), and a commit gate has off/observe/enforce modes, letting the next commit through after two blocks in one session. They review the reviewers using revert counts, pre-merge rejections, and a size-matched control set of clean changes. A missed bug becomes a rule only if it shows up in at least two PRs, is identifiable from a diff, survives three agents trying to disprove it, and is approved by a human in a PR. Flaky tests can't be fixed with sleeps or retries; if no root cause is found, the test is deleted with a written reason. Rule files are pruned on a routine.
numbers: On the Claude Code team, the vast majority of our code (~90%) is written and reviewed by Claude.

In internal testing around structured file generation, having a separate grader check Claude’s work against a rubric improved task success by up to 10 points over a standard prompting loop, with the largest gains on the hardest problems.
If a check is still failing after three rounds, Claude stops and brings in a human.
We maintain a reliability checklist with 39 items, each with a trigger that can be read from a diff, a check, and the incidents or PRs behind it.
Claude reads the diff and checks only the items whose trigger matches–usually 3 to 10–so nobody has to memorize past outages.
These must occur in at least two PRs and be identifiable from a diff to be considered a potential rule.
If at least two find the bug, it's a detectable bug.
denominator_notes: 「约 90%」没有口径（行、PR 还是 commit），而且这次说的是「写和审」都由 Claude 做，和此前「约 90% 由 Claude 写」（评审帖）不是同一个说法。「最多提升 10 个点」来自结构化文件生成的内部测试，不是 Claude Code 仓库本身的数据，没给基线和样本量。39 条清单、每次命中 3–10 条是规模描述，没有给出清单拦下了多少问题。「评审 reviewer」的三个指标（回滚、合并前被拒、干净对照组）只给了定义没给数值。
denominator_notes_en: "About 90%" has no stated basis (lines, PRs, or commits), and this time the claim is that Claude both writes and reviews it, which differs from the earlier "Claude writes about 90%" (review post). "Up to 10 points" comes from internal testing on structured file generation, not from the Claude Code repo itself, with no baseline or sample size. The 39-item checklist and 3 to 10 matches per diff describe scale only; nothing says how many issues the checklist caught. The three reviewer-quality metrics (reverts, pre-merge rejections, clean control set) are defined but no values are given.
transferable: 不依赖 lab 条件、可以直接拿走的几个动作：1）每个服务写一个 verify skill，把「怎么启动、怎么点一遍」写清楚，先把它调稳再扩大 agent 并行数；2）把评审规则文件放在 PR 改不到的地方（只读 base 分支），评审结果绑定 commit SHA；3）新的提交闸门先开 observe 模式记日志，看完误报再 enforce，并给 commit 留「为什么没验证」的说明口子；4）把历史事故整理成带 diff 触发条件的清单，让 agent 按 diff 只查命中项；5）漏判转规则要有门槛（至少两例、能从 diff 识别、人批准），并定期删规则。前提：E2E 环境能被 agent 自动拉起，测试不能 flaky，否则 agent 学会的是重跑。
transferable_en: Steps that don't need lab conditions: 1) write a verify skill per service that spells out how to boot and click through it, and make it reliable before raising agent parallelism; 2) keep review rule files where a PR can't touch them (read from the base branch only) and bind review results to a commit SHA; 3) launch any new commit gate in observe mode, review false positives, then enforce, and allow a commit message to explain why it wasn't verified; 4) turn past incidents into a checklist with diff-readable triggers so the agent checks only matching items; 5) put a bar on turning misses into rules (at least two cases, identifiable from a diff, human-approved) and prune rules regularly. Prerequisites: agents can spin up the E2E environment on their own, and tests aren't flaky, or the agent learns to rerun instead of fix.
caveats: 厂商自报，作者是 Anthropic 员工，帖子同时在推 Code Review、/verify、hook 等自家功能；只描述了 Claude Code 这一个团队，而这个团队做的就是 agent 工具本身，自带 dogfooding 和高熟练度；全文几乎没有效果数据（commit 闸门拦下多少、误报率多少、清单命中后发现了什么都没说）。
caveats_en: Vendor self-report by an Anthropic employee, and the post also promotes its own features (Code Review, /verify, hooks). It covers a single team, one that builds the agent tool itself and has built-in dogfooding and high fluency. There is almost no outcome data: nothing on how many commits the gate blocked, its false-positive rate, or what checklist matches actually found.
headline_en: The Claude Code team runs its verification layer as its own system: changes can't touch the rules that judge them, new gates go observe-then-enforce, and missed bugs become rules.

title: Using a "chaos loop" to harden the Claude Docs launch: 60 server errors across billions of requests
headline: 一个工程师让 Claude 在 staging 上连跑两周「压测→读遥测→修→再压」，上线前把要用的 pod 从 500+ 压到约 50；前提是提前写死不变量、列清哪些决策必须停下等人，并为了让 agent 看得懂遥测去选技术栈
what_they_do: Claude Docs 上线前三周还是单节点 PoC。上线前约两周，一名工程师在 Claude Code 里开一个长期运行的 coordinator 会话，驱动一个按生产镜像搭的 staging 集群（每天百万级合成文档），循环做「选故障场景→跑 harness→用 Datadog MCP 读遥测→给出选项和推荐→可撤回的改动直接部署到 staging→重跑」，大部分活派给 sub-agent，还通过 Slack MCP 问其他基础设施团队的 agent 有没有踩过同样的坑。开跑前先规定：改 schema、key 布局、文档存储方式这类难撤回的决策必须停下问人；另给两条硬不变量（文档几乎秒开、服务端确认过的编辑不能丢）。为了让 agent 拿到干净信号，每个数据库查询都上报名字和扫描/返回行数，Claude 边跑边补缺的遥测；服务用无 GC 的 Rust 写、依赖压到最少、必要的依赖 vendor 进来，理由是「Claude 测到的每个数字都要能追到我们自己写的代码」。上线时 Claude 预演过的修复都挂在运行时开关后面，出压力就翻开关。
what_they_do_en: Three weeks before launch, Claude Docs was a single-node proof of concept. About two weeks out, one engineer left a long-running coordinator session open in Claude Code that drove a production-mirroring staging cluster (over a million synthetic docs a day) through a loop: pick a failure scenario, run the harness, read telemetry through the Datadog MCP, propose options with a recommendation, deploy easily reversible changes straight to staging, rerun. Most of the work went to sub-agents, and the coordinator also asked other infrastructure teams' agents, via the Slack MCP, whether the scaling approach hit pitfalls they had already seen. Before starting, the engineer listed which decisions required a human (schema changes, key layout, how docs are stored and materialized) and set two hard invariants: docs open almost instantly, and an acknowledged edit is never lost. To give the agent a clean signal, every database query reports its name plus rows scanned versus returned, and Claude added missing telemetry as it went. The service was written in Rust (no garbage collector), with minimal dependencies and the essential ones vendored, so that "any number Claude measured traced back to code we wrote." Fixes rehearsed in staging shipped behind runtime flags, so launch-week pressure was handled by flipping a flag.
numbers: By September 22, people had created over 4.6 million docs.
Across 2 billion requests we saw only 60 server errors, and we never had to roll back.
In the busiest week, that usually meant about 11 sub-agents running at a time, and 30 at the peak.
After about three days of iterating, that doc topped out around 180 MB, and our estimate of what we’d need for launch dropped from more than 500 memory-optimized pods to about 50.
We rolled prod 629 times in September and never once rolled back.
Seven of the ten scenarios we’d rehearsed on staging actually happened in prod.
At Claude Fable 5.2's API list price (as of November 2026), I used roughly $125,000 of inference from the end of August to launch day.
A couple of years ago, work on this scale I'd guess would have taken a team of engineers about six months.
Knowing what I know now, I think we could have spent about half as much.

Scaling our spend down to that third and taking out the mistakes I made while I was still figuring out the setup, I’d put a two week push like this one at $3,000 to $10,000 at the same list price (I haven’t actually run this, so it’s only a rough sense).
denominator_notes: 「60 个服务端错误 / 20 亿请求」「零回滚」是上线第一周（9/16–9/22）的数字，没有说错误怎么定义、客户端错误和超时算不算。「500+ pod 降到约 50」是两次估算的对比，不是实测的生产节省。「约 12.5 万美元推理」按标价折算，内部实际成本未知，而且包含作者摸索流程时的浪费；「两年前要一个团队干六个月」是作者自己的猜测。小团队「3,000–10,000 美元」作者明说没跑过。「7/10 预演场景在生产出现」没有说明另外那些生产问题是不是预演之外的。同期 Docs 团队还落了上千个编辑器修复，上线结果不能全算到这个 loop 上。
denominator_notes_en: "60 server errors across 2 billion requests" and "no rollbacks" cover launch week (Sep 16 to Sep 22); the post doesn't define an error or say whether client errors and timeouts count. "More than 500 pods down to about 50" compares two estimates, not measured production savings. "Roughly $125,000 of inference" is priced at list rate, so real internal cost is unknown, and it includes waste from the author figuring out the process; "a team of engineers about six months" is the author's own guess. The $3,000 to $10,000 figure for a small team is explicitly untested. "Seven of ten rehearsed scenarios happened in prod" says nothing about production issues outside the rehearsed set. The Docs team landed thousands of editor fixes in the same window, so the launch outcome can't be credited to the loop alone.
transferable: 可以拿走的是这套 loop 的结构，不是 12.5 万美元的规模：1）一个工程师 + 一个 staging 环境 + 一个有 MCP 的可观测平台就能起步，先让 agent 写一个打 10 倍真实流量、故意杀实例/卡数据库/峰值中部署的压测脚本；2）开跑前把核心技术不变量写成文字交给 agent，再列一张「必须停下给我选项和推荐」的决策清单，标准是难不难撤回（schema、存储格式）；3）让遥测对 agent 可读：每个查询打名字、带扫描/返回行数，允许 agent 边跑边补埋点；4）修复挂在运行时开关后面上线。前提：staging 要真能镜像生产、agent 的改动只能落 staging；选「agent 好测量」的技术栈（少依赖、无 GC 噪声）是 Anthropic 的经验，没有和 Go 做对照，换栈前要自己评估。sub-agent 太烧 token 时，作者说单 agent 也能跑。
transferable_en: What transfers is the loop structure, not the $125,000 scale. 1) Start with one engineer, a staging environment, and an observability provider that has an MCP server; have the agent write a load script that pushes 10x real traffic and deliberately kills instances, stalls the database, and deploys mid-spike. 2) Before the run, write down the core technical invariants for the agent, plus a list of decisions where it must stop and offer options with a recommendation, drawn by how hard the change is to undo (schema, storage format). 3) Make telemetry legible to the agent: name every query, report rows scanned versus returned, and let the agent add instrumentation as it goes. 4) Ship fixes behind runtime flags. Prerequisites: staging has to genuinely mirror production, and the agent's changes must land only in staging. Choosing a stack the agent can measure (few dependencies, no GC noise) is Anthropic's experience without a bake-off against Go, so evaluate before switching languages. If sub-agents burn too many tokens, the author says a single agent also works.
caveats: 厂商自报：作者是 Anthropic 员工，用的是内部研究模型（作者说大致相当于 Claude Fable 5.2），帖子在推自家模型的长任务能力，并声称几个月前的模型会「目标漂移」做不到。单一服务、单一工程师的经验，Anthropic 有无限推理额度和成熟的平台/存储团队打底；Rust 的选择没有做对照实验；小团队成本是推算。
caveats_en: Vendor self-report: the author works at Anthropic and used an internal research model (described as roughly comparable to Claude Fable 5.2); the post promotes its own models' long-running ability and claims models from a few months earlier would have suffered goal drift. It reflects one service and one engineer, backed by effectively unlimited inference and mature platform and storage teams. The Rust choice was not tested against an alternative, and the small-team cost is an extrapolation.
headline_en: One engineer had Claude loop on staging for two weeks (load, read telemetry, fix, reload) and cut the launch estimate from 500+ pods to about 50; it worked because invariants were written down first, hard-to-undo decisions were reserved for a human, and the stack was chosen so the agent could read its telemetry.

title: Maintainers don’t need more AI bug reports. They need fixes.
headline: AI 找漏洞已经不是瓶颈，修才是：GitHub 和微软把几千条 AI 发现经 AI 分诊 + 人工逐条核验压成 99 份带补丁的报告，一半以上已修，但人工核验本身还没法规模化
what_they_do: GitHub Security Lab 和微软给六个开源项目（AutoGPT、Caddy、Express、FastMCP、ImageMagick、Netty）跑了一个试点，事先征得维护者同意。流程分四步：微软的多模型 agent 扫描 harness（Codename MDASH，跑在 MAI Cyber 模型上）扫代码并给出修复建议；GitHub Security Lab 用定制 Copilot skill 做的分诊 agent 去重、验真、只留高影响问题，维护者从不看原始扫描结果；微软 FORGE Lab 七名研究员人工核验每一条；最后经私有漏洞报告通道交给维护者，修不修、怎么修由维护者定。他们给出的规矩是：发给别人的每条 AI 发现都要先对照项目已知问题、威胁模型和安全策略核验，并附补丁。
what_they_do_en: GitHub Security Lab and Microsoft ran a pilot with six open source projects (AutoGPT, Caddy, Express, FastMCP, ImageMagick, Netty), with maintainers' consent up front. The pipeline has four steps: Microsoft's multi-model agentic scanning harness (Codename MDASH, on the MAI Cyber model) scans the code and suggests fixes; a GitHub Security Lab triage agent built on tailored Copilot skills dedupes, checks validity, and keeps only high-impact bugs, so maintainers never see raw scan output; seven Microsoft FORGE Lab researchers verify every remaining finding by hand; reports go to maintainers through private vulnerability reporting, and maintainers decide what to fix and how. The resulting standard: check every AI finding against what the project already knows, its threat model, and its security policy before sending it, and include a fix.
numbers: After AI triage and hand review by seven Microsoft FORGE Lab researchers, maintainers received 99 private reports.
As of November 15, they had fixed 55, and 14 of those fixes were already in a release.
Caddy’s maintainers fixed all 22 of the reports they received in a week or less.
Seven researchers spent about two days per project checking findings by hand.
Normally, a security advisory would take us around 30 minutes to 1 hour on average to read, understand, and make a fix.
denominator_notes: 「几千条」原始发现没有给具体数，所以不知道 AI 分诊和人工核验各砍掉了多少、误报率多少。99 份报告里 55 份已修是截至 11 月 15 日的快照，剩下 44 份是没修、修不了还是被判为非问题，没有拆开。七人 × 每项目约两天，六个项目合计约 84 人·天，这是这套流程的主要成本，文中没有和「不核验直接发」的维护者成本做对比。「30 分钟到 1 小时」是一位维护者的说法，不是测量值。
denominator_notes_en: The raw "thousands" of findings has no exact count, so we can't tell how much AI triage versus human review removed, or what the false-positive rate was. 55 fixed out of 99 is a snapshot as of November 15; the remaining 44 aren't broken down into unfixed, unfixable, or judged not-a-bug. Seven researchers at about two days per project across six projects is roughly 84 person-days, the main cost of the pipeline, and the post doesn't compare it with the maintainer cost of unverified reports. "30 minutes to 1 hour" is one maintainer's account, not a measurement.
transferable: 内部用 AI 做安全扫描或代码审计时同样适用：1）AI 发现不要直接派给代码 owner，中间放一层「AI 去重/验真 + 人工逐条核验」，owner 收到的是短清单 + 可评审的补丁，而不是扫描结果；2）把「先对照已知问题、威胁模型、安全策略核验」写成发报告方的义务；3）预算按人工核验算：这个试点大约每个项目 7 人 × 2 天，规模化前要先算清楚这部分人力，或者先在一两个服务上试；4）修复走 owner 已有的工作流（私有报告、私有 fork 上跑 CI）。前提：有懂安全的人能做核验，并且 owner 事先同意接收。
transferable_en: This applies equally to internal AI security scanning or code audits. 1) Don't route AI findings straight to code owners; put a layer of AI dedup and validity checks plus per-finding human verification in between, so owners get a short list with reviewable patches rather than scan output. 2) Make "verify against known issues, the threat model, and the security policy first" the sender's obligation. 3) Budget for human verification: this pilot used about seven people for two days per project, so size that headcount before scaling, or start with one or two services. 4) Deliver fixes through the owner's existing workflow (private reports, CI on private forks). Prerequisites: people with security expertise available to verify, and owners who agreed in advance to receive reports.
caveats: 厂商自报，GitHub 和微软同时在推 MAI Cyber 2、Copilot 自动修复和 Secure Open Source Fund；只有六个项目，而且都是该基金的校友项目，作者自己也说样本小、只能当早期经验；维护者评价是挑选过的引语；这是对外部开源项目的试点，不是两家公司内部代码库的数据。
caveats_en: Vendor self-report: GitHub and Microsoft are also promoting MAI Cyber 2, Copilot autofix, and the Secure Open Source Fund. Only six projects, all alumni of that fund, and the authors themselves call it a small sample and early lessons. Maintainer feedback consists of selected quotes. This was a pilot on external open source projects, not data from either company's internal codebase.
headline_en: Finding vulnerabilities with AI is no longer the bottleneck, fixing them is: GitHub and Microsoft cut thousands of AI findings to 99 patched reports via AI triage plus per-finding human review, over half are fixed, but the human review step doesn't scale yet.

title: When digital workers need a computer: How we’re using Windows 365 for Agents at Microsoft
headline: 微软业务运营把订单处理交给「数字员工」前先简化流程，再给 agent 独立身份、按功能最小授权、会自动退役的托管电脑；最难的问题不在 agent 本身，而在开通、计费和生命周期
what_they_do: 微软业务运营（报价到回款、合规、合作伙伴流程）和内部 IT（Microsoft Digital）一起，在一个运营单元试点「数字员工」：用内部的 BPO AI Toolkit 把操作知识转成流程指令、策略和可复用 agent 能力，编排 agent 按需调用 skill；遇到没有可靠 API、校验藏在 UI 里的老系统，就借一台托管 Cloud PC 像人一样操作。他们的做法是先用持续改进（他们叫「CI + AI」）简化流程和数据，再上 agent；agent 用专门的身份认证，按功能授权（能建订单不能取消或删除），网络只放行所需端点，而不是复制员工权限；执行中留证据，遇到例外带上下文升级给人。落地时最难的是给 agent 开通 Cloud PC、分配身份和许可证、计费，这些原本要租户管理员手动操作，于是和 FinOps 一起做用量上限和成本分摊，并要求提前定好 owner、监控和退役机制。
what_they_do_en: Microsoft Business Operations (quote-to-cash, compliance, partner processes) and internal IT (Microsoft Digital) are piloting "digital workers" in one operating unit. The internal BPO AI Toolkit turns operational knowledge into process instructions, policies, and reusable agent capabilities, and an orchestrating agent calls skills as needed; when a step depends on a legacy app with no reliable API or validations that live in the UI, the agent checks out a managed Cloud PC and works the interface the way a person would. The approach is to simplify the process and data first through continuous improvement (they call it "CI + AI") before adding agents. Agents authenticate with agent-specific identities, get function-scoped rights (create an order but not cancel or delete one), and have network access limited to the endpoints they need instead of a copied employee profile; they record evidence as they work and escalate exceptions to people with context. The hardest problems were provisioning Cloud PCs, assigning identities and licenses, and billing, which initially required manual tenant-admin steps, so they are working with FinOps on usage limits and cost allocation and require ownership, monitoring, and retirement to be defined up front.
numbers: The BPO AI Toolkit has reduced human touch by 75% and cut cycle time from 25 to 10.3 hours, while completing thousands of orders with no rework.
With Windows 365 for Agents, the team has a path to further reduce human touch by up to 95% and processing time to four hours.
denominator_notes: 「人工接触减少 75%」没有说怎么数接触（步骤、工时还是人次），也没说是哪个流程、多长时间、多少订单的基线；「25 小时降到 10.3 小时」的周期时间同样没有样本和时间段。「几千单零返工」没有给总单量和以前的返工率。「最多 95%、4 小时」是未来目标，不是结果。数字是 BPO Toolkit 的，Windows 365 for Agents 本身对这些数字的贡献没有单独给出。
denominator_notes_en: "Reduced human touch by 75%" doesn't say how touch is counted (steps, hours, or handoffs), nor which process, period, or order baseline it covers; the cycle time drop from 25 to 10.3 hours likewise has no sample or time window. "Thousands of orders with no rework" gives neither the total volume nor the previous rework rate. "Up to 95% and four hours" is a target, not a result. The figures belong to the BPO Toolkit; Windows 365 for Agents' own contribution isn't separated out.
transferable: 给非工程运营团队上 agent 时可以照抄的顺序：1）先挑重复量大、摩擦高的流程，把步骤、数据和策略理顺，坏流程不要直接自动化；2）执行方式从简到繁：有 API 或确定性自动化就用它，只有必须操作 UI 的步骤才给 agent 一台受管电脑；3）从第一天起给 agent 独立身份和按职能的最小权限模板（能创建不能删除），不要复制员工账号；4）规模化前把 owner、开通、监控、成本分摊、退役写成运营模型，并让 FinOps 参与；5）例外交给人时附上 agent 已做了什么、卡在哪、之后会发生什么。前提：IT 能为 agent 发身份和设备，有可观测的审计记录。
transferable_en: An order of operations to copy when bringing agents into non-engineering operations: 1) pick high-volume, high-friction processes and fix their steps, data, and policies first rather than automating a bad process; 2) use the simplest execution method that fits, APIs or deterministic automation where they exist, and give the agent a managed computer only for steps that require the UI; 3) from day one, give agents their own identities and function-based least-privilege templates (create but not delete) rather than copying an employee account; 4) before scaling, write down ownership, provisioning, monitoring, cost allocation, and retirement as an operating model, with FinOps involved; 5) when handing an exception to a person, include what the agent did, where it stopped, and what happens next. Prerequisites: IT can issue identities and devices to agents, and there is an observable audit trail.
caveats: 厂商自报的 Customer Zero 帖：微软在推 Windows 365 for Agents 和 Marketplace 上的工作台，文中多处是产品经理的引语；只有一个运营单元的试点，仍在分阶段推广；效果数字口径不清，而且混了未来目标。
caveats_en: Vendor self-reported Customer Zero post: Microsoft is promoting Windows 365 for Agents and a Marketplace workbench, and much of the text is product-manager quotes. It is a pilot in one operating unit that is still rolling out in phases. The outcome figures have unclear definitions and mix in future targets.
headline_en: Before handing order processing to digital workers, Microsoft Business Operations simplifies the process, then gives each agent its own identity, function-scoped least privilege, and a managed computer with a retirement plan; the hardest problems were provisioning, billing, and lifecycle, not the agent.

title: How Meta Uses AI Agents to Scale ML Innovations Across Ads Ranking Models
headline: Meta 把广告模型的「技术移植」拆成发现、泛化、落地三段，每段给 agent 配自己的度量：发现看召回率、落地看每个实验要人插手几次和 agent 自己修好了几成问题；而 agent 能接手的前提，是先花两年把模型做成标准模板
what_they_do: Meta 广告排序有大量结构各异的模型，一个模型上验证过的技术（新架构、训练优化等）要逐个改写才能用到别的模型上，过去全靠领域专家手工做。他们先用两年把模型拆成可复用的标准模板（SMT），确定性步骤自动化；剩下的判断（哪个技术值得移到哪个模型、超参搜多宽、失败原因）从 2026 年 3 月起交给共享知识库的 agent：跨全体模型排优先级、借鉴数百万次历史训练缩小搜索、管理数百个并发多日训练并回收低价值任务的 GPU。最高收入的模型仍由工程师主导，agent 跟着学每次调整，再推到剩下的模型。agent 移植的技术和人工移植的走同一套离线指标和线上 A/B 门槛，人审关键决定并批准上线。
numbers: Since agents began driving execution in March 2026, we estimate AI agents handle over 60% of all technique propagation.

Measured against the same work before agents, early results show 3x greater engineering productivity, a median 4x reduction in training compute across select combinations, and an estimated $45M+ in compute savings by the end of the year.

Over the last 2 years, through standardization and automation, we have shipped 5,000+ technique-model combinations across our large, diverse fleet of models while reducing per-model engineering time by 92%.

Now they can keep oversight at the decision points, approving plans and setting priorities at a 3x greater productivity (each engineer can now handle 3x more technique-model adaptations), compressing the time from a proven technique to a shipped model.
Today it can take over a year for every proven technique to reach every applicable model.
denominator_notes: 60% 是「estimate」，没说按技术-模型组合数还是工作量计。3 倍生产率定义为每个工程师能处理的适配数，是对比「agent 之前的同类工作」，没给基线人数和时间段，且是「early results」。4 倍训练算力下降是「select combinations」的中位数，挑选标准未说明。4,500 万美元是「estimated」的年底预期，不是已实现。92% 和 5,000+ 是两年标准化和自动化的成果，不是 agent 的贡献，别混在一起引用。
transferable: 两点可直接借：一是先标准化再上 agent——把系统收敛成少量模板，确定性部分写成自动化，agent 只接判断题，搜索空间才收得住；二是按阶段给 agent 定度量，不只看最终结果：候选筛选阶段看召回（漏掉的永远没第二次机会）、精度当护栏，执行阶段看「每个任务的人工干预次数」和「agent 自行诊断并修复的问题占比」。对高价值对象，先让工程师带着 agent 做几例、agent 记录每个决定，再让 agent 推广到其余对象。前提是有可复用的实验平台和统一的上线门槛（离线指标 + A/B）。
caveats: 单一团队自报，数字多为估计和早期结果；没有给出 agent 移植的失败率、被拒提案比例，也没公布干预次数和自修复占比的实际数值——只说了要量这些。Meta 广告有现成的大规模训练和实验设施、数百万次历史训练记录，一般组织不具备。
headline_en: Meta split ads-model "technique propagation" into discovery, generalization, and adoption, with agent metrics per stage (recall for discovery; human interventions per experiment and share of issues agents self-fix for adoption). Agents could take over only after two years spent standardizing models into templates.
what_they_do_en: Meta's ads ranking runs many models with different architectures. A technique proven on one model (new architecture, training optimization, etc.) has to be re-adapted for each other model, which used to be manual work by domain experts. Meta first spent two years refactoring models into reusable Standard Model Templates and automating the deterministic steps. Since March 2026, the remaining judgment calls (which technique goes to which model, how wide to search hyperparameters, why a run failed) go to agents with a shared knowledge base. The agents prioritize across the whole fleet, use millions of past training runs to narrow search, and manage hundreds of concurrent multi-day training jobs, reclaiming GPUs from low-value runs. For the highest-revenue models, engineers still lead; the agent records each of their adjustments, then extends them to the remaining models. Agent-propagated techniques pass the same offline metrics and online A/B bar as human ones, and humans review key decisions and approve what ships.
denominator_notes_en: The 60% is an "estimate" and doesn't say whether it counts technique-model combinations or effort. The 3x productivity is defined as adaptations per engineer versus "the same work before agents," with no baseline headcount or period, and is labeled "early results." The 4x training-compute reduction is a median over "select combinations" with unstated selection criteria. The $45M is an "estimated" year-end figure, not realized savings. The 92% and 5,000+ come from two years of standardization and automation, not from agents; don't cite them together.
transferable_en: Two things to borrow directly. First, standardize before adding agents: collapse the system into a small set of templates, automate the deterministic parts, and give agents only the judgment calls, so the search space stays bounded. Second, set agent metrics per stage, not just on the final result: for candidate selection, track recall (a missed candidate never gets a second chance) with precision as a guardrail; for execution, track human interventions per task and the share of issues the agent diagnoses and fixes on its own. For high-value targets, have engineers do a few cases with the agent recording every decision, then let the agent extend to the rest. Prerequisites: a reusable experiment platform and a single launch bar (offline metrics plus A/B).
caveats_en: Single-team self-report; most numbers are estimates or early results. No failure rate or rejected-proposal rate for agent propagation, and no actual values for intervention counts or self-fix share; the post only says these are measured. Meta ads has large-scale training and experiment infrastructure and millions of historical runs that most organizations lack.
